greek: Φησὶν οὖν· τὰ μὲν ὑπὸ τῆς Πυθίας ἢ Δωδωνίδων ἢ Κλαρίου ἢ ἐν Βραγχίδαις ἢ ἐν Ἄμμωνος ὑπὸ μυρίων τε ἄλλων θεοπρόπων προειρημένα, ὑφ᾿ ὧν ἐπιεικῶς πᾶσα γῆ κατῳκίσθη, ταῦτα μὲν (ἐν) οὐδενὶ λόγῳ τίθενται· τὰ δὲ ὑπο τῶν ἐν Ἰουδαίᾳ τῷ ἐκείνων τρόπῳ λεχθέντα ἢ μὴ λεχθέντα, καὶ ὥσπερ εἰώθασιν ἔτι νῦν οἱ περὶ Φοινίκην τε καὶ Παλαιστίνην, ταῦτά γε θαυμαστὰ καὶ ἀπαράλλακτα ἡγοῦνται. λέγωμεν οὖν περὶ τῶν κατειλεγμένων χρηστηρίων ὅτι δυνατὸν μὲν ἡμῖν συνάγουσιν ἀπὸ Ἀριστοτέλους καὶ τῶν τὰ τοῦ Περιπάτου φιλοσοφησάντων οὐκ ὀλίγα εἰπεῖν εἰς ἀνατροπὴν τοῦ περὶ τῆς Πυθίας καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν χρηστηρίων λόγου· δυνατὸν δὲ καὶ τὰ λελεγμένα τῷ Ἐπικούρῳ καὶ τοῖς ἀσπαζομένοις αὐτοῦ τὸν λόγον περὶ τῶν αὐτῶν παραθέμενον δεῖξαι ὅτι καὶ Ἑλλήνων τινὲς ἀνατρέπουσι τὰς νομιζομένας καὶ τεθαυμασμένας ἐν πάσῃ Ἑλλάδι θεοπροπίας. ἀλλὰ γὰρ δεδόσθω μὴ εἶναι πλάσματα μηδὲ προσποιήσεις ἀνθρώπων περὶ θεοφορίας τὰ περὶ τὴν Πυθίαν καὶ τὰ λοιπὰ χρηστήρια· ἴδωμεν οὖν εἰ μὴ καὶ οὕτως δύναται τοῖς φιλαλήθως ἐξετάζουσι τὰ πράγματα ἀποδείκνυσθαι ὅτι καὶ τῷ παραδεχομένῳ εἶναι ταῦτα τὰ μαντεῖα οὐκ ἀναγκαῖον προσέσθαι ὅτι θεοί τινες εἰσὶ παρ᾿ αὐτοῖς, ἀλλ᾿ ἐκ τοῦ ἐναντίου δαίμονές τινες φαῦλοι καὶ πνεύματα ἐχθρὰ τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ κωλύοντα τὴν τῆς ψυχῆς ἄνοδον καὶ δι᾿ ἀρετῆς πορείαν καὶ τῆς ἀληθινῆς εὐσεβείας ἀποκατάστασιν πρὸς τὸν θεόν. ἱστόρηται τοίνυν περὶ τῆς Πυθίας, ὅπερ δοκεῖ τῶν ἄλλων μαντείων λαμπρότερον τυγχάνειν. ὅτι περικαθεζομένη τὸ τῆς Κασταλίας στόμιον ἡ τοῦ Ἀπόλλωνος προφῆτις δέχεται πνεῦμα διὰ τῶν γυναικείων κόλπων· οὗ πληρωθεῖσα ἀποφθέγγεται τὰ νομιζόμενα εἶναι σεμνὰ καὶ θεῖα μαντεύματα. ὅρα δὴ διὰ τούτων εἰ μὴ τὸ τοῦ πνεύματος ἐκείνου ἀκάθαρτον καὶ βέβηλον ἐμφαίνεται, μὴ διὰ μανῶν καὶ ἀφανῶν πόρων καὶ πολλῷ γυναικείων κόλπων καθαρωτέρων ἐπεισιὸν τῇ ψυχῇ τῆς θεσπιζούσης ἀλλὰ διὰ τούτων, ἃ οὐδὲ θέμις ἦν τῷ σώφρονι καὶ ἀνθρώπῳ βλέπειν, οὔπω λέγεσθαι ἢ καὶ ἅπτεσθαι· καὶ τοῦτο ποιεῖν οὐχ ἅπαξ που οὐδὲ δὶς (ἴσως γὰρ ἔδοξεν ἀνεκτότερον τὸ τοιοῦτο τυγχάνειν), ἀλλὰ τοσαυτάκις, ὁσάκις προφητεύειν ἐκείνη ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἀπόλλωνος πεπίστευται. ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ εἰς ἔκστασιν καὶ μανικὴν ἄγειν κατάστασιν τὴν δῆθεν προφητεύουσαν, ὡς μηδαμῶς αυτὴν ἑαυτῇ παρακολουθεῖν, οὐ θείου πνεύματος ἔργον ἐστίν· ἐχρῆν γὰρ τὸν κάτοχον τῷ θείῳ πνεύματι πολλῷ πρότερον παντὸς οὑτινοσοῦν τοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν χρησμῶν διδασκομένου τὸ συμβαλλόμενον εἰς τὸν μέσον καὶ κατὰ φύσιν βίον ἢ πρὸς τὸ λυσιτελὲς ἢ πρὸς τὸ συμφέρον ὠφεληθῆναι καὶ διορατικώτερον παρ᾿ ἐκεῖνο μάλιστα καιροῦ τυγχάνειν, ὅτε σύνεστιν αὐτῷ τὸ θεῖον.

excerpts.author: Hippolytus
english: First fragment (Preface) As I wish to give an accurate account of the times of the captivity of the children of Israel in Babylon , and to discuss the prophecies contained in the visions of the blessed Daniel, (as well as) his manner of life from his boyhood in Babylon , I too shall proceed to bear my testimony to that holy and righteous man, a prophet and witness of Christ , who not only declared the visions of Nebuchadnezzar the king in those times, but also trained youths of like mind with himself, and raised up faithful witnesses in the world. He is horn, then, in the time of the prophetic ministry of the blessed Jeremiah, and in the reign of Jehoiakim or Eliakim. Along with the other captives, he is carried off a prisoner to Babylon . Now there are born to the blessed Josiah these five sons — Jehoahaz, Eliakim, Johanan, Zedekiah, or Jeconiah, and Sadum. And on his father's death, Jehoahaz is anointed as king by the people at the age of twenty-three years. Against him comes up Pharaoh -Necho, in the third month of his reign; and he takes him (Jehoahaz) prisoner, and carries him into Egypt , and imposes tribute on the land to the extent of one hundred talents of silver and ten talents of gold. And in his stead he sets up his brother Eliakim as king over the land, whose name also he changed to Jehoiakim, and who was then eleven years old. Against him came up Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon , and carries him off prisoner to Babylon , taking with him also some of the vessels…

1. In speaking of a lioness from the sea, he meant the rising of the kingdom of Babylon , and that this was the golden head of the image. And in speaking of its eagle wings, be meant that king Nebuchadnezzar was exalted and that his glory was lifted up against God. Then he says its wings were plucked off, i.e., that his glory was destroyed; for he was driven out of his kingdom. And the words, A man's heart was given it, and it was made stand upon the feet of a man , mean that he came to himself again, and recognised that he was but a man , and gave the glory to God . Then after the lioness he sees a second beast, like a bear, which signified the Persians. For after the Babylonians the Persians obtained the power. And in saying that it had three ribs in its mouth, he pointed to the three nations, Persians , Medes, and Babylonians , which were expressed in the image by the silver after the gold. Then comes the third beast, a leopard, which means the Greeks; for after the Persians , Alexander of Macedon had the power, when Darius was overthrown, which was also indicated by the brass in the image. And in saying that the beast had four wings of a fowl, and four heads, he showed most clearly how the kingdom of Alexander was parted into four divisions. For in speaking of four heads, he meant the four kings that arose out of it. For Alexander, when dying, divided his kingdom into four parts. Then he says, The fourth beast (was) dreadful and terrible: it had iron teeth, and claws of…

2. After this, then, what remains, beloved, but the toes of the feet of the image, in which part shall be of iron and part of clay mixed together? By the toes of the feet he meant, mystically , the ten kings that rise out of that kingdom. As Daniel says, I considered the beast; and, lo, (there were) ten horns behind, among which shall come up another little horn springing from them; by which none other is meant than the antichrist that is to rise; and he shall set up the kingdom of Judah. And in saying that three horns were plucked up by the roots by this one, he indicates the three kings of Egypt , Libya, and Ethiopia , whom this one will slay in the array of war . And when he has conquered all, he will prove himself a terrible and savage tyrant, and will cause tribulation and persecution to the saints , exalting himself against them. And after him, it remains that the stone shall come from heaven which smote the image and shivered it, and subverted all the kingdoms, and gave the kingdom to the saints of the Most High. This became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.

3. As these things, then, are destined to come to pass, and as the toes of the image turn out to be democracies, and the ten horns of the beast are distributed among ten kings, let us look at what is before us more carefully, and scan it, as it were, with open eye. The golden head of the image is identical with the lioness, by which the Babylonians were represented. The golden shoulders and the arms of silver are the same with the bear, by which the Persians and Medes are meant. The belly and thighs of brass are the leopard, by which the Greeks who ruled from Alexander onwards are intended. The legs of iron are the dreadful and terrible beast, by which the Romans who hold the empire now are meant. The toes of clay and iron are the ten horns which are to be. The one other little horn springing up in their midst is the antichrist. The stone that smites the image and breaks it in pieces, and that filled the whole earth, is Christ, who comes from heaven and brings judgment on the world.

excerpts.author: Cyprian
english: When the Lord warns us, saying, "You are the salt of the earth" (Matt 5:13), and commands us to be simple in innocence yet prudent with simplicity, what else should we do, dearest brothers, but take thought for ourselves? With watchful, anxious hearts we must understand and guard against the cunning enemy’s plots, lest we who have put on Christ, the wisdom of God the Father, appear less wise in protecting our salvation. Persecution is not the only danger, nor only those open attacks that overthrow God’s servants. Caution comes easily when the threat is obvious, and the mind braces for battle when the adversary shows himself. The enemy is far more to be feared and avoided when he creeps in secretly, slipping in under the guise of peace with hidden approaches — which is why he bears the name of the serpent. This is his constant cunning: the blind, hidden deceit of circumventing humanity. From the world’s beginning he deceived, flattering with lying words and catching simple souls off guard through their unguarded credulity. He even tried to tempt the Lord Himself, approaching secretly as if to creep in again and deceive. But he was recognized and repulsed, and so he was thrown down because he was detected. From this we have been given an example: we must flee the way of the old man and follow in the footsteps of the living Christ, lest, being unguarded, we fall once more into the snare of death; instead, foreseeing the danger, we may lay hold of immortality. And how can we possess immortality unless we keep the commandments of Christ by which death is overcome and conquered, He Himself warning and saying, "If you wish to enter life, keep the commandments" (Matt 19:17), and again, "If you do what I command you, I no longer call you servants, but friends" (John 15:14)? These He calls strong and stable, founded on a massive rock, solidified with immovable and unshakable firmness against all the tempests and whirlwinds of the world. "Everyone who hears these words of mine and does them," He says, "I will liken to a wise man who built his house on the rock. The rain fell, the floods came, the winds blew and beat against that house, and it did not fall, because it had been founded on the rock" (Matt 7:24–25). Therefore we must stand firm on His words, and learn to do everything He taught and commanded. But how can someone claim to believe in Christ if he does not do what Christ commanded? Where will he reach the reward of faith if he refuses to keep the faith of the commandment? He must waver and wander, carried off by the spirit of error and tossed like dust the wind whirls about; he will not advance toward salvation who does not hold to the truth of the saving way. Yet, dearest brothers, we must beware not only of open and manifest dangers, but also of those that deceive with the subtlety of cunning fraud. What could be more cunning or subtle than this: after the enemy was detected and thrown down by Christ’s advent, after the light came to the Gentiles and the saving light shone for human salvation — so that the deaf received the hearing of spiritual grace, the blind opened their eyes to God, the weak were strengthened by eternal health, the lame ran to the Church, the mute prayed with clear voices, and seeing idols abandoned and his own seats and temples deserted by the multitude of believers — he devised a new deceit to mislead the unguarded under the very title of the Christian name? He invented heresies and schisms to subvert the faith, corrupt the truth, and divide the unity. Those he cannot hold in the blindness of the old way, he encircles and deceives with the error of a new way. He snatches men from the very Church; and while they think they have approached the light and escaped the world’s night, he pours darkness into them again, unknown to them, so that, not standing with the Gospel of Christ and its observance and law, they call themselves Christians, and walking in darkness they imagine they have the light. The adversary flatters and deceives, transforming himself into an angel of light (2 Cor 11:14) and disguising his ministers as ministers of righteousness, calling night day, destruction salvation, despair hope, perfidy faith, antichrist Christ — so that, while they speak what sounds plausible, they frustrate the truth with subtlety. This happens, dearest brothers, when we do not return to the origin of truth, nor seek the Head, nor preserve the doctrine of the heavenly Master.

latin: CUM moneat Dominus et dicat: Vos estis sal terrae, cumque esse nos jubeat ad innocentiam simplices, et tamen cum simplicitate prudentes, quid aliud, fratres dilectissimi, quam providere nos convenit, et sollicito corde vigilantes, subdoli hostis insidias intelligere pariter et cavere ne qui Christum sapientiam Dei Patris induimus, minus sapere in tuenda salute videamur? Neque enim persecutio sola metuenda est et ea quae subruendis ac dejiciendis Dei servis aperta impugnatione grassantur. Facilior cautio est ubi manifesta formido est, et ad certamen animus ante praestruitur quando se adversarius confitetur. Plus metuendus est et cavendus inimicus cum latenter obrepit, cum, per pacis imaginem fallens, occultis accessibus serpit; unde et nomen serpentis accepit. Ea est ejus semper astutia, ea est circumveniendi hominis caeca et latebrosa fallacia. Sic ab initio statim mundi fefellit, et, verbis mendacibus blandiens, rudes animas incauta credulitate decepit. Dominum ipsum tentare conatus, quasi obreperet rursus et falleret, latenter accessit. Intellectus tamen est et retusus; et ideo prostratus, quia agnitus atque detectus. Unde nobis exemplum datum est veteris hominis viam fugere, vestigiis Christi viventis insistere; ne denuo incauti in mortis laqueum revolvamur, sed, ad periculum providi, accepta immortalitate potiamur. Immortalitate autem potiri quomodo possumus, nisi ea quibus mors expugnatur et vincitur, Christi mandata servemus, ipso monente et dicente: Si vis ad vitam venire, serva mandata. Et iterum: Si feceritis quae mando vobis, jam non dico vos servos, sed amicos. Hos denique fortes dicit et stabiles, hos super petram robusta mole fundatos, hos contra omnes tempestates et turbines saeculi immobili et inconcussa firmitate solidatos. Qui audit, inquit, verba mea et facit ea, similabo eum viro sapienti qui aedificavit domum suam supra petram. Descendit pluvia, venerunt flumina, flaverunt venti et impegerunt in domum illam, et non cecidit; fundata enim fuit super petram. Verbis igitur ejus insistere, quaecumque et docuit et fecit discere et facere debemus. Caeterum credere se in Christum, quomodo dicit qui non facit quod Christus facere praecepit? Aut unde perveniet ad praemium fidei, qui fidem non vult servare mandati? Nutet necesse est et vagetur, et, spiritu erroris abreptus, velut pulvis quem ventus excutit ventiletur; nec ambulando proficiet ad salutem, qui salutaris viae non tenet veritatem. Cavenda sunt autem, fratres dilectissimi, non solum quae sunt aperta atque manifesta, sed et astutae fraudis subtilitate fallentia. Quid vero astutius, quidve subtilius, quam ut Christi adventu detectus ac prostratus inimicus, postquam lux Gentibus venit et sospitandis hominibus salutare lumen effulsit, ut surdi auditum gratiae spiritalis admitterent, aperirent ad Deum oculos suos caeci, infirmi aeterna sanitate revalescerent, claudi ad Ecclesiam currerent, muti claris vocibus et precibus orarent, videns ille idola derelicta et per nimium credentium populum sedes suas ac templa deserta, excogitaverit novam fraudem, ut sub ipso christiani nominis titulo fallat incautos? Haereses invenit et schismata, quibus subverteret fidem, veritatem corrumperet, scinderet unitatem. Quos detinere non potest in viae veteris caecitate, circumscribit et decipit novi itineris errore. Rapit de ipsa Ecclesia homines; et, dum sibi appropinquasse jam lumini atque evasisse saeculi noctem videntur, alias nescientibus tenebras rursus infundit, ut cum Evangelio Christi et cum observatione ejus et lege non stantes, Christianos se vocent, et ambulantes in tenebris habere se lumen existiment, blandiente adversario atque fallente, qui, secundum Apostoli vocem, transfigurat se velut angelum lucis, et ministros suos subornat velut ministros justitiae, asserentes noctem pro die, interitum pro salute, desperationem sub obtentu spei, perfidiam sub praetextu fidei, antichristum sub vocabulo Christi; ut, dum verisimilia mentiuntur, veritatem subtilitate frustrentur. Hoc eo fit, fratres dilectissimi, dum ad veritatis originem non reditur, nec caput quaeritur, nec magistri coelestis doctrina servatur.

excerpts.author: Cyprian
english: Peace has been restored to the Church, my dearly beloved brothers, and what recently seemed impossible to unbelievers and the faithless has come to pass: divine help and vengeance have repaired our security. Our minds return to joy, and now that the storm of oppression has broken and the cloud has dispersed, tranquility and serenity shine forth again. We must give praise to God and celebrate his benefits and gifts with thanksgiving, even though our voice never ceased giving thanks even during the persecution. For the enemy cannot be allowed so much power that we who love the Lord with our whole heart and soul and strength do not always and everywhere proclaim his blessings and praises with glory. The day that everyone longed for has arrived, and after the horrible, dark gloom of the long night, the world has shone out radiant with the Lord's light. We look upon the confessors with joy, those renowned for their good name and glorious for the praises of virtue and faith; we cling to them with holy kisses and embrace those we have long desired with an insatiable longing. The white cohort of Christ's soldiers stands here, those who broke the fierce and turbulent fury of the persecution by standing their ground, prepared for the patience of prison and armed for the endurance of death. You resisted the world bravely, you offered a glorious spectacle to God, and you became an example for the brothers who follow. A religious voice spoke Christ, confessing that it had once believed in him. Illustrious hands, accustomed only to divine works, resisted sacrilegious sacrifices. Mouths sanctified by heavenly food, after receiving the body and blood of the Lord, rejected profane contagions and the remnants of idols. Your heads remained free from the impious and wicked veil that covered the captive heads of those who sacrificed. Your foreheads, pure with the sign of God, could not bear the devil's crown; they reserved themselves for the crown of the Lord. How gladly mother Church receives you as you return from battle! How blessed and rejoicing she opens her gates so that you may enter with assembled ranks, carrying trophies from the prostrate enemy! Triumphant men and women come forward, those who, fighting against the world, also conquered their sex. Virgins come too, bearing the double glory of their warfare, and boys who surpass their years with virtues. And the rest of the great multitude of those who stood firm follows your glory, tracking your footsteps with insignia of praise closely joined. The same sincerity of heart is in them, the same integrity of tenacious faith. Fixed on the unshaken roots of heavenly precepts and strengthened by evangelical traditions, they were not terrified by prescribed exiles, destined torments, loss of property, or bodily punishments. Days were being appointed for the testing of faith. But whoever remembers that he has renounced the world knows no day of the world; nor does he calculate earthly times, who hopes for eternity from God. No one, my dearly beloved brothers, no one should mutilate this glory; no one should weaken the incorrupt firmness of those who stood with malicious detraction. When the day appointed for those who deny has passed, whoever has not professed within that day has confessed himself to be a Christian. The first title of victory is to confess the Lord when seized by the hands of the Gentiles; the second step toward glory is to be reserved for the Lord by a cautious withdrawal. The former is a public confession, the latter a private one. The former overcomes the judge of the world; the latter, content with God as his judge, keeps a pure conscience with integrity of heart. There, fortitude is more prompt; here, solicitude is more secure. The one, with his hour approaching, was already found mature; the other, perhaps delayed, who abandoned his patrimony and withdrew for that very reason because he would not deny — he certainly would have confessed if he too had been detained.

latin: PAX ecce, dilectissimi fratres, Ecclesiae reddita est et, quod difficile nuper incredulis ac perfidis impossibile videbatur, ope atque ultione divina securitas nostra reparata est. In laetitiam mentes redeunt, et, tempestate pressurae ac nube discussa, tranquillitas ac serenitas refulserunt. Dandae laudes Deo, et beneficia ejus ac munera cum gratiarum actione celebranda, quamvis agere gratias nostra vox nec in persecutione cessaverit. Neque enim tantum inimico licere potest ut non, qui Dominum toto corde et anima et virtute diligimus, benedictiones ejus et laudes semper et ubique cum gloria praedicemus. Exoptatus votis omnium dies venit, et, post longae noctis horribilem tetramque caliginem, Domini luce radiatus mundus eluxit. Confessores, praeconio boni nominis claros et virtutis ac fidei laudibus gloriosos, laetis conspectibus intuemur, sanctis osculis adhaerentes, desideratos diu inexplebili cupiditate complectimur. Adest militum Christi cohors candida, qui persecutionis urgentus ferociam turbulentam stabili congressione fregerunt, parati ad patientiam carceris, armati ad tolerantiam mortis. Repugnastis fortiter saeculo, spectaculum gloriosum praebuistis Deo, secuturis fratribus fuistis exemplo. Religiosa vox Christum locuta est, in quem se semel credidisse confessa est. Illustres manus, quae non nisi divinis operibus assueverant, sacrificiis sacrilegis restiterunt. Sanctificata ora coelestibus cibis, post corpus et sanguinem Domini, profana contagia et idolorum reliquias respuerunt. Ab impio sceleratoque velamine, quo illic velabantur sacrificantium capita captiva, caput vestrum liberum mansit. Frons cum signo Dei pura, diaboli coronam ferre non potuit, coronae se Domini reservavit. Quam vos laete sinu suo excipit mater Ecclesia de praelio revertentes! quam beata, quam gaudens portas suas aperit, ut adunatis agminibus intretis, de hoste prostrato trophaea referentes! Cum triumphantibus viris et feminae veniunt, quae cum saeculo dimicantes, sexum quoque vicerunt. Veniunt et geminata militiae suae gloria virgines, et pueri annos suos virtutibus transeuntes. Necnon et caetera stantium multitudo vestram gloriam sequitur, proximis et pene conjunctis laudis insignibus vestigia vestra comitatur. Eadem et in illis sinceritas cordis, eadem fidei tenacis integritas. Inconcussis praeceptorum coelestium radicibus nixos et evangelicis traditionibus roboratos, non praescripta exilia, non destinata tormenta, non rei familiaris damna, non corporis supplicia terruerunt. Explorandae fidei praefiniebantur dies. Sed qui saeculo renuntiasse se meminit, nullum saeculi diem novit; nec tempora terrena jam computat qui aeternitatem de Deo sperat. Nemo, fratres dilectissimi, nemo hanc gloriam mutilet, nemo incorruptam stantium firmitatem maligna obtrectatione debilitet. Cum dies negantibus praestitutus excessit, quisquis professus intra diem non est, Christianum se esse confessus est. Primus est victoriae titulus, gentilium manibus apprehensum Dominum confiteri: secundus ad gloriam gradus est cauta secessione subtractum Domino reservari. Illa publica, haec privata confessio est. Ille judicem saeculi vincit, hic contentus Deo suo judice conscientiam puram cordis integritate custodit. Illic, fortitudo promptior, hic sollicitudo securior. Ille appropinquante hora sua, jam maturus inventus est; hic fortasse dilatus est qui, patrimonio derelicto, idcirco secessit quia non erat negaturus: confiteretur utique si fuisset et ipse detentus.

excerpts.author: Cyprian
english: My dear brothers, the Gospel's teachings are nothing less than divine instructions: they lay the foundations of hope, strengthen the pillars of faith, nourish the heart, steer our journey, and defend our salvation. While they instruct receptive minds here on earth, they lead us into the heavenly kingdom. God chose to speak and be heard many times through his servants the prophets, yet the words of the Son are far greater. The Word of God, who once spoke through the prophets, now testifies with his own voice. He no longer merely commands that a way be prepared for his coming; he comes himself, opening the way and showing it to us. We once wandered blindly in the darkness of death, but enlightened by the light of grace, we now walk the path of life with the Lord as our guide and ruler.

Among his many salutary warnings and divine precepts given for our salvation, he also gave us the very form of prayer, teaching us what to ask for. The One who gave us life taught us to pray, out of the same kindness by which he deigned to grant all other gifts. He did this so that when we speak to the Father using the prayer and petition the Son taught, we may be heard more readily. He had already foretold the hour when true worshipers would worship the Father in spirit and truth (John 4:23), and he fulfilled that promise. We have received the Spirit and truth from his sanctification; therefore we must also worship truly and spiritually, following his tradition. What prayer could be more spiritual than the one Christ gave us, since he is the one who sent us the Holy Spirit? What prayer could be truer before the Father than the one spoken by the Son, who is Truth itself? To pray in any other way than he taught is not just ignorance; it is a fault. He himself said: "You reject the commandment of God, that you may establish your tradition."

Therefore, dear brothers, let us pray as God our teacher has taught. It is a friendly, intimate prayer to ask God for what is his own, letting Christ's prayer rise to the Father's ears. When we pray, let the Father recognize the words of his Son. The One who dwells within our hearts should also be in our voices. Since we have him as our advocate with the Father for our sins, when we sinners plead for pardon, let us speak the words of our advocate. He declared that whatever we ask the Father in his name, he will give us (John 14:13-14). How much more effectively, then, do we obtain what we seek in Christ's name if we ask using his own prayer?

latin: EVANGELICA praecepta, fratres dilectissimi, nihil aliud sunt quam magisteria divina, fundamenta aedificandae spei, firmamenta corroborandae fidei, nutrimenta fovendi cordis, gubernacula dirigendi itineris, praesidia obtinendae salutis; quae, dum dociles credentium mentes in terris instruunt, ad coelestia regna perducunt. Multa et per Prophetas servos suos dici Deus voluit et audiri; sed quanto majora quae Filius loquitur, quae Dei sermo qui in Prophetis fuit propria voce testatur, non jam mandans ut paretur venienti via, sed ipse veniens, et viam nobis aperiens et ostendens; ut qui, in tenebris mortis errantes, improvidi et caeci prius fuimus, luce gratiae luminati, iter vitae duce et rectore Domino teneremus. Qui inter caetera salutaria sua monita et praecepta divina quibus populo suo consulit ad salutem, etiam orandi ipse formam dedit, ipse quid precaremur monuit et instruxit. Qui fecit vivere, docuit et orare, benignitate ea scilicet qua et caetera dare et conferre dignatus est; ut, dum prece et oratione quam Filius docuit apud Patrem loquimur, facilius audiamur. Jam praedixerat horam venire quando veri adoratores adorarent Patrem in spiritu et veritate, et implevit quod ante promisit; ut qui spiritum et veritatem de ejus sanctificatione percepimus, de traditione quoque ejus vere et spiritaliter adoremus. Quae enim potest esse magis spiritalis oratio quam quae a Christo nobis data est, a quo nobis et Spiritus sanctus missus est? Quae vera magis apud Patrem precatio quam quae a Filio, qui est Veritas, de ejus ore prolata est? ut aliter orare quam docuit non ignorantia sola sit, sed et culpa, quando ipse posuerit et dixerit: Rejicitis mandatum Dei, ut traditionem vestram statuatis. Oremus itaque, fratres dilectissimi, sicut magister Deus docuit. Amica et familiaris oratio est Deum de suo rogare, ad aures ejus ascendere Christi oratione. Agnoscat Pater Filii sui verba cum precem facimus. Qui habitat intus in pectore, ipse sit et in voce. Et cum ipsum habeamus apud Patrem advocatum pro peccatis nostris, quando peccatores pro delictis nostris petimus, advocati nostri verba promamus. Nam, cum dicat quia quodcumque petierimus a Patre in nomine ejus dabit nobis,, quanto efficacius impetramus quod petimus in Christi nomine, si petamus ipsius oratione?

excerpts.author: Cyprian
english: Countless and tremendous are the divine benefits through which the rich and abundant clemency of God the Father and Christ has worked and continues to work for our salvation. The Father sent the Son to preserve and give us life so that He might restore us, and the Son willed to be sent and to become the Son of Man so that He might make us sons of God. He humbled Himself to raise up the people who lay prostrate; He was wounded to heal our wounds; He became a servant to lead servants into freedom; He endured death to offer immortality to mortals. These are many and great gifts of divine mercy. But consider further: what kind of providence, how great a clemency, plans for us with a saving purpose so that the redeemed person might be more fully provided for? When the Lord came, He healed the wounds Adam bore and cured the ancient venom of the serpent. He gave a law to the healed and commanded them not to sin again, lest something worse befall the sinner. We were confined, shut in by a narrow prescription of innocence. Human frailty and weakness would have had no recourse unless divine pity came to our aid once more, displaying works of justice and mercy and opening a way to safeguard salvation, so that we might wash away whatever filth we contract afterwards through alms. The Holy Spirit speaks in the divine Scriptures and says: "Sins are purified by alms and faith" — not the sins contracted before, for those are purified by the blood and sanctification of Christ. He says again: "Just as water extinguishes fire, so alms extinguishes sin." Here it is shown and proven that, just as the fire of Gehenna is quenched by the bath of saving water, so the flame of sins is calmed by alms and just works. Because the remission of sins is given once in Baptism, a constant and daily practice that imitates Baptism again obtains God's indulgence. The Lord teaches this also in the Gospel. When His disciples were rebuked for eating without washing their hands, He answered: "The One who made the inside also made the outside. But give alms, and behold, everything is clean for you" (Luke 11:41). He was teaching and showing that it is not the hands that need washing, but the heart, and that the filth inside rather than outside must be removed; the one who purifies the inside also purifies the outside, and with a cleansed mind he begins to be clean in skin and body as well. Furthermore, warning us and showing from what source we can be clean and purified, He added that alms must be given. The Merciful One teaches and urges us to practice mercy; because He seeks to save those He redeemed at a great price, He teaches that those stained after the grace of Baptism can be purified again. Let us therefore recognize, dear brothers, the wholesome gift of divine indulgence, and let us cure our wounds with spiritual remedies so that we may be cleansed and purified from our sins, since we cannot exist without some wound of conscience. No one should flatter himself about having a pure and spotless heart, trusting his own innocence to think medicine need not be applied to wounds, since it is written: "Who can boast of having a chaste heart, or who can boast of being free from sins?" And again John says in his Epistle: "If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us." If no one can be without sin, and whoever claims to be blameless is either proud or foolish, how necessary and kind is divine clemency, which knows that the healed do not lack subsequent wounds and has given remedies to heal and save those wounds again! Finally, dear brothers, the divine admonition has never ceased or fallen silent, so that in the holy Scriptures, both old and new, the people of God might always and everywhere be urged to works of mercy; and with the Holy Spirit singing and exhorting, whoever is instructed in the hope of the heavenly kingdom is commanded to give alms. God commands and orders Isaiah: "Cry out with strength, do not hold back; lift up your voice like a trumpet, and declare to my people their sins and to the house of Jacob their wicked deeds" (Isaiah 58:1). When He had commanded that their sins be rebuked and their wicked deeds laid bare with full indignation, and had said they could not satisfy for their sins even with prayers, supplications, and fasts, nor placate God's wrath even by wearing sackcloth and ashes, yet in the final passage He showed that God can be appeased only by alms, adding: "Break your bread for the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house; if you see the naked, clothe him, and do not hide from your own flesh" (Isaiah 58:7). Then your light will break forth like the dawn, your healing will spring up quickly, your righteousness will go before you, and the glory of the Lord will be your rear guard. Then you will call, and the Lord will answer; you will cry for help, and He will say: Here I am (Isaiah 58:8-9).

latin: MULTA et magna sunt, fratres charissimi beneficia divina quibus in salutem nostram Dei Patris et Christi larga et copiosa clementia et operata sit et semper operetur, quod conservandis ac vivificandis nobis Pater Filium misit, ut reparare nos posset, quodque Filius missus esse et hominis filius fieri voluit ut nos Dei filios faceret. Humiliavit se, ut populum qui prius jacebat erigeret: vulneratus est, ut vulnera nostra curaret: servivit, ut ad libertatem servientes extraheret: mori sustinuit, ut immortalitatem mortalibus exhiberet. Multa haec sunt et magna divinae misericordiae munera. Sed adhuc, qualis providentia illa et quanta clementia est quod nobis salutari ratione prospicitur, ut homini qui redemptus est reservando plenius consulatur! Nam, cum Dominus adveniens sanasset illa quae Adam portaverat vulnera, et venena serpentis antiqua curasset, legem dedit sano, et praecepit ne ultra jam peccaret, ne quid peccanti gravius eveniret. Coarctati eramus et in angustum innocentiae praescriptione conclusi. Nec haberet quid fragilitatis humanae infirmitas atque imbecillitas faceret, nisi iterum pietas divina subveniens, justitiae et misericordiae operibus ostensis, viam quamdam tuendae salutis aperiret, ut sordes postmodum, quascumque contrahimus, eleemosynis abluamus. Loquitur in Scripturis divinis Spiritus sanctus et dicit: Eleemosynis et fide delicta purgantur. Non utique illa delicta quae fuerant ante contracta, nam illa Christi sanguine et sanctificatione purgantur. Item denuo dicit: Sicut aqua extinguit ignem, sic eleemosyna extinguit peccatum. Hic quoque ostenditur et probatur quia, sicut lavacro aquae salutaris gehennae ignis extinguitur, ita et eleemosynis atque operationibus justis delictorum flamma sopitur. Et quia semel in Baptismo remissa peccatorum datur, assidua et jugis operatio Baptismi instar imitata, Dei rursus indulgentiam largitur. Hoc et in Evangelio Dominus docet. Nam cum denotarentur discipuli ejus quod ederent, nec prius manus abluissent, respondit et dixit: Qui fecit quod intus est, fecit et quod foris est. Verum date eleemosynam, et ecce vobis munda omnia: docens scilicet et ostendens non manus lavandas esse, sed pectus, et sordes intrinsecus potius quam extrinsecus detrahendas; verum qui purgaverit quod est intus, eum quoque id quod foris est repurgasse, et emundata mente, cute quoque et corpore mundum esse coepisse. Porro autem, monens et ostendens unde mundi et purgati esse possimus, addidit eleemosynas esse faciendas. Misericors docet et monet misericordiam fieri; et quia servare quaerit quos magno pretio redemit, post Baptismi gratiam sordidatos docet denuo posse purgari. Agnoscamus itaque, fratres charissimi, divinae indulgentiae munus salubre, et emundandis purgandisque peccatis nostris, qui sine aliquo conscientiae vulnere esse non possumus, medelis spiritalibus vulnera nostra curemus. Nec quisquam sic sibi de puro atque immaculato pectore blandiatur, ut, innocentia sua fretus, medicinam non putet adhibendam esse vulneribus, cum scriptum sit: Quis gloriabitur castum se habere cor, aut quis gloriabitur mundum se esse a peccatis? et iterum in Epistola sua Joannes ponat et dicat: Si dixerimus quia peccatum non habemus, nos ipsos decipimus, et veritas in nobis non est. Si autem nemo esse sine peccato potest, et quisquis inculpatum se esse dixerit, aut superbus aut stultus est, quam necessaria, quam benigna est divina clementia, quae, cum sciat non deesse sanatis quaedam postmodum vulnera, dedit curandis denuo sanandisque vulneribus remedia salutaria! Numquam denique, fratres dilectissimi, admonitio divina cessavit et tacuit quominus in Scripturis sanctis tam veteribus quam novis semper et ubique ad misericordiae opera Dei populus provocaretur; et canente atque exhortante Spiritu sancto, quisquis ad spem regni coelestis instruitur, facere eleemosynas jubetur. Mandat et praecipit Esaiae Deus: Exclama, inquit, in fortitudine, et noli parcere. Sicut tuba exalta vocem tuam, et annuntia plebi meae peccata ipsorum et domui Jacob facinora eorum. Et cum peccata eis sua exprobrari praecepisset, cumque eorum facinora pleno indignationis impetu protulisset, dixissetque eos nec, si orationibus et precibus et jejuniis uterentur, satisfacere pro delictis posse, nec, si in cilicio et cinere volverentur, iram Dei posse lenire, in novissima tamen parte, demonstrans solis eleemosynis Deum posse placari, addidit dicens: Frange esurienti panem tuum, et egenos sine tecto induc in domum tuam. Si videris nudum, vesti eum, et domesticos seminis tui non despicias. Tunc erumpet temporaneum lumen tuum, et vestimenta tua cito orientur, et praeibit ante te justitia, et claritas Dei circumdabit te. Tunc exclamabis, et Deus exaudiet te. Dum adhuc loqueris dicet: Ecce adsum.

excerpts.author: Novatian
english: Both the logic of reason and the authority of faith — grounded in the Lord's own words and writings — urge us to believe in the Holy Spirit after all that has gone before. This Spirit was promised to the church long ago, but was given at the appointed seasons. He was promised through the prophet Joel (Joel 2:29), yet bestowed through Christ. "In the last days, I will pour out my Spirit on my servants and handmaids." The Lord Himself said, "Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive anyone's sins, they are forgiven; if you retain them, they are retained" (John 20:22-23). The Lord Christ calls this same Holy Spirit now the Paraclete, now the Spirit of truth. He is not a newcomer in the Gospel, nor was He given for the first time there. It was this very Spirit who accused the people through the prophets and who acted as advocate for the nations through the apostles. The former deserved accusation because they had despised the Law; the latter deserve the Spirit's advocacy because they strive to attain the law of the Gospel. There is a real difference in the kinds of duties He performs, since the reasons for His action vary with the times; yet He who acts is not thereby a different person, nor does He become another while so acting. He remains one and the same, distributing His offices across times, occasions, and moments. Finally, the apostle Paul writes: "Since we have the same spirit of faith as it is written, 'I believed, therefore I spoke,' we also believe and therefore speak" (2 Cor 4:13). So it is one and the same Spirit at work in the prophets and the apostles — except that there He was present only for a moment, whereas here He abides forever. There He did not dwell in them permanently; here He remains in them always. There He was distributed in measure; here He is poured out in fullness. There He was given sparingly; here He is supplied lavishly. Yet He was not manifested before the Lord's resurrection, but was bestowed through Christ's resurrection. For Jesus said, "I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate to be with you forever — the Spirit of truth" (John 14:16-17). "When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father — the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father" (John 15:26). "If I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send Him to you" (John 16:7). "When the Spirit of truth comes, He will guide you into all the truth" (John 16:13).

latin: Sed enim ordo rationis et fidei auctoritas digestis uocibus et litteris domini admonet nos post haec credere etiam in spiritum sanctum, olim ecclesiae repromissum, sed statutis temporum opportunitatibus redditum. est enim per Ioelem prophetam repromissus, sed per Christum redditus. in nouissimis, inquit, diebus effundam de spiritu meo super seruos et ancillas meas. dominus autem: accipite spiritum sanctum; quorum remiseritis peccata, erunt remissa; et quorum retinueritis, erunt retenta. hunc autem spiritum sanctum dominus Christus modo paracletum appellat, modo spiritum ueritatis esse pronuntiat. qui non est in euangelio nouus, sed nec noue datus. nam hic ipse et in prophetis populum accusauit, et in apostolis aduocationem gentibus praestitit. nam illi ut accusarentur merebantur, quia contempserant legem: et qui ex gentibus credunt, ut patrocinio spiritus adiuuentur merentur, quia ad euangelicam peruenire gestiunt legem. differentia sane in illo genera officiorum, quoniam in temporibus differens ratio causarum: nec ex hoc tamen ipse diuersus, qui haec sic gerit, nec alter est, dum sic agit, sed unus atque ipse est, diuidens officia sua per tempora et rerum occasiones atque momenta. denique apostolus Paulus: habentes, inquit, eundem spiritum, sicut scriptum est: credidi, propter quod locutus sum, et nos credimus, ideo loquimur. vnus ergo et idem spiritus, qui in prophetis et apostolis; nisi quoniam ibi ad momentum, hic semper. ceterum ibi, non ut semper in illis inesset, hic, ut in illis semper maneret: et ibi mediocriter distributus, hic totus effusus; ibi parce datus, hic large commodatus; nec tamen ante resurrectionem’ domini exhibitus, sed per resurrectionem Christi contributus. rogabo enim aiebat, patrem, et alium aduocatum dabit uobis, ut uobiscum sit in aeternum, spiritum ueritatis. et: cum uenerit aduocatus ile, quem ego missurus sum uobis a patre meo, spiritum ueritatis, qui de patre meo procedit. et: si non abiero ego, aduocatus ille non ueniet ad uos: si autem ego abiero, remittam illum ad uos. et: cum uenerit spiritus ueritatis, ille uos diriget in omnem ueritatem.

excerpts.author: Didache
english: Concerning baptism, baptize in this way: after you have said all these things, baptize into the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit using living water. If you do not have living water, use other water; if you cannot baptize in cold water, use warm water. If you have neither, pour water on the head three times into the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. Before the baptism, let the one who baptizes and the one who is baptized fast, and anyone else who is able; you must command the one being baptized to fast for one or two days.

excerpts.author: Barnabas
english: Let us ask whether the Lord saw fit to reveal the meaning of the water and the cross. Concerning the water, Scripture addresses Israel: the baptism that brings forgiveness of sins will not be accepted, yet they will build for themselves. The prophet declares, "Be appalled, O heavens, and shudder, O earth, for this people has committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the spring of living water, and have dug their own cisterns, broken cisterns that hold no water" (Jeremiah 2:13). "Is my holy mountain Sinai a barren rock? You will become like fledglings fluttering away, torn from the nest." Again the prophet says, "I will go before you and level the mountains; I will shatter bronze gates and break iron bars. I will give you hidden, dark, unseen treasures, so that you may know that I am the Lord God" (Isaiah 45:2–3). Also: "You will dwell in a high cave of a strong rock." And: "His water is faithful; you will see the king in glory, and your soul will meditate on the fear of the Lord." In another prophet we read: "The one who does these things is like a tree planted by streams of water, which yields its fruit in season, whose leaf does not wither, and whatever he does prospers" (Psalm 1:3). The wicked are not so; they are like chaff the wind blows away. Therefore the wicked will not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous, for the Lord knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked perishes. Notice how the water and the cross are appointed for the same end. He says: "Blessed are those who, hoping in the cross, have gone down into the water." He adds that the reward comes in its own time: "Then, he says, I will repay." Now "the leaf will not wither" means this: every word that proceeds from your mouth in faith and love will become a means of repentance and hope for many. Another prophet says: "The land of Jacob was praised above all the earth" — meaning the vessel of his Spirit is glorified. Then: "A river flowed from the right, and beautiful trees grew from it; whoever eats of them will live forever." This signifies that we go down into the water full of sins and filth, and come up bearing fruit in our hearts — the fear and hope in Jesus, possessing the Spirit. "Whoever eats of these will live forever" means: whoever hears these words spoken and believes will live forever.

greek: Ζητήσωμεν δέ, εἰ ἐμέλησεν τῷ κυρίῳ προφανερῶσαι περὶ τοῦ ὕδατος καὶ περὶ τοῦ σταυροῦ. περὶ μὲν τοῦ ὕδατος γέγραπται ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰσραήλ, πῶς τὸ βάπτισμα τὸ φέρον ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν οὐ μὴ προσδέξονται, ἀλλ’ ἑαυτοῖς οἰκοδομήσουσιν. λέγει γὰρ ὁ προφήτης: Ἔκστηθι οὐρανέ, καὶ ἐπὶ τούτῳ πλεῖον φριξάτω ἡ γῆ, ὅτι δύο καὶ πονηρὰ ἐποίησεν ὁ λαὸς οὗτος: ἐμὲ ἐγκατέλιπον, πηγὴν ζωῆς, καὶ ἑαυτοῖς ὤρυξαν βόθρον θανάτου. Μὴ πέτρα ἔρημός ἐστιν τὸ ὄρος τὸ ἅγιόν μου Σινᾶ; ἔσεσθε γὰρ ὡς πετεινοῦ νοσσοὶ ἀνιπτάμενοι νοσσιᾶς ἀφῃρημένοι. καὶ πάλιν λέγει ὁ προφήτης: Ἐγὼ πορεύσομαι ἔμπροσθέν σου καὶ ὄρη ὁμαλιῶ καὶ πύλας χαλκᾶς συντρίψω καὶ μοχλοὺς σιδηροῦς συγκλάσω, καὶ δώσω σοι θησαυροὺς σκοτεινούς, ἀποκρύφους, ἀοράτους, ἵνα γνῶσιν ὅτι ἐγὼ κύριος ὁ θεός. καί: Κατοικήσεις ἐν ὑψηλῷ σπηλαίῳ πέτρας ἰσχυρᾶς. καί: τὸ ὕδωρ αὐτοῦ πιστόν: βασιλέα μετὰ δόξης ὄψεσθε, καὶ ἡ ψυχὴ ὑμῶν μελετήσει φόβον κυρίου καὶ πάλιν ἐν ἄλλῳ προφήτῃ λέγει: Καὶ ἔσται ὁ ταῦτα ποιῶν ὡς τὸ ξύλον τὸ πεφυτευμένον παρὰ τὰς διεξόδους τῶν ὑδάτων, ὃ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ δώσει ἐν καιρῷ αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὸ φύλλον αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἀπορυήσεται, καὶ πάντα, ὅσα ἂν ποιῇ, κατευοδωθήσεται. οὐχ οὕτως οἱ ἀσεβεῖς, οὐχ οὕτως, ἀλλ’ ἢ ὡς ὁ χνοῦς, ὃν ἐκρίπτει ὁ ἄνεμος ἀπὸ προσώπου τῆς γῆς. διὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἀναστήσονται ἀσεβεῖς ἐν κρίσει οὐδὲ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἐν βουλῇ δικαίων, ὅτι γινώσκει κύριος ὁδὸν δικαίων, καὶ ὁδὸς ἀσεβῶν ἀπολεῖται. αἰσθάνεσθε, πῶς τὸ ὕδωρ καὶ τὸν σταυρὸν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ὥρισεν. τοῦτο γὰρ λέγει: μακάριοι, οἲ ἐπὶ τὸν σταυρὸν ἐλπίσαντες κατέβησαν εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ, ὅτι τὸν μὲν μισθὸν λέγει ἐν καιρῷ αὐτοῦ: τότε, φησίν, ἀποδώσω. νῦν δὲ ὅ λέγει: τὰ φύλλα οὐκ ἀπορυήσεται, τοῦτο λέγει: ὅτι πᾶν ῥῆμα, ὃ ἐὰν ἐξελεύσεται ἐξ ὑμῶν διὰ τοῦ στόματος ὑμῶν ἐν πίστει καὶ ἀγάπῃ, ἔσται εἰς ἐπιστροφὴν καὶ ἐλπίδα πολλοῖς. καὶ πάλιν ἕτερος προφήτης λέγει. Καὶ ἦν ἡ γῆ τοῦ Ἰακὼβ ἐπαινουμένη παρὰ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν. τοῦτο λέγει: τὸ σκεῦος τοῦ πνεύματος αὐτοῦ δοξάζει. εἶτα τί λέγει; Καὶ ἦν ποταμὸς ἕλκων ἐκ δεξιῶν, καὶ ἀνέβαινεν ἐξ αὐτοῦ δένδρα ὡραῖα: καὶ ὃς ἂν φάγῃ ἐξ αὐτῶν, ζήσεται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα. τοῦτο λέγει ὅτι ἡμεῖς μὲν καταβαίνομεν εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ γέμοντες ἁμαρτιῶν καὶ ῥύπου, καὶ ἀναβαίνομεν καρποφοροῦντες ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ τὸν φόβον καὶ τὴν ἐλπίδα εἰς τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐν τῷ πνεύματι ἔχοντες. Καὶ ὃς ἂν φάγῃ ἀπὸ τούτων, ζήσεται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, τοῦτο λέγει: ὃς ἄν, φησίν, ἀκούσῃ τούτων λαλουμένων καὶ πιστεύσῃ, ζήσεται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.

excerpts.citation: Ignatius of Antioch — To the Ephesians 18
excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: My spirit is a lowly offering laid down for the cross. To those who do not believe, the cross is a stumbling block (1 Corinthians 1:23); to us it is salvation and eternal life (1 Corinthians 1:18). Where is the wise man? Where is the debater (1 Corinthians 1:20)? Where is the boasting of the so-called clever?

For our God, Jesus the Christ, was carried in the womb by Mary, as God had planned: of David's seed (Romans 1:3), yet of the Holy Spirit (Matthew 1:18, 20). He was born, and he was baptized, so that by his suffering he might make the water clean.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: Brothers, do not speak any evil against the crucified one, nor mock his bruises, by which it is possible for all to be healed, just as we also have been healed. It is a good thing, if you are persuaded by these words, to circumcise your hardness of heart—a hardness you do not possess because of your own opinion, since it was given as a sign, not as a work of righteousness, as the words compel. Therefore, having come to agreement, do not rail against the Son of God, nor, by obeying Pharisee teachers, ever despise the King of Israel, just as your synagogue rulers teach after the prayer. For if the one who touches things not pleasing to God is like one who touches the daughter of God, how much more so the one who touches the Beloved. That this one is he has been sufficiently demonstrated. When they fell silent, I said: 'I, my friends, now speak the scriptures as the Seventy interpreted them; for having spoken them to you previously just as you possess them, I was testing you to see how your opinion was already disposed.' For when I recited the scripture that says: 'Woe to them, because they devise a wicked plan against themselves,' saying, 'Let us remove the righteous one, because he is troublesome to us,' as the Seventy interpreted it, I assented; but you said, 'Let us bind the righteous one, because he is troublesome to us,' speaking exactly what you wished to say. You have done something else, and it does not seem to me that you have listened attentively to the words. But since the day is now about to end—for the sun is already in the west—I will cease after adding one thing to what has been said; yet this very thing was also spoken to me within what was said, and it seems right to me to elaborate on it again. (Isaiah 3:10-11)

greek: Μὴ δή, ὦ ἀδελφοί, κακόν τι εἴπητε εἰς ἐκεῖνον τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον, μηδὲ χλευάσητε αὐτοῦ τοὺς μώλωπας, οἷς ἰαθῆναι πᾶσι δυνατόν, ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς ἰάθημεν . Καλὸν γάρ, ἢν πεισθέντες τοῖς λόγοις περιτμηθῆτε τὴν σκληροκαρδίαν, ἥν οὐχὶ δι᾿ ὑμῶν ἐγγινομένην γνώμην ἔχετε, ἐπειδὴ εἰς σημεῖον ἦν δεδομένη, ἀλλ᾿ οὐκ εἰς δικαιοπραξίας ἔργον, ὡς οἱ λόγοι ἀναγκάζουσι. Συμφάμενοι οὖν μὴ λοιδορῆτε ἐπὶ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ, μηδὲ Φαρισαίοις πειθόμενοι διδασκάλοις τὸν βασιλέα τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ ἐπισκώψητέ ποτε, ὁποῖα διδάσκουσιν οἱ ἀρχισυνάγωγοι ὑμῶν, μετὰ τὴν προσευχήν. Εἰ γὰρ ὁ ἁπτόμενος τῶν μὴ εὐαρέστων τῷ θεῷ ὡς ὁ ἁπτόμενος κόρης τοῦ θεοῦ , πολὺ μᾶλλον ὁ τοῦ ἠγαπημένου καθαπτόμενος . Ὅτι δὲ οὗτος αὐτός ἐστι, καὶ ἱκανῶς ἀποδέδεικται. Καὶ σιγώντων αὐτῶν εἶπον· Ἐγώ, ὦ φίλοι. καὶ τὰς γραφὰς λέγω νῦν ὡς ἐξηγήσαντο οἱ ἑβδομήκοντα· εἰπὼν γὰρ αὐτὰς πρότερον ὡς ὑμεῖς αὐτὰς ἔχετε, πεῖραν ὑμῶν ἐποιούμην πῶς διάκεισθε ἤδη τὴν γνώμην. Λέγων γὰρ τὴν γραφήν, ἣ λέγει· Οὐαὶ αὐτοῖς, ὅτι βεβούλευνται βουλὴν πονηρὰν καθ᾿ ἑαυτῶν εἰπόντες· ὡς ἐξηγήσαντο οἱ ἑβδομήκοντα ἐπήνεγκα· Ἄρωμεν τὸν δίκαιον, ὅτι δύσχρηστος ἡμῖν ἐστιν· ἐμοῦ ἐν ἀρχῇ τῆς ὁμιλίας καὶ εἰπόντος ὅπερ ὑμεῖς εἰρῆσθαι βούλεσθε, εἰπόντες· Δήσωμεν τὸν δίκαιον, ὅτι δύσχρηστος ἡμῖν ἐστιν . Ἄλλα δέ τινα ἐπράξατε, καὶ οὐ δοκεῖτέ μοι ἐνηκόως τῶν λόγων ἐπακηκοέναι. Ἀλλ᾿ ἐπεὶ καὶ νῦν ἤδη ἡ ἡμέρα πέρας ποιεῖσθαι μέλλει, πρὸς δυσμὰς γὰρ ἤδη ὁ ἥλιός ἐστι, καὶ ἔν τι προσθεὶς τοῖς εἰρημένοις παύσομαι· τοῦτο δ᾿ αὐτὸ καὶ ἐν τοῖς εἰρημένοις μοι ἐρρέθη, ἀλλὰ πάλιν αὐτὸ ἐπεξεργάσασθαι ἄν δίκαιον εἶναί μοι δοκεῖ.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: I will explain how we devoted ourselves to God after being renewed through Christ, so that by covering this point we may not appear to be doing something wrong in our account. Those who are persuaded and believe that what we teach and say is true, and who promise they can live accordingly, are taught to pray and ask God for forgiveness of their past sins while fasting, with us praying and fasting alongside them. Then we lead them to where there is water, and they are reborn in the same manner of rebirth that we ourselves experienced. For in the name of God, the Father of all and our Master, and of our Savior Jesus Christ, and of the Holy Spirit, they undergo the washing in the water. Christ said, "Unless you are born again, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven" (John 3:5). It is obvious to everyone that those who have been born once cannot re-enter the wombs of those who gave birth to them. Through the prophet Isaiah, as we wrote earlier, it was declared how those who have sinned and repent will escape their sins. The words are: "Wash yourselves, become clean, remove the evil from your souls, learn to do good, seek justice for the orphan, defend the widow, and come now, let us reason together," says the Lord. "Though your sins are like scarlet, I will make them white as snow; though they are like crimson, I will make them white as wool. But if you refuse to listen, the sword will devour you, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken" (Isaiah 1:16–20). We learned this teaching from the apostles for this very reason. Since we were born by necessity from moist seed through the union of our parents, without knowledge of our first birth, and fell into foul and evil habits, we must not remain children of necessity and ignorance but become children of choice and knowledge, obtaining forgiveness for the sins we previously committed. Over the one who chooses to be reborn and has repented of their sins, the name of God, the Father of all and our Master, is invoked in the water as the one leading them to the washing pronounces that name alone. No one can utter a name for the unutterable God; anyone who dares claim to do so displays reckless madness. This washing is called enlightenment, because the minds of those learning these things are enlightened. And in the name of Jesus Christ, who was crucified under Pontius Pilate, and in the name of the Holy Spirit, who foretold through the prophets all things concerning Jesus, the one being enlightened is washed.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: After the person who has been convinced and has assented is washed in this way, we bring them to the so-called brothers, where they are gathered together, so that we may offer common prayers for ourselves, for the one who has been enlightened, and for all others everywhere. We pray so that, having learned the true things, we may be deemed worthy and be found to be good citizens through our deeds and guardians of the things entrusted to us, so that we may be saved for eternal salvation. We greet one another with a kiss after the prayers have ended.

Then bread, a cup of water, and wine are offered to the one presiding over the brothers. He takes them and offers praise and glory to the Father of all through the name of the Son and the Holy Spirit, and he makes a lengthy thanksgiving for having been deemed worthy of these gifts by him. When he has finished the prayers and the thanksgiving, all the people present shout out, saying: Amen. In the Hebrew language, Amen means "so be it." After the presider has given thanks and all the people have shouted, those we call deacons give each of those present a share of the bread, wine, and water over which thanks has been given, and they carry it to those who are absent.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: We have already received a portion of God's Spirit as a down payment toward perfection and preparation for incorruptibility, growing gradually accustomed to bearing and carrying God within us. The apostle calls this a guarantee — that is, a share in the honor God has promised us — writing to the Ephesians: "In him you also, when you heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, and believed in him, were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit, who is the guarantee of our inheritance" (Eph 1:13–14). Because this guarantee dwells in us, it already makes us spiritual people, transforming what is mortal by the power of immortality. As the apostle says, "You are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if in fact the Spirit of God dwells in you" (Rom 8:9). This change does not mean the loss of our flesh, but its communion with the Spirit. The recipients of that letter were not without bodies; they had received the Spirit of God, in whom we cry out, "Abba, Father." If even now, holding the guarantee, we cry "Abba, Father," what will happen when we rise and see him face to face? When our limbs pour out a hymn of overflowing joy, glorifying the one who raised us from the dead and gave us eternal life? If the guarantee, embracing us, already enables us to call God Father, what will the full measure of the Spirit's grace — given to humanity by God — accomplish? It will conform us to Christ and bring us to the Father's perfection, for it will fashion humanity according to the image and likeness of God.

Therefore, those who possess the Spirit's guarantee and refuse to serve the flesh, instead submitting themselves to the Spirit and living justly in every way, are rightly called spiritual by the apostle, because the Spirit of God dwells in them. Spiritual people are not disembodied spirits; our substance — the union of soul and body — receives the Spirit of God and so is brought to completion. But those who reject the Spirit's counsel and enslave themselves to fleshly pleasures live irrationally, abandoned without restraint to their desires. They have no breath of the divine Spirit; they live like pigs and dogs. The apostle rightly calls them carnal, for they perceive nothing beyond the flesh. For the same reason, the prophets liken them to irrational animals, citing their irrational herd behavior: "Stallions maddened with lust, each neighing after his neighbor's wife" (Jer 5:8). Again: "Man in his pomp, yet without understanding, is like the beasts that perish" (Ps 49:20). They are compared to beasts because they choose an irrational life. In common speech we too call such people brute beasts. The law anticipated all this figuratively, sketching the human portrait through animals: "Whatever has a divided hoof and chews the cud is clean; whatever lacks one or both is unclean" (Lev 11:3–4). Who then are clean? Those who walk firmly by faith in the Father and the Son — that is the stability of the divided hoof — and who meditate on God's words day and night so they may be adorned with good works — that is the virtue of chewing the cud. The unclean who lack both hoof and rumination are those who have no faith in God and do not meditate on his words: this is the abomination of the nations. Those who chew the cud but lack the divided hoof — these are unclean — represent the Jews: they have God's words in their mouths but do not root themselves firmly in the Father and the Son. Their kind is slippery, like single-hoofed animals that easily stumble. But those with divided hooves stand firmer, each step supporting the next, one hoof bearing up the other. Similarly unclean are those who have the divided hoof but do not ruminate: this describes all heretics and those who neglect God's words and are not adorned with works of justice. To them the Lord says, "Why do you call me 'Lord, Lord,' and not do what I tell you?" (Luke 6:46). They claim to believe in the Father and the Son, yet they never meditate on God's words as they ought, nor are they clothed in righteous deeds. Instead, as we have said, they have adopted the life of pigs and dogs, surrendering themselves to impurity, gluttony, and every other vice. Justly, therefore, the apostle calls all such people carnal: because of their unbelief and self-indulgence they fail to receive the divine Spirit, and they cast themselves out in various ways, living irrationally in their lusts. The prophets named them beasts and wild animals; custom calls them irrational cattle; the law declares them unclean.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: We now receive a portion of His Spirit as a down payment toward perfection and preparation for incorruptibility, gradually growing accustomed to taking and bearing God within us. The Apostle calls this a guarantee—that is, a share of the honor God has promised us—in his letter to the Ephesians, where he writes that you, having heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, and having believed, were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit, who is the guarantee of our inheritance (Ephesians 1:13-14). Because this guarantee dwells in us, it now makes us spiritual, turning what is mortal into immortality. As Paul says, you are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, since the Spirit of God dwells in you (Romans 8:9). This transformation does not happen by the loss of the flesh but by communion with the Spirit. After all, those to whom he wrote still had bodies; they had simply received the Spirit of God, in whom we cry, "Abba, Father." If we already cry "Abba, Father" while holding only the guarantee, what will happen when we rise and see Him face to face? When our members overflow with a hymn of abundant exultation, glorifying the One who raised them from the dead and gave them eternal life? If the guarantee, embracing a person within itself, already makes us say "Abba, Father," what will the full grace of the Spirit do when it is given to humanity by God? It will make us like Him and perfect us as the Father is perfect, for it will fashion humanity according to the image and likeness of God.

Therefore, the Apostle rightly calls those who possess the guarantee of the Spirit and do not serve the flesh but subject themselves to the Spirit—and who live justly in all things—spiritual, because the Spirit of God dwells in them. Disembodied spirits would not be spiritual human beings; rather, our substance, the union of soul and body, becomes a perfect human being when it receives the Spirit of God. But those who reject the Spirit's counsel and serve the pleasures of the flesh, living irrationally and surrendering unrestrained to their desires, have no aspiration of the divine Spirit; they live like pigs and dogs. The Apostle justly calls them carnal, for they sense nothing but carnal things. For this same reason the prophets also liken them to irrational animals, pointing to their irrational gathering: "Stallions maddened have become like mares, each one neighing after his neighbor's wife." Again: "When he was in honor, he was likened to the beasts of burden." This is because he emulates an irrational life, making himself like the beasts. We, too, in common speech call such people beasts of burden and irrational cattle. The Law, however, foretold all this figuratively, portraying humanity through animals. It says: whatever has a divided hoof and chews the cud is declared clean; whatever lacks one or both is set apart as unclean. Who, then, are the clean? Those who make their way firmly to the Father and the Son through faith; this firmness is the divided hoof. And they meditate on God's words day and night so that they may be adorned with good works; this is the virtue of chewing the cud. The unclean are those who have neither the divided hoof nor chew the cud—that is, those who have no faith in God and do not meditate on His words; this is the abomination of the Gentiles. Those who chew the cud but lack the divided hoof are also unclean; this is the portrait of the Jews, who have God's words in their mouths but do not root their stability in the Father and the Son, and so their kind is slippery. They are single-hoofed animals that easily slip; but those with a divided hoof are more stable, their split hooves succeeding each other along the way, one hoof supporting the other. Likewise unclean are those who have the divided hoof but do not chew the cud; this describes all heretics and those who do not meditate on God's words nor adorn themselves with works of justice. To them the Lord says: "Why do you call me 'Lord, Lord,' and not do what I tell you?" (Matthew 7:21-23). For such people claim to believe in the Father and the Son, yet they never meditate on God's words as they ought, nor are they adorned with works of justice; instead, as we said before, they have taken on the life of pigs and dogs, surrendering themselves to uncleanness, gluttony, and the rest of the vices. Justly, therefore, the Apostle calls all such people carnal and animal-like because their unbelief and luxury keep them from attaining the divine Spirit, and they cast themselves out in various ways, living irrationally in their lusts; the prophets call them beasts of burden and wild animals; common usage interprets them as irrational cattle; and the Law declares them unclean.

latin: Nunc autem partem aliquam a Spiritu ejus sumimus, ad perfectionem et praeparationem incorruptele, paulatim assuescentes capere et portare Deum: quod et pignus dixit Apostolus, hoc est, pars ejus honoris qui a Deo nobis promissus est, in epistola quze ad Ephesios est, dicens: In quo et vos, audito verbo veritatis, Evangelio salutis vestrar, in quo credentes signati Spiritu promissionis sancto, qui est pignus hwreditatis nostra. Sie ergo pignus hoc habitans in nobis jam spiritales efficit, et mortale ab immortalitate; Vos enim, ait, non estis in carne, sed in Spiritu, siquidem Spiritus Dei habitat in vobis. isautem non secundum jacturam carnis, sed secundum communionem Spiritus fit. Non enim erant sine carne, quibus scribebat ; sed qui assumserant Spiritum Dei, in quo clamamus, Abba Pater. Si igitur nunc pignus habentes clamamus, Abba Pater; quid fiet quando resurgentes faciem ad faciem videbimus eum; quando membra affluenter exultationis hymnum protulerint, glorificantia eum, qui suscitaverit ea ex mortuis, et eternam vitam donaverit ? Si enim pignus 7 complectens hominem in semetipsum, jam facit dicere, Abba Pater, quid faciet universa Spiritus gratia, quze hominibus dabitur §a Deo? similes nos ei efficiet, et perficiet Patris; efficiet enim hominem secundum imaginem et similitudinem Dei. Qui ergo pignus Spiritus habent, et non carnis serviunt, sed subjiciunt semetipsos Spiritui, conversantur in omnibus, juste Apostolus spiritales vocat, quoniam Spiritus Dei habitat in ipsis. Ineorporales autem spiritus non erunt homines spiritales; sed substantia nostra, id est, anime et carnis adunatio assumens Spiritum Dei, hominem perficit. Eos autem qui abjiciunt quidem Spiritus consilium, carnis autem voluptatibus serviunt, et irrationabiliter vivunt, et ineffrenati dejiciuntur in sua desideria, quippe nullam habentes aspirationem divini spiritus, sed porcorum et canum more vivunt; hos juste Apostolus carnales vocat, quoniam nihil aliud quam carnalia sentiunt. 2. Qui sunt ergo mundi? excerpts.author: Theophilus of Antioch
english: The beginning of creation is light, because the things being made are revealed by the light (Genesis 1:1-31). Therefore God says, 'Let there be light,' and it is clear that the light is good for humans (Genesis 1:1-31). God separates the light from the darkness, calls the light day and the darkness night, and there is evening and morning, the first day (Genesis 1:1-31). God says, 'Let there be a firmament in the middle of the water to separate water from water,' and it happens; God makes the firmament, separates the water under it from the water above it, calls the firmament heaven, and sees that it is good; evening and morning mark the second day (Genesis 1:1-31). God says, 'Let the water under heaven be gathered into one place and let dry land appear,' and it happens; the water gathers, dry land appears, God calls the dry land earth and the gatherings seas, and sees that it is good; evening and morning mark the third day (Genesis 1:1-31). God says, 'Let the earth produce vegetation, plants yielding seed according to their kind and likeness, and trees bearing fruit with seed in them according to their kind,' and it happens; the earth produces vegetation and trees, and God sees that it is good; evening and morning mark the third day (Genesis 1:1-31). God says, 'Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven to give light on the earth, to separate day and night, and to serve as signs, seasons, days, and years,' and it happens; God makes the two great lights—the greater to rule the day, the lesser to rule the night—and the stars, places them in the firmament to give light on the earth, to rule day and night, and to separate light from darkness, and sees that it is good; evening and morning mark the fourth day (Genesis 1:1-31). God says, 'Let the waters produce living creatures and let birds fly above the earth across the firmament,' and it happens; God makes the great sea creatures and every living thing that moves, and every winged bird according to its kind, sees that it is good, blesses them saying, 'Be fruitful and multiply, fill the waters in the seas, and let the birds multiply on the earth'; evening and morning mark the fifth day (Genesis 1:1-31). God says, 'Let the earth produce living creatures according to their kinds—four‑footed animals, creeping things, and beasts of the earth,' and it happens; God makes the beasts, livestock, and all creeping things, and sees that it is good (Genesis 1:1-31). God says, 'Let us make man in our image and likeness, and let them rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of heaven, the livestock, all the earth, and every creeping thing,' and God makes man in His image, male and female, blesses them saying, 'Be fruitful and multiply, fill the earth, subdue it, and rule over the fish, birds, livestock, all the earth, and every creeping thing,' and says, 'Behold, I have given you every seed‑bearing plant and every tree with fruit for food, and to every beast, bird, and creeping thing with the breath of life, every green plant for food'; it happens, and God sees everything He made, and behold, it is very good; evening and morning mark the sixth day (Genesis 1:1-31). The heavens and the earth and all their host are completed; God finishes His work on the sixth day, rests on the seventh day from all His work, blesses the seventh day and sanctifies it because He rested from all His work that He began to make (Genesis 1:1-31).

greek: Ἀρχὴ δὲ τῆς ποιήσεως φῶς ἐστιν, ἐπειδὴ τὰ κοσμούμενα τὸ φῶς φανεροῖ. Διὸ λέγει· Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ θεός· Γενηθήτω φῶς. [Καὶ ἐγένετο φῶς. Καὶ εἶδεν ὁ θεὸς τὸ φῶς ὅτι καλόν.] Δηλονότι καλὸν ἀνθρώπῳ γεγονός. Καὶ διεχώρισεν ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ φωτὸς καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σκότους. Καὶ ἐκάλεσεν ὁ θεὸς τὸ φῶς ἡμέραν, καὶ τὸ σκότος ἐκάλεσε νύκτα. Καὶ ἐγένετο ἑσπέρα καὶ ἐγένετο πρωΐ, ἡμέρα μία. Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ θεός· Γενηθήτω στερέωμα ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ ὕδατος, καὶ ἔστω διαχωρίζον ἀνὰ μέσον ὕδατος καὶ ὕδατος. Καὶ ἐγένετο οὕτως. Καὶ ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς τὸ στερέωμα, καὶ διεχώρισεν ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ ὕδατος ὃ ἦν ὑποκάτω τοῦ στερεώματος, καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ ὕδατος τοῦ ἐπάνω τοῦ στερεώματος. Καὶ ἐκάλεσεν ὁ θεὸς· τὸ στερέωμα οὐρανόν· καὶ εἶδεν ὁ θεὸς ὅτι καλόν. Καὶ ἐγένετο ἑσπέρα καὶ ἐγένετο πρωΐ, ἡμέρα δευτέρα. Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ θεός· Συναχθήτω τὸ ὕδωρ τὸ ὑποκάτω τοῦ οὐρανοῦ εἰς συναγωγὴν μίαν, καὶ ὀφθήτω ἡ ξηρά. Καὶ ἐγένετο οὕτως. Καὶ συνήχθη τὸ ὕδωρ εἰς τὰς συναγωγὰς αὐτῶν, καὶ ὤφθη ἡ ξηρά. Καὶ ἐκάλεσεν ὁ θεὸς τὴν ξηρὰν γῆν, καὶ τὰ συστήματα τῶν ὑδάτων ἐκάλεσεν θαλάσσας. Καὶ εἶδεν ὁ θεὸς ὅτι καλόν. Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ θεός· Βλαστησάτω ἡ γῆ βοτάνην χόρτου σπεῖρον σπέρμα κατὰ γένος καὶ καθ᾿ ὁμοιότητα, καὶ ξύλον κάρπιμον ποιοῦν καρπόν, οὗ τὸ σπέρμα αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ εἰς ὁμοιότητα. Καὶ ἐγένετο οὕτως. Καὶ ἐξήνεγκεν ἡ γῆ βοτάνην χόρτου σπεῖρον σπέρμα κατὰ γένος, καὶ ξύλον κάρπιμον ποιοῦν καρπόν, οὗ τὸ σπέρμα ἐν αὐτῷ κατὰ γένος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. Καὶ εἶδεν ὁ θεὸς ὅτι καλόν. Καὶ ἐγένετο ἑσπέρα καὶ ἐγένετο πρωΐ, ἡμέρα τρίτη. Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ θεός· Γενηθήτωσαν φωστῆρες ἐν τῷ στερεώματι τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, εἰς φαῦσιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ διαχωρίζειν ἀνὰ μέσον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τῆς κυκτός, καὶ ἔστωσαν εἰς σημεῖα καὶ εἰς καιροὺς καὶ εἰς ἡμέρας καὶ εἰς ἐνιαυτούς, καὶ ἔστωσαν εἰς φαῦσιν ἐν τῷ στερεώματι τοῦ οὐρανοῦ φαίνειν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. Καὶ ἐγένετο οὕτως. Καὶ ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς τοὺς δύο φωστῆρας τοὺς μεγάλους, τὸν φωστῆρα τὸν μέγαν εἰς ἀρχὰς τῆς ἡμέρας, καὶ τὸν φωστῆρα τὸν ἐλάσσω εἰς ἀρχὰς τῆς κυκτός, καὶ τοὺς ἀστέρας· καὶ ἔθετο αὐτοὺς ὁ θεὸς ἐν τῷ στερεώματι τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ὥστε φαίνειν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἄρχειν τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τῆς νυκτός, καὶ διαχωρίζειν ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ φωτὸς καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σκότους. Καὶ εἶδεν ὁ θεὸς ὅτι καλόν. Καὶ ἐγένετο ἑσπέρα καὶ ἐγένετο πρωΐ, ἡμέρα τετάρτη. Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ θεός· Ἐξαγαγέτω τὰ ὕδατα ἑρπετὰ ψυχῶν ζωσῶν, καὶ πετεινὰ πετόμενα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς κατὰ τὸ στερέωμα τοῦ οὐρανοῦ. Καὶ ἐγένετο οὕτως. Καὶ ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς τὰ κήτη τὰ μεγάλα καὶ πᾶσαν ψυχὴν ζώων ἑρπετῶν, ἃ ἐξήγαγεν τὰ ὕδατα κατὰ γένη αὐτῶν, καὶ πᾶν πετεινὸν πτερωτὸν κατὰ γένος. Καὶ εἶδεν ὁ θεὸς ὅτι καλά. Καὶ εὐλόγησεν αὐτὰ ὁ θεὸς λέγων· Αὐξάνεσθε καὶ πληθύνεσθε, καὶ πληρώσατε τὰ ὕδατα τῆς θαλάσσης, καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ πληθυνέτω ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. Καὶ ἐγένετο ἑσπέρα καὶ ἐγένετο πρωΐ, ἡμέρα πέμπτη. Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ θεός· Ἐξαγαγέτω ἡ γῆ ψυχὴν ζῶσαν κατὰ γένος, τετράποδα καὶ ἑρπετὰ καὶ θηρία τῆς γῆς κατὰ γένος. Καὶ ἐγένετο οὕτως. Καὶ ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς τὰ θηρία τῆς γῆς κατὰ γένος, καὶ τὰ κτήνη κατὰ γένος, καὶ πάντα τὰ ἑρπετὰ τῆς γῆς. Καὶ εἶδεν ὁ θεὸς ὅτι καλόν. Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ θεός· Ποιήσωμεν ἄνθρωπον κατ᾿ εἰκόνα ἡμετέραν καὶ καθ᾿ ὁμοίωσιν, καὶ ἀρχέτωσαν τῶν ἰχθύων τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ τῶν πετεινῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ τῶν κτηνῶν καὶ πάσης τῆς γῆς καὶ πάντων τῶν ἑρπετῶν τῶν ἑρπόντων ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. Καὶ ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν ἄνθρωπον, κατ᾿ εἰκόνα θεοῦ ἐποίησεν αὐτόν, ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ ἐποίησεν αὐτούς. Καὶ εὐλόγησεν αὐτοὺς ὁ θεὸς λέγων· Αὐξάνεσθε καὶ πληθύνεσθε, καὶ πληρώσατε τὴν γῆν, καὶ κατακυριεύσατε αὐτῆς, καὶ ἄρχετε τῶν ἰχθύων τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ τῶν πετεινῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ πάντων τῶν κτηνῶν καὶ πάσης τῆς γῆς καὶ πάντων τῶν ἑρπετῶν τῶν ἑρπόντων ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ θεός· Ἰδοὺ δέδωκα ὑμῖν πᾶν χόρτον σπόριμον σπεῖρον σπέρμα, ὅ ἐστιν ἐπάνω πάσης τῆς γῆς, καὶ πᾶν ξύλον, ὃ ἔχει ἐν αὐτῷ καρπὸν σπέρματος σπορίμου, ὑμῖν ἔσται εἰς βρῶσιν, καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς θηρίοις τῆς γῆς καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς πετεινοῖς τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ παντὶ ἑρπετῷ ἕρποντι ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὃ ἔχει ἐν αὐτῷ πνοὴν ζωῆς. πάντα χόρτον χλωρὸν εἰς βρῶσιν. Καὶ ἐγένετο οὕτως. Καὶ εἶδεν ὁ θεὸς πάντα ὅσα ἐποίησεν, καὶ ἰδοὺ καλὰ λίαν. Καὶ ἐγένετο ἑσπέρα καὶ ἐγένετο πρωΐ, ἥμερα ἕκτη. Καὶ συνετελέσθησαν ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ καὶ πᾶς ὁ κόσμος αὐτῶν. Καὶ συνετέλεσεν ὁ θεὸς ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ἕκτῃ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ ἃ ἐποίησεν, καὶ κατέπαυσεν ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ἑβδόμῃ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ ὧν ἐποίησεν. Καὶ εὐλόγησεν ὁ θεὸς τὴν ἡμέραν τὴν ἑβδόμην, καὶ ἡγίασεν αὐτήν, ὅτι ἐν αὐτῇ κατέπαυσεν ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ ὧν ἤρξατο ὁ θεὸς ποιῆσαι.

excerpts.author: Theophilus of Antioch
english: But to start from earthly things below and call the making of created things human, lowly, and very weak in its conception toward God — that is what it is. A human, being low, begins building from the ground, yet cannot achieve order and make a roof unless he first lays a foundation. God's power, however, is shown in this: he first makes what comes to be from non‑being, and does so as he wishes. What is impossible for humans is possible for God. Therefore the prophet first spoke of the heaven's making as holding the character of a roof, saying, 'In the beginning God made the heaven' — that is, through the beginning the heaven came to be, as we have already shown (Genesis 1:1). He calls earth powerful ground and foundation; abyss is the mass of the waters; darkness exists because the heaven God made covered the waters and the earth like a lid. Spirit is what was brought upon the water, which God gave to quicken creation, just as a soul to a human — the fine mingling with the fine (for spirit is fine and water is fine) — so that the spirit may nourish the water, and the water together with the spirit may nourish creation, passing through everywhere. The one spirit, bearing a likeness of light, mediated between the water and the heaven, so that in some way darkness might not share with the heaven, which is nearer to God, before God said, 'Let light come to be.' Just as the heaven, being a vault, held the matter like a lump. And another prophet, named Isaiah, also spoke of the heaven, saying, 'God is the one who made the heaven like a vault and stretched it out like a tent to dwell' (Isaiah 40:22). God's arrangement — that is, his Word — shining like a lamp in an enclosed room, illuminated the region under heaven, having made it apart from the world. God called the light day and the darkness night; for a human would not have known to call the light day or the darkness night, nor anything else, had he not received the naming from the God who made them.

In the first premise of the history and genesis of the world, holy Scripture spoke not of this firmament but of another heaven, invisible to us, after which this visible heaven is called firmament — the one upon which half the water was taken up, so that it might serve humanity for rains, showers, and dews. The other half of the water was left on the earth for rivers, springs, and seas. While the water still held the earth, especially the hollow places, God through his Word made the water gather into one gathering and the dry land become visible, though it had previously been invisible. The earth, now visible, still existed unprepared. God therefore prepared and adorned it with all kinds of grasses, seeds, and plants.
