latin: Dehinc manus imponitur, per benedictionem advocans et invitans Spiritum sanctum. Sane humano ingenio licebit spiritum in aquam arcessere et concorporationem eorum, accommodatis desuper manibus, alio spiritu tantae claritatis animare; Deo autem in suo organo non licebit per manus sanctas sublimitatem modulari spiritalem? Sed est hoc quoque de veteri sacramento, quo nepotes suos ex Joseph Ephraim et Manassem Jacob, capitibus impositis et intermutatis manibus, benedixerit, et quidem ita transversim obliquatis in se, ut Christum deformantes, jam tunc portenderent benedictionem in Christum futuram. Tunc ille sanctissimus Spiritus super emundata et benedicta corpora libens a Patre descendit, super Baptismi aquas, tanquam pristinam sedem recognoscens, conquiescit, columbae figura delapsus in Dominum, ut natura Spiritus sancti declararetur per animal simplicitatis et innocentiae, quod etiam corporaliter ipso felle careat columba. Ideoque: Estote, inquit, simplices sicut columbae, ne hoc quidem sine argumento praecedentis figurae. Quemadmodum enim post aquas diluvii, quibus iniquitas antiqua purgata est, post Baptismum (ut ita dixerim) mundi pacem coelestis irae praeco columba terris adnuntiavit dimissa ex arca, et cum olea reversa; quod signum etiam apud nationes paci praetenditur: eadem dispositione spiritalis effectus terrae, id est carni nostrae emergenti de lavacro post vetera delicta, columba sancti Spiritus advolat, pacem Dei afferens, emissa de coelis, ubi Ecclesia est arca figurata. Sed mundus rursus delinquit, quo male comparetur Baptismus diluvio. Itaque igni destinatur, sicut et homo qui post Baptismum delicta restaurat, ut hoc quoque in signum admonitionis nostrae debeat accipi.

excerpts.author: Tertullian
english: How many natural safeguards, how many gracious privileges, how many disciplinary rites, figures, prefigurings, and prayers have established water's sacred role? (Exodus 14:28) First, when the people marched out of Egypt and crossed the sea, they escaped Pharaoh's power, while the water swallowed the king and his entire army. What figure could more clearly mirror the sacrament of Baptism? Nations are freed from the world through water, leaving behind the devil, their former master, crushed beneath the flood. (Exodus 15:25) Again, Moses' wood healed water poisoned by bitterness, turning it sweet for the people's benefit. That wood was Christ, who cures the deadliest veins of a poisonous, bitter nature through the waters of Baptism. This is the water that flowed from the rock that traveled with the people. If the rock is Christ, then beyond doubt we see the water in Christ blessed for Baptism. How immense is water's grace before God and his Christ for confirming Baptism. Christ is never without water, since he himself was baptized in it. (John 2:1-11) He launched the first signs of his power with water at a wedding feast. (John 4:14) When he preaches, he calls the thirsty to his eternal water. When he teaches on love, he endorses a cup of water offered to a brother as a work of love. He regains strength at a well; he walks freely on the water, crosses it, and serves water to his disciples. He keeps testifying to Baptism up to his passion; when he is handed over to the cross, water intervenes — Pilate's washing hands prove it; when his side is pierced, water bursts out — the soldier's lance bears witness. (John 19:34)

latin: Quot igitur patrocinia naturae, quot privilegia gratiae, quot solemnia disciplinae, figurae, praestructiones, precationes religionem aquae ordinaverunt? Primo quidem, cum populus de Aegypto libere expeditus, vim regis Aegypti, per aquam transgressus, evadit, ipsum regem cum totis copiis aqua exstinxit. Quae figura manifestior in Baptimi sacramento? Liberantur de saeculo nationes per aquam scilicet, et diabolum, dominatorem pristinum, in aqua oppressum derelinquunt. Item aqua de amaritudinis vitio in suum commodum suavitatis Mosei ligno remediatur. Lignum illud erat Christus, venenatae et amarae retro naturae venas insaluberrimas, aquas Baptismi, scilicet, ex sese remedians. Haec est aqua, quae de comite petra populo defluebat. Si enim petra Christus, sine dubio aqua in Christo Baptismum videmus benedici. Quanta aquae gratia penes Deum et Christum ejus est ad Baptismi confirmationem. Nunquam sine aqua Christus, siquidem et ipse aqua tinguitur. Prima rudimenta potestatis suae, vocatus ad nuptias, aqua auspicatur. Cum sermonem facit, sitientes ad aquam suam invitat sempiternam. Cum de agape docet, aquae calicem, fratri oblatum, inter opera dilectionis probat. Apud puteum vires resumit; super aquam incedit libenter, transfretat; aquam discentibus ministrat; perseverat testimonium Baptismi usque ad passionem; cum deditur in crucem, aqua intervenit, sciunt Pilati manus; cum vulneratur, aqua de latere prorumpit, scit lancea militis.

english: Preface In the name of the Father , and the Son , and the Holy Spirit , one God. This is a transcript of the excellent law. But before beginning to give the transcript of the book of the law, it will be worth while to instruct you, O brother, as to its excellence, and the dignity of its disposition. Its first excellence is, that God delivered it by the hand of our most blessed ruler, the chief of the prophets , and first of the apostles , or those who were sent to the children of Israel , viz. Moses the son of Amram, the son of Kohath, of the sons of Levi. Now he was adorned with all manner of wisdom, and endowed with the best genius. Illustrious in dignity, remarkable for the integrity of his disposition, distinguished for power of reason, he talked with God . And He chose him as an instrument of value. By His leader and prophet , God Most High sent it clown to us, and committed it to us (blessed be His name) in the Syriac tongue of the Targum, which the Seventy translated into the Hebrew tongue, to wit, into the tongue of the nation, and the idiom of the common people. Moses . therefore, received it from the eternal Lord, and was the first to whom it was entrusted, and who obeyed its rules and ordinances. Then he taught it to the children of Israel , who also embraced it. And he explained to them its profound mysteries and dark places. And he expounded to them those things which were less easy, as God permitted him, and concealed from them those secrets of the law, as God…

6. Hippolytus, the Syrian expositor of the Targum, has said: We find in an ancient Hebrew copy that God commanded Noah to range the wild beasts in order in the lower floor or storey, and to separate the males from the females by putting wooden stakes between them. And thus, too, he did with all the cattle, and also with the birds in the middle storey. And God ordered the males thus to be separated from the females for the sake of decency and purity, lest they should perchance get intermingled with each other. Moreover, God said to Moses : Provide victuals for yourself and your children. And let them be of wheat, ground, pounded, kneaded with water, and dried. And Noah there and then bade his wife, and his sons' wives, diligently attend to kneading dough and laying it in the oven. They kneaded dough accordingly, and prepared just about as much as might be sufficient for them, so that nothing should remain over but the very least. And God charged Noah , saying to him: Whosoever shall first announce to you the approach of the deluge, him you shall destroy that very moment. In the meantime, moreover, the wife of Cham was standing by, about to put a large piece of bread into the oven. And suddenly, according to the word of the Lord, water rushed forth from the oven, and the flow of water penetrated and destroyed the bread. Therefore the wife of Cham exclaimed, addressing herself to Noah : Oh, sir, the word of God has come good: that which God foretold has come to pass; execute,…

excerpts.author: Hippolytus
english: These words confront the Jewish people and the defilement they committed against Christ, because they believed their citizenship existed only on earth. The promise is not merely that they will 'receive' something, but that they will 'inherit' it. As for the wicked, even if they are exalted, their dishonor only becomes greater. It is like someone ugly and deformed: if you lift them up, you do not glorify them; you only make their shame more obvious to more people. In the same way, God exalts the wicked so that their shame becomes evident. Pharaoh was exalted too, but only so that the whole world would have him as an accuser.

excerpts.author: Cyprian
english: My beloved brothers, peace has returned to the Church, and what recently seemed impossible to unbelievers and the faithless has come to pass: our security has been restored through God's help and his vengeance. Joy has returned to our minds; the storm of oppression has blown over and the cloud has lifted, so that tranquility and serenity shine forth once more. We must give praise to God and celebrate his benefits and gifts with thanksgiving, even though our voice never stopped giving thanks, not even during the persecution. After all, the enemy cannot be allowed so much power that we who love the Lord with our whole heart and soul and strength would fail to proclaim his blessings and praises everywhere and always, with glory.

The day everyone longed for has arrived. After the horrible, dark gloom of a long night, the world has blazed with the Lord's light. We gaze on the confessors, famous for their good name and glorious for the praise of their virtue and faith. With joyful hearts we cling to them with holy kisses, embracing those we have desired for so long with a longing that could never be satisfied. The white cohort of Christ's soldiers stands here — men who broke the fierce and turbulent fury of the persecution by standing their ground, ready for the patience prison demands, armed for the endurance death demands. You resisted the world with strength. You gave God a glorious spectacle. You became an example for the brothers who would follow.

A religious voice spoke Christ, confessing that it had believed in him once and for all. Illustrious hands, accustomed only to divine works, refused to take part in sacrilegious sacrifices. Mouths sanctified by heavenly food, after receiving the body and blood of the Lord, spat out profane contagions and the remnants of idols. Your heads remained free of the impious, wicked veil that covered the captive heads of those who sacrificed. Your foreheads, marked pure with the sign of God, could not bear the devil's crown; they reserved themselves for the Lord's crown. How gladly mother Church welcomes you back from the battle! How blessed, how overjoyed she throws open her gates so that you may enter with gathered ranks, carrying trophies from the prostrate enemy!

With the triumphant men come women who, fighting the world, conquered even their own sex. Virgins come too, bearing the double glory of their warfare, and boys who surpassed their years through virtue. The rest of the multitude standing by follows your glory, treading in your footsteps with honors of praise that nearly join your own. The same sincerity of heart is in them, the same tenacity of faith. Rooted in the unshaken roots of heavenly precepts and strengthened by the traditions of the Gospel, they were not terrified by prescribed exiles, or destined torments, or the loss of their estates, or bodily punishments. Days were set aside to test their faith. But the one who remembers that he has renounced the world knows no day of the world; the one who hopes for eternity from God no longer calculates earthly time.

No one, my beloved brothers, no one should mutilate this glory, no one should weaken the uncorrupted firmness of those who stood firm with malicious detraction. When the day appointed for those who denied had passed, whoever had not professed within that day confessed himself a Christian. The first title of victory is to confess the Lord when he is seized by the hands of the Gentiles. The second step to glory is to be reserved for the Lord by a cautious withdrawal. The former is a public confession; the latter is a private one. The former conquers the judge of the world; the latter, content with God as his judge, guards a pure conscience with the integrity of his heart. There, fortitude is more prompt; here, solicitude is more secure. The former, with his hour approaching, was already found mature. The latter was perhaps delayed — he who abandoned his patrimony withdrew precisely because he was not going to deny; he certainly would have confessed if he had also been detained.

latin: PAX ecce, dilectissimi fratres, Ecclesiae reddita est et, quod difficile nuper incredulis ac perfidis impossibile videbatur, ope atque ultione divina securitas nostra reparata est. In laetitiam mentes redeunt, et, tempestate pressurae ac nube discussa, tranquillitas ac serenitas refulserunt. Dandae laudes Deo, et beneficia ejus ac munera cum gratiarum actione celebranda, quamvis agere gratias nostra vox nec in persecutione cessaverit. Neque enim tantum inimico licere potest ut non, qui Dominum toto corde et anima et virtute diligimus, benedictiones ejus et laudes semper et ubique cum gloria praedicemus. Exoptatus votis omnium dies venit, et, post longae noctis horribilem tetramque caliginem, Domini luce radiatus mundus eluxit. Confessores, praeconio boni nominis claros et virtutis ac fidei laudibus gloriosos, laetis conspectibus intuemur, sanctis osculis adhaerentes, desideratos diu inexplebili cupiditate complectimur. Adest militum Christi cohors candida, qui persecutionis urgentus ferociam turbulentam stabili congressione fregerunt, parati ad patientiam carceris, armati ad tolerantiam mortis. Repugnastis fortiter saeculo, spectaculum gloriosum praebuistis Deo, secuturis fratribus fuistis exemplo. Religiosa vox Christum locuta est, in quem se semel credidisse confessa est. Illustres manus, quae non nisi divinis operibus assueverant, sacrificiis sacrilegis restiterunt. Sanctificata ora coelestibus cibis, post corpus et sanguinem Domini, profana contagia et idolorum reliquias respuerunt. Ab impio sceleratoque velamine, quo illic velabantur sacrificantium capita captiva, caput vestrum liberum mansit. Frons cum signo Dei pura, diaboli coronam ferre non potuit, coronae se Domini reservavit. Quam vos laete sinu suo excipit mater Ecclesia de praelio revertentes! quam beata, quam gaudens portas suas aperit, ut adunatis agminibus intretis, de hoste prostrato trophaea referentes! Cum triumphantibus viris et feminae veniunt, quae cum saeculo dimicantes, sexum quoque vicerunt. Veniunt et geminata militiae suae gloria virgines, et pueri annos suos virtutibus transeuntes. Necnon et caetera stantium multitudo vestram gloriam sequitur, proximis et pene conjunctis laudis insignibus vestigia vestra comitatur. Eadem et in illis sinceritas cordis, eadem fidei tenacis integritas. Inconcussis praeceptorum coelestium radicibus nixos et evangelicis traditionibus roboratos, non praescripta exilia, non destinata tormenta, non rei familiaris damna, non corporis supplicia terruerunt. Explorandae fidei praefiniebantur dies. Sed qui saeculo renuntiasse se meminit, nullum saeculi diem novit; nec tempora terrena jam computat qui aeternitatem de Deo sperat. Nemo, fratres dilectissimi, nemo hanc gloriam mutilet, nemo incorruptam stantium firmitatem maligna obtrectatione debilitet. Cum dies negantibus praestitutus excessit, quisquis professus intra diem non est, Christianum se esse confessus est. Primus est victoriae titulus, gentilium manibus apprehensum Dominum confiteri: secundus ad gloriam gradus est cauta secessione subtractum Domino reservari. Illa publica, haec privata confessio est. Ille judicem saeculi vincit, hic contentus Deo suo judice conscientiam puram cordis integritate custodit. Illic, fortitudo promptior, hic sollicitudo securior. Ille appropinquante hora sua, jam maturus inventus est; hic fortasse dilatus est qui, patrimonio derelicto, idcirco secessit quia non erat negaturus: confiteretur utique si fuisset et ipse detentus.

excerpts.author: Barnabas
english: I must also speak to you about the temple. The wretched people were deceived; they pinned their hope on a building instead of on their God who made them, as if that structure were God's house. They dedicated it almost the way the nations dedicate their shrines. But listen to how the Lord does away with it: "Who measured heaven with a span or the earth with a handful? Was it not I?" says the Lord. "Heaven is my throne and the earth is the footstool of my feet. What kind of house will you build for me, or what place will serve as my rest?" (Isaiah 66:1-2). You can see that their hope is empty. He says again, "Look, the ones who tore down this temple will themselves rebuild it." That happened because they went to war, so enemies destroyed it; now even the enemies' servants will rebuild it. Once more, when the city, the temple, and the people of Israel were about to be handed over, the truth was revealed. Scripture says, "In the last days the Lord will hand over the sheep of the pasture, the fold, and their tower to destruction" (Micah 4:1-5), and it came to pass just as the Lord spoke. So let us ask whether a temple of God exists. It does—wherever God himself says to make and prepare it. As it is written, "When the week is completed, the temple of God will be built gloriously in the name of the Lord." I conclude, then, that a temple exists. Now learn how it will be built in the Lord's name. Before we believed in God, the dwelling of our heart was perishable and weak—truly a hand-built temple—because it was full of idolatry and served as a house of demons, since we did everything contrary to God. But it will be rebuilt in the Lord's name. Pay attention, then, that the Lord's temple may be built gloriously. Learn how: we received forgiveness of sins and put our hope in the name, so we became new, created again from the beginning. Therefore God truly dwells in us, in our inner dwelling. How? His word of faith, his call of promise, the wisdom of his righteous judgments, the commands of his teaching—he himself prophesying in us, he himself living in us—opens for us the door of the temple, which is the mouth, granting us repentance and leading us into the imperishable temple. The one who longs to be saved looks not at the human speaker but at the One who dwells and speaks within him, overcome with awe because he has never heard such words from a mouth before, nor has he ever desired to hear them until now. This is the spiritual temple being built for the Lord.

greek: Ἔτι δὲ καὶ περὶ τοῦ ναοῦ ἐρῶ ὑμῖν, ὡς πλανώμενοι οἱ ταλαίπωροι εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν ἤλπισαν, καὶ οὐκ ἐπὶ τὸν θεὸν αὐτῶν τὸν ποιήσαντα αὐτούς, ὡς ὄντα οἶκον θεοῦ. σχεδὸν γὰρ ὡς τὰ ἔθνη ἀφιέρωσαν αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ναῷ. ἀλλὰ πῶς λέγει κύριος καταργῶν αὐτόν, μάθετε: Τίς ἐμέτρησεν τὸν οὐρανὸν σπιθαμῇ ἢ τὴν γῆν δρακί; οὐκ ἐγώ; λέγει κύριος: Ὁ οὐρανός μοι θρόνος, ἡ δὲ γῆ ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν μου: ποῖον οἶκον οἰκοδομήσετέ μοι, ἢ τίς τόπος τῆς καταπαύσεώς μου; ἐγνώκατε, ὅτι ματαία ἡ ἐλπὶς αὐτῶν. πέρας γέ τοι πάλιν λέγει: Ἰδού, οἱ καθελόντες τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον αὐτοὶ αὐτὸν οἰκοδομήσουσιν. γίνεται, διὰ γὰρ τὸ πολεμεῖν αὐτοὺς καθῃρέθη ὑπὸ τῶν ἐχθρῶν: νῦν καὶ αὐτοὶ οἱ τῶν ἐχθρῶν ὑπηρέται ἀνοικοδομήσουσιν αὐτόν. πάλιν ὡς ἔμελλεν ἡ πόλις καὶ ὁ ναὸς καὶ ὁ λαὸς Ἰσραὴλ παραδίδοσθαι, ἐφανερώθη. λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφή: Καὶ ἔσται ἐπ’ ἐσχάτων τῶν ἡμερῶν, καὶ παραδώσει κύριος τὰ πρόβατα τῆς νομῆς καὶ τὴν μάνδραν καὶ τὸν πύργον αὐτῶν εἰς καταφθοράν. καὶ ἐγένετο καθ̓ ἃ ἐλάλησεν κύριος. ζητήσωμεν δέ, εἰ ἔστιν ναὸς θεοῦ. ἔστιν, ὅπου αὐτὸς λέγει ποιεῖν καὶ καταρτίζειν. γέγραπται γάρ: Καὶ ἔσται, τῆς ἑβδομάδος συντελουμένης οἰκοδομηθήσεται ναὸς θεοῦ ἐνδόξως ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι κυρίου. εὑρίσκω οὖν, ὅτι ἔστιν ναός. πῶς οὖν οἰκοδομηθήσεται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι κυρίου, μάθετε. πρὸ τοῦ ἡμᾶς πιστεῦσαι τῷ θεῷ ἦν ἡμῶν τὸ κατοικητήριον τῆς καρδίας φθαρτὸν καὶ ἀσθενές, ὡς ἀληθῶς οἰκοδομητὸς ναὸς διὰ χειρός, ὅτι ἦν πλήρης μὲν εἰδωλολατρείας καὶ ἦν οἶκος δαιμονίων διὰ τὸ ποιεῖν, ὅσα ἦν ἐναντία τῷ θεῷ, Οἰκοδομηθήσεται δὲ ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι κυρίου. προσέχετε δέ, ἵνα ὁ ναὸς τοῦ κυρίου ἐνδόξως οἰκοδομηθῇ. πῶς, μάθετε. λαβόντες τὴν ἄφεσιν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν καὶ ἐλπίσαντες ἐπὶ τὸ ὄνομα ἐγενόμεθα καινοί, πάλιν ἐξ ἀρχῆς κτιζόμενοι: διὸ ἐν τῷ κατοικητηρίῳ ἡμῶν ἀληθῶς ὁ θεὸς κατοικεῖ ἐν ἡμῖν. πῶς; ὁ λόγος αὐτοῦ τῆς πίστεως, ἡ κλῆσις αὐτοῦ τῆς ἐπαγγελίας, ἡ σοφία τῶν δικαιωμάτων, αἱ ἐντολαὶ τῆς διδαχῆς, αὐτὸς ἐν ἡμῖν προφητεύων, αὐτὸς ἐν ἡμῖν κατοικῶν, τοὺς τῷ θανάτῳ δεδουλωμένους ἀνοίγων ἡμῖν τὴν θύραν τοῦ ναοῦ, ὅ ἐστιν στόμα, μετάνοιαν διδοὺς ἡμῖν, εἰσάγει εἰς τὸν ἄφθαρτον ναόν. ὁ γὰρ ποθῶν σωθῆναι βλέπει οὐκ εἰς τὸν ἄνθρωπον, ἀλλ’ εἰς τὸν ἐν αὐτῷ κατοικοῦντα καὶ λαλοῦντα, ἐπ’ αὐτῷ ἐκπλησσόμενος, ἐπὶ τῷ μηδέποτε μήτε τοῦ λέγοντος τὰ ῥήματα ἀκηκοέναι ἐκ τοῦ στόματος μήτε αὐτός ποτε ἐπιτεθυμηκέναι ἀκούειν. τοῦτό ἐστιν πνευματικὸς ναὸς οἰκοδομούμενος τῷ κυρίῳ.

excerpts.citation: Ignatius of Antioch — To the Ephesians 9
excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: I have heard that some people passed your way from there, carrying bad teaching. You would not let them sow it among you. You stopped your ears so as not to take in what they were sowing. For you are stones of the Father's temple, made ready for the building of God the Father (1 Corinthians 3:9). You are lifted to the heights by the crane of Jesus Christ, which is the cross, and you use the Holy Spirit as your rope. Your faith is the winch that raises you, and love is the road that climbs to God.

So you are all companions in one procession: God-bearers and temple-bearers, Christ-bearers, bearers of holy things, dressed at every point in the commandments of Jesus Christ. Rejoicing in all this, I have been counted worthy to talk with you through what I write and to share your joy, because in this human life you love nothing but God alone.

greek: Ἔγνων δὲ παροδεύσαντάς τινας ἐκεῖθεν, ἔχοντας κακὴν διδαχήν: οὓς οὐκ εἰάσατε σπεῖραι εἰς ὑμᾶς, βύσαντες τὰ ὦτα, εἰς τὸ μὴ παραδέξασθαι τὰ σπειρόμενα ὑπ’ αὐτῶν, ὡς ὄντες λίθοι ναοῦ πατρός, ἡτοιμασμένοι εἰς οἰκοδομὴν θεοῦ πατρός, ἀναφερόμενοι εἰς τὰ ὕψη διὰ τῆς μηχανῆς Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὅς ἐστιν σταυρός, σχοινίῳ χρώμενοι τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ: ἡ δὲ πίστις ὑμῶν ἀναγωγεὺς ὑμῶν, ἡ δὲ ἀγάπη ὁδὸς ἡ ἀναφέρουσα εἰς θεόν.

ἐστὲ οὖν καὶ σύνοδοι πάντες, θεοφόροι καὶ ναοφόροι, χριστοφόροι, ἁγιοφόροι, κατὰ πάντα κεκοσμημένοι ἐντολαῖς Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ: οἶς καὶ ἀγαλλιώμενος ἠξιώθην δἰ ὦν γράφω προσομιλῆσαι ὑμῖν καὶ συγχαρῆναι, ὅτι κατ’ ἀνθρώπων βίον οὐδὲν ἀγαπᾶτε εἰ μὴ μόνον τὸν θεόν.

english: He says, "Take sorrow away from yourself, for it is also a sister of double-mindedness and bitterness." I ask, "Lord, how can it be a sister of these? It seems to me that bitterness, double-mindedness, and sorrow are each completely different things." He answers, "You are a foolish person who fails to understand. Sorrow is the most wicked and most terrible of all spirits toward God's servants. It corrupts a person in every way, drives out the Holy Spirit, and yet also saves." I reply, "Lord, I am foolish and do not understand these parables. How can it both drive out and save? I cannot grasp it."

He says, "Listen. People who have never investigated the truth nor sought God, but merely believed, and who entangle themselves in business, wealth, pagan friendships, and the many other affairs of this age --- all who cling to these things cannot understand the parables of God. Their own actions darken them, corrupt them, and harden them. Good vineyards, when neglected, become hardened with thorns and weeds of every kind. In the same way, people who have believed yet fall into these many affairs I just mentioned wander from their own minds. They understand nothing at all about righteousness. Even when they hear about God and truth, their minds remain occupied with their own pursuits, so they understand nothing."

"But those who fear God, investigate Him and the truth, and set their hearts toward the Lord --- they quickly understand and grasp everything said to them, because they carry the fear of the Lord within themselves. Where the Lord dwells, great understanding also dwells. So cling to the Lord, and you will understand and grasp all things."

"Now listen, foolish one, to how sorrow drives out the Holy Spirit and yet also saves. When a double-minded person undertakes some action and fails because of his double-mindedness, that sorrow enters him, grieves the Holy Spirit, and drives it out. Then again, when bitterness fastens onto a person over some matter and he becomes deeply bitter, sorrow once more enters the heart of that bitter person. He grieves over the evil he did and repents. This sorrow appears to bring salvation, because the evildoer repented. Yet both actions grieve the Spirit: double-mindedness, because it failed to accomplish its aim; bitterness, because it did evil. Both double-mindedness and bitterness are grievous to the Holy Spirit."

"Therefore, take sorrow away from yourself. Do not grieve the Holy Spirit who lives in you, or He may complain to God and leave you. The Spirit of God given to this flesh cannot endure sorrow or distress. So put on cheerfulness, which always finds grace with God and is acceptable to Him, and live in it. Every cheerful person does good works, thinks good thoughts, and despises sorrow. But a sorrowful person always does evil. First, he grieves the Holy Spirit who was given to make him cheerful. Second, by grieving the Spirit, he commits lawlessness, neither interceding nor confessing to the Lord. The intercession of a sorrowful person never has the power to ascend to God's altar."

"Why, I ask, does the sorrowful person's intercession not ascend to the altar? Because, he says, sorrow sits entrenched in his heart. Sorrow mixed with intercession prevents the prayer from rising pure to the altar. Just as vinegar and wine mixed together lose their proper flavor, so sorrow mixed with the Holy Spirit destroys true intercession. Cleanse yourself from this wicked sorrow, and you will live for God. All who cast off sorrow and clothe themselves in complete cheerfulness will live for God."

greek: Ἆρον ἀπὸ σεαυτοῦ, φησί, τὴν λύπην: καὶ γὰρ αὕτη ἀδελφή ἐστι τῆς διψυχίας καὶ τῆς ὀξυχολίας. Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, ἀδελφή ἐστι τούτων; ἄλλο γάρ μοι δοκεῖ εἶναι ὀξυχολία καὶ ἄλλο διψυχία καὶ ἄλλο λύπη. Ἀσύνετος εἶ ἄνθρωπε, φησί, καὶ οὐ νοεῖς, ὅτι ἡ λύπη πάντων τῶν πνευμάτων πονηροτέρα ἐστὶ καὶ δεινοτάτη τοῖς δούλοις τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ παρὰ πάντα τὰ πνεύματα καταφθείρει τὸν ἄνθρωπον καὶ ἐκτρίβει τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον καὶ πάλιν σώζει; Ἐγώ, φημί, κύριε, ἀσύνετός εἰμι καὶ οὐ συνίω τὰς παραβολὰς ταύτας. πῶς γὰρ δύναται ἐκτρίβειν καὶ πάλιν σώζειν, οὐ νοῶ. Ἄκουε, φησίν: οἱ μηδέποτε ἐρευνήσαντες περὶ τῆς ἀληθείας μηδὲ ἐπιζητήσαντες περὶ τῆς θεότητος, πιστεύσαντες δὲ μόνον, ἐμπεφυρμένοι δὲ πραγματείαις καὶ πλούτῳ καὶ φιλίαις ἐθνικαῖς καὶ ἄλλαις πολλαῖς πραγματείαις τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου: ὅσοι οὖν τούτοις πρόσκεινται, οὐ νοοῦσι τὰς παραβολὰς τῆς θεότητος: ἐπισκοτοῦνται γὰρ ὑπὸ τούτων τῶν πράξεων καὶ καταφθείρονται καὶ γίνονται κεχερσωμένοι. καθὼς οἱ ἀμπελῶνες οἱ καλοί, ὅταν ἀμελείας τύχωσι, χερσοῦνται ἀπὸ τῶν ἀκανθῶν καὶ βοτανῶν ποικίλων, οὕτως οἱ ἄνθρωποι οἱ πιστεύσαντες καὶ εἰς ταύτας τὰς πράξεις τὰς πολλὰς ἐμπίπτοντες τὰς προειρημένας, ἀποπλανῶνται ἀπὸ τῆς διανοίας αὐτῶν, καὶ οὐδὲν ὅλως νοοῦσι περὶ δικαιοσύνης, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὅταν ἀκούσωσι περὶ θεότητος καὶ ἀληθείας, ὁ νοῦς αὐτῶν περὶ τὴν πρᾶξιν αὐτῶν καταγίνεται, καὶ οὐδὲν ὅλως νοοῦσιν. οἱ δὲ φόβον ἔχοντες θεοῦ καὶ ἐρευνῶντες περὶ θεότητος καὶ ἀληθείας καὶ τὴν καρδίαν ἔχοντες πρὸς τὸν κύριον, πάντα τὰ λεγόμενα αὐτοῖς τάχιον νοοῦσι καὶ συνίουσιν, ὅτι ἔχουσι τὸν φόβον τοῦ κυρίου ἐν ἑαυτοῖς: ὅπου γὰρ ὁ κύριος κατοικεῖ, ἐκεῖ καὶ σύνεσις πολλή. κολλήθητι οὖν τῷ κυρίῳ, καὶ πάντα συνήσεις καὶ νοήσεις. Ἄκουε οὖν, φησίν, ἀνόητε, πῶς ἡ λύπη ἐκτρίβει τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον καὶ πάλιν σώζει: ὅταν ὁ δίψυχος ἐπιβάληται πρᾶξίν τινα καὶ ταύτης ἀποτύχῃ διὰ τὴν διψυχίαν αὐτοῦ, ἡ λύπη αὕτη εἰσπορεύεται εἰς τὸν ἄνθρωπον καὶ λυπεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον καὶ ἐκτρίβει αὐτό. εἶτα πάλιν ἡ ὀξυχολία ὅταν κολληθῇ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ περὶ πράγματός τινος, καὶ λίαν πικρανθῇ, πάλιν ἡ λύπη εἰσπορεύεται εἰς τὴν καρδίαν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τοῦ ὀξυχολήσαντος, καὶ λυπεῖται ἐπὶ τῇ πράξει αὐτοῦ ᾗ ἔπραξε καὶ μετανοεῖ, ὅτι πονηρὸν εἰργάσατο. αὕτη οὖν ἡ λύπη δοκεῖ σωτηρίαν ἔχειν, ὅτι τὸ πονηρὸν πράξας μετενόησεν. ἀμφότεραι οὖν αἱ πράξεις λυποῦσι τὸ πνεῦμα: ἡ μὲν διψυχία, ὅτι οὐκ ἐπέτυχε τῆς πράξεως αὐτῆς, ἡ δὲ ὀξυχολία λυπεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα, ὅτι ἔπραξε τὸ πονηρόν. ἀμφότερα οὖν λυπηρά ἐστι τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ, ἡ διψυχία καὶ ἡ ὀξυχολία. ἆρον οὖν ἀπὸ σεαυτοῦ τὴν λύπην καὶ μὴ θλῖβε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τὸ ἐν σοὶ κατοικοῦν, μήποτε ἐντεύξηται τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἀποστῇ ἀπὸ σοῦ. τὸ γὰρ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ τὸ δοθὲν εἰς τὴν σάρκα ταύτην λύπην οὐχ ὑποφέρει οὐδὲ στενοχωρίαν. Ἔνδυσαι οὖν τὴν ἱλαρότητα, τὴν πάντοτε ἔχουσαν χάριν παρὰ τῷ θεῷ καὶ εὐπρόσδεκτον οὖσαν αὐτῷ, καὶ ἐντρύφα ἐν αὐτῇ. πᾶς γὰρ ἱλαρὸς ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὰ ἐργάζεται καὶ ἀγαθὰ φρονεῖ καὶ καταφρονεῖ τῆς λύπης. ὁ δὲ λυπηρὸς ἀνὴρ πάντοτε πονηρεύεται: πρῶτον μὲν πονηρεύεται, ὅτι λυπεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τὸ δοθὲν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἱλαρόν: δεύτερον δὲ λυπῶν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἀνομίαν ἐργάζεται, μὴ ἐντυγχάνων μηδὲ ἐξομολογούμενος τῷ κυρίῳ. Πάντοτε γὰρ λυπηροῦ ἀνδρὸς ἡ ἔντευξις οὐκ ἔχει δύναμιν τοῦ ἀναβῆναι ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τοῦ θεοῦ. Διατί, φημί, οὐκ ἀναβαίνει ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον ἡ ἔντευξις τοῦ λυπουμένου; Ὅτι, φησίν, ἡ λύπη ἐγκάθηται εἰς τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ. μεμιγμένη οὖν ἡ λύπη μετὰ τῆς ἐντεύξεως οὐκ ἀφίησι τὴν ἔντευξιν ἀναβῆναι καθαρὰν ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον. ὥσπερ γὰρ ὄξος καὶ οἶνος μεμιγμένα ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ τὴν αὐτὴν ἡδονὴν οὐκ ἔχουσιν, οὕτω καὶ ἡ λύπη μεμιγμένη μετὰ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος τὴν αὐτὴν ἔντευξιν οὐκ ἔχει. καθάρισον οὖν σεαυτὸν ἀπὸ τῆς λύπης τῆς πονηρᾶς ταύτης, καὶ ζήσῃ τῷ θεῷ: καὶ πάντες ζήσονται τῷ θεῷ, ὅσοι ἂν ἀποβάλωσιν ἀφ̓ ἑαυτῶν τὴν λύπην καὶ ἐνδύσωνται πᾶσαν ἱλαρότητα.

excerpts.author: Hermas
english:
The Spirit showed me people sitting on a bench and another man seated on a chair. He asked me, "Do you see those sitting on the bench?" I answered, "Yes, Lord." He said, "These are faithful, but the one on the chair is a false prophet who ruins the minds of God's slaves — he ruins the double-minded, not the faithful. Those double-minded people come to him like a seer and ask what will happen to them. The false prophet has no divine spiritual power in himself, yet he answers according to their questions and their wicked desires, filling their souls just as they wish. Because he is empty, he gives empty answers; whatever he is asked, he responds to the emptiness in the questioner. Sometimes he even speaks true words, for the devil fills him with his own spirit, hoping to break some of the righteous. But those who are strong in the Lord's faith, clothed with truth, do not cling to such spirits; they stay away from them. However, the double-minded who often repent go to practice divination like the nations, and they bring greater sin upon themselves by idolatry. Anyone who consults a false prophet about some action is an idolater, empty of truth, and foolish.

Every spirit given by God does not need to be asked questions; it has the power of divinity and speaks everything from itself, because it comes from above, from the power of the Holy Spirit. But the spirit that must be asked and speaks according to human desires is earthly and slight, having no power — it does not speak at all unless someone asks it.

I asked, "Lord, how will a person know who is a prophet and who is a false prophet?" He replied, "Listen about both prophets. As I tell you, so you will test the prophet and the false prophet. Test the man who has the divine spirit by his life. First, the one who has the spirit from above is gentle, quiet, and humble; he avoids all wickedness and the empty desires of this world. He makes himself more needy than everyone else. He does not answer anyone who questions him, nor does he speak on his own. The Holy Spirit does not speak just because a person wants to speak; it speaks only when God wants it to speak. When such a man enters a gathering of righteous men who have faith in the divine spirit and they pray to God, the angel of the prophetic spirit who is with him fills the man. Filled with the Holy Spirit, he speaks to the crowd as the Lord wills. Thus the spirit of divinity becomes manifest. That is how great the power of the spirit of the Lord's divinity is.

Now listen about the earthly, empty spirit that has no power and is foolish. First, the man who thinks he has a spirit exalts himself and wants the chief seat. He is instantly haughty, shameless, and talkative. He lives in many luxuries and many other deceptions, and he accepts payment for his prophecies; if he receives nothing, he does not prophesy. Can a divine spirit accept payment and prophesy? It is impossible for a prophet of God to do this; the spirit of such prophets is earthly. He never approaches a gathering of righteous men; he avoids them. Instead, he clings to the double-minded and empty. He prophesies to them in a corner and deceives them, speaking everything emptily, because he answers empty things. An empty vessel placed among empty vessels does not break; they harmonize with each other. But when he enters a gathering full of righteous men who have the spirit of divinity and they pray, that man becomes empty. The earthly spirit flees from him in fear, the man goes mute, and he is completely crushed, unable to say anything. If you store wine or oil in a storeroom and put an empty jar among them, then later empty the storeroom, you will find that jar still empty. So also the false prophets, when they come among the spirits of the righteous, are found exactly as they were when they came.

You now have the life of both prophets. Test the man who claims to be spirit-bearing by his works and his life. But you — believe the spirit that comes from God and has power. Do not believe anything the earthly, empty spirit says, because there is no power in it; it comes from the devil.

Listen to the parable I am about to tell you. Take a stone and throw it into the sky — see if you can touch it. Or take a siphon of water and siphon it into the sky — see if you can pierce the sky. "How, Lord," I said, "can these things happen? Both are impossible." He answered, "As these things are impossible, so also the earthly spirits are impossible and inactive. Take instead the power that comes from above. Hail is a tiny grain, yet when it falls on a man's head, how much pain it causes. Or take a drop that falls from a jar to the ground and pierces the stone. Do you see? The things from above, though smallest, falling on the earth, have great power. So also the divine spirit coming from above is powerful. Believe in this spirit, but keep away from the other."

greek: Ἔδειξέ μοι ἐπὶ συμψελλίου καθημένους ἀνθρώπους καὶ ἕτερον ἄνθρωπον καθήμενον ἐπὶ καθέδραν, καὶ λέγει μοι: Βλέπεις τοὺς ἐπὶ τοῦ συμψελλίου καθημένους; Βλέπω, φημί, κύριε. Οὗτοι, φησί, πιστοί εἰσι, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τὴν καθέδραν ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστίν, ὃς ἀπόλλυσι τὴν διάνοιαν τῶν δούλων τοῦ θεοῦ: τῶν διψύχων δὲ ἀπόλλυσιν, οὐ τῶν πιστῶν. οὗτοι οὖν οἱ δίψυχοι ὡς ἐπὶ μάντιν ἔρχονται καὶ ἐπερωτῶσιν αὐτόν, τί ἄρα ἔσται αὐτοῖς: κἀκεῖνος ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης, μηδεμίαν ἔχων ἐν ἑαυτῷ δύναμιν πνεύματος θείου, λαλεῖ μετ’ αὐτῶν κατὰ τὰ ἐπερωτήματα αὐτῶν καὶ κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς πονηρίας αὐτῶν καὶ πληροῖ τὰς ψυχὰς αὐτῶν, καθὼς αὐτοὶ βούλονται. αὐτὸς γὰρ κενὸς ὢν κενὰ καὶ ἀποκρίνεται κενοῖς: ὃ γὰρ ἐὰν ἐπερωτηθῇ, πρὸς τὸ κένωμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀποκρίνεται. τινὰ δὲ καὶ ῥήματα ἀληθῆ λαλεῖ: ὁ γὰρ διάβολος πληροῖ αὐτὸν τῷ αὐτοῦ πνεύματι, εἴ τινα δυνήσεται ῥῆξαι τῶν δικαίων. ὅσοι οὖν ἰσχυροί εἰσιν ἐν τῇ πίστει τοῦ κυρίου, ἐνδεδυμένοι τὴν ἀλήθειαν, τοῖς τοιούτοις πνεύμασιν οὐ κολλῶνται, ἀλλ’ ἀπέχονται ἀπ’ αὐτῶν: ὅσοι δὲ δίψυχοί εἰσι καὶ πυκνῶς μετανοοῦσι, μαντεύονται ὡς καὶ τὰ ἔθνη καὶ ἑαυτοῖς μείζονα ἁμαρτίαν ἐπιφέρουσιν εἰδωλολατροῦντες: ὁ γὰρ ἐπερωτῶν ψευδοπροφήτην περὶ πράξεώς τινος εἰδωλολάτρης ἐστὶ καὶ κενὸς ἀπὸ τῆς ἀληθείας καὶ ἄφρων. πᾶν γὰρ πνεῦμα ἀπὸ θεοῦ δοθὲν οὐκ ἐπερωτᾶται, ἀλλὰ ἔχον τὴν δύναμιν τῆς θεότητος ἀφ̓ ἑαυτοῦ λαλεῖ πάντα, ὅτι ἄνωθέν ἐστιν ἀπὸ τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ θείου πνεύματος. τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα τὸ ἐπερωτώμενον καὶ λαλοῦν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐπίγειόν ἐστι καὶ ἐλαφρόν, δύναμιν μὴ ἔχον: καὶ ὅλως οὐ λαλεῖ, ἐὰν μὴ ἐπερωτηθῇ. Πῶς οὖν, φημί, κύριε, ἄνθρωπος γνώσεται, τίς αὐτῶν προφήτης καὶ τίς ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστίν; Ἄκουε, φησί, περὶ ἀμφοτέρων τῶν προφητῶν: καὶ ὥς σοι μέλλω λέγειν, οὕτω δοκιμάσεις τὸν προφήτην καὶ τὸν ψευδοπροφήτην. ἀπὸ τῆς ζωῆς δοκίμαζε τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν ἔχοντα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἄνωθεν πραΰς ἐστι καὶ ἡσύχιος και ταπεινόφρων καὶ ἀπεχόμενος ἀπὸ πάσης πονηρίας καὶ ἐπιθυμίας ματαίας τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου καὶ ἑαυτὸν ἐνδεέστερον ποιεῖ πάντων τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ οὐδενὶ οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνεται ἐπερωτώμενος, οὐδὲ καταμόνας λαλεῖ, οὐδὲ ὅταν θέλῃ ἄνθρωπος λαλεῖν, λαλεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, ἀλλὰ τότε λαλεῖ, ὅταν θελήσῃ αὐτὸν ὁ θεὸς λαλῆσαι. ὅταν οὖν ἔλθῃ ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων τῶν ἐχόντων πίστιν θείου πνεύματος καὶ ἔντευξις γένηται πρὸς τὸν θεὸν τῆς συναγωγῆς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐκείνων, τότε ὁ ἄγγελος τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος ὁ κείμενος πρὸς αὐτὸν πληροῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, καὶ πληρωθεὶς ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ λαλεῖ εἰς τὸ πλῆθος, καθὼς ὁ κύριος βούλεται. οὕτως οὖν φανερὸν ἔσται τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς θεότητος. ὅση οὖν περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς θεότητος τοῦ κυρίου ἡ δύναμις αὕτη. ἄκουε νῦν, φησί, περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐπιγείου καὶ κενοῦ καὶ δύναμιν μὴ ἔχοντος, ἀλλὰ ὄντος μωροῦ. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὁ δοκῶν πνεῦμα ἔχειν ὑψοῖ ἑαυτὸν καὶ θέλει πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἔχειν, καὶ εὐθὺς ἰταμός ἐστι καὶ ἀναιδὴς καὶ πολύλαλος καὶ ἐν τρυφαῖς πολλαῖς ἀναστρεφόμενος καὶ ἐν ἑτέραις πολλαῖς ἀπάταις καὶ μισθοὺς λαμβάνων τῆς προφητείας αὐτοῦ: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ λάβῃ, οὐ προφητεύει. δύναται οὖν πνεῦμα θεῖον μισθοὺς λαμβάνειν καὶ προφητεύειν; οὐκ ἐνδέχεται τοῦτο ποιεῖν θεοῦ προφήτην, ἀλλὰ τῶν τοιούτων προφητῶν ἐπίγειόν ἐστι τὸ πνεῦμα. εἶτα ὅλως εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων οὐκ ἐγγίζει, ἀλλ’ ἀποφεύγει αὐτούς: κολλᾶται δὲ τοῖς διψύχοις καὶ κενοῖς καὶ κατὰ γωνίαν αὐτοῖς προφητεύει καὶ ἀπατᾷ αὐτοὺς λαλῶν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας αὐτῶν πάντα κενῶς: κενοῖς γὰρ καὶ ἀποκρίνεται: τὸ γὰρ κενὸν σκεῦος μετὰ τῶν κενῶν συντιθέμενον οὐ θραύεται, ἀλλὰ συμφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις. ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ εἰς συναγωγὴν πλήρη ἀνδρῶν δικαίων ἐχόντων πνεῦμα θεότητος καὶ ἔντευξις ἀπ’ αὐτῶν γένηται, κενοῦται ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος, καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἐπίγειον ἀπὸ τοῦ φόβου φεύγει ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ κωφοῦται ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος καὶ ὅλως συνθραύεται, μηδὲν δυνάμενος λαλῆσαι. ἐὰν γὰρ εἰς ἀποθήκην στιβάσῃς οἶνον ἢ ἔλαιον καὶ ἐν αὐτοῖς θῇς κεράμιον κενόν, καὶ πάλιν ἀποστιβάσαι θελήσῃς τὴν ἀποθήκην, τὸ κεράμιον ἐκεῖνο, ὃ ἔθηκας κενόν, κενὸν καὶ εὑρήσεις: οὕτω καὶ οἱ προφῆται οἱ κενοὶ ὅταν ἔλθωσιν εἰς πνεύματα δικαίων, ὁποῖοι ἦλθον, τοιοῦτοι καὶ εὑρίσκονται. ἔχεις ἀμφοτέρων τῶν προφητῶν τὴν ζωήν. δοκίμαζε οὖν ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων καὶ τῆς ζωῆς τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν λέγοντα ἑαυτὸν πνευματοφόρον εἶναι. σὺ δὲ πίστευε τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἐρχομένῳ ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἔχοντι δύναμιν: τῷ δὲ πνεύματι τῷ ἐπιγείῳ καὶ κενῷ μηδὲν πίστευε, ὅτι ἐν αὐτῷ δύναμις οὐκ ἔστιν: ἀπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου γὰρ ἔρχεται. ἄκουσον οὖν τὴν παραβολήν, ἣν μέλλω σοι λέγειν: λάβε λίθον καὶ βάλε εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, ἴδε, εἰ δύνασαι ἅψασθαι αὐτοῦ: ἢ πάλιν λάβε σίφωνα ὕδατος καὶ σιφώνισον εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, ἴδε, εἰ δύνασαι τρυπῆσαι τὸν οὐρανόν. Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, δύναται ταῦτα γενέσθαι; ἀδύνατα γὰρ ἀμφότερα ταῦτα εἴρηκας. Ὡς ταῦτα οὖν, φησίν, ἀδύνατά ἐστιν, οὕτω καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἐπίγεια ἀδύνατά ἐστι καὶ ἀδρανῆ. λάβε οὖν τὴν δύναμιν τὴν ἄνωθεν ἐρχομένην: ἡ χάλαζα ἐλάχιστόν ἐστι κοκκάριον, καὶ ὅταν ἐπιπέσῃ ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν ἀνθρώπου, πῶς πόνον παρέχει; ἢ πάλιν λάβε σταγόνα, ἣ ἀπὸ τοῦ κεράμου πίπτει χαμαὶ καὶ τρυπᾷ τὸν λίθον. βλέπεις οὖν, ὅτι τὰ ἄνωθεν ἐλάχιστα πίπτοντα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν μεγάλην δύναμιν ἔχει: οὕτω καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον ἄνωθεν ἐρχόμενον δυνατόν ἐστι: τούτῳ οὖν τῷ πνεύματι πίστευε, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ ἑτέρου ἀπέχου.

excerpts.author: Hermas
english: Be patient and wise, and you will master every evil deed and carry out all righteousness. If you are patient, the Holy Spirit who lives in you will remain pure, not crowded out by any evil spirit. Instead, He will dwell in a spacious place, rejoicing and glad with the vessel He inhabits, and He will serve God with great cheerfulness, possessing His own readiness within Himself. But if bitterness draws near, the Holy Spirit—who is tender—is immediately distressed, because He no longer has a pure place. He seeks to leave, choked by the evil spirit and defiled by bitterness, unable to serve the Lord as He desires. The Lord dwells in patience, but the devil dwells in bitterness; therefore, both spirits dwelling in the same person is unprofitable and evil. If you take a tiny bit of wormwood and pour it into a jar of honey, does it not ruin the whole batch? That small amount of wormwood destroys the honey's sweetness and makes it useless to its master. But if no wormwood is added, the honey stays sweet and useful. You see that patience is sweeter than honey and useful to the Lord, and He makes His home in it. Bitterness, by contrast, is bitter and useless. If bitterness mixes with patience, patience is defiled and its prayer is no longer useful to God. I want, Lord, to know how bitterness works so I can guard against it. If you and your household do not guard against it, you will lose all hope. But guard against it, for I am with you. All who repent with their whole heart will also guard against it, because I will be with them and preserve them, since they have all been justified by the most glorious angel. Listen now to how evil bitterness works: it destroys my servants and leads them astray from righteousness. It does not lead astray those who are full of faith, nor can it gain a foothold in them, because my power is with them; it leads astray only those who are empty and double-minded. When it sees such people standing firm, it insinuates itself into their hearts. Over nothing at all, a man or woman becomes bitter about worldly concerns—food, some trifle, a friend, giving or receiving, or similar foolish things. All these are foolish, empty, senseless, and unprofitable for God's servants. Patience, on the other hand, is great, strong, powerful, steadfast, and thrives in spacious breadth. It is cheerful, rejoicing, carefree, glorifying the Lord at all times, holding nothing bitter within itself, remaining gentle and quiet always. This patience dwells with those who have whole faith. Bitterness is first foolish, frivolous, and senseless. From senselessness comes bitterness, from bitterness comes anger, from anger comes wrath, from wrath comes resentment. This resentment, composed of so many evils, becomes a great and incurable sin. When these spirits inhabit one vessel along with the Holy Spirit, the vessel cannot contain them; it overflows. The tender Spirit, unaccustomed to dwelling with an evil spirit or harshness, departs from that person and seeks a home with gentleness and quietness. Once the Spirit leaves, that person is emptied of the righteous Spirit, filled instead with evil spirits, and becomes unstable in every action—tossed here and there by those spirits, completely blinded to good understanding. This is what happens to all who are bitter. So keep away from bitterness, the most evil spirit. Put on patience, resist bitterness and harshness, and you will be found with the dignity the Lord loves. Be careful not to forget this command: if you master it, you will also be able to keep the other commands I am about to give you. Be strong in them and be empowered, and let all be empowered who wish to walk in them.

greek: Μακρόθυμος, φησί, γίνου καὶ συνετός, καὶ πάντων τῶν πονηρῶν ἔργων κατακυριεύσεις καὶ ἐργάσῃ πᾶσαν δικαιοσύνην. ἐὰν γὰρ μακρόθυμος ἔσῃ, τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τὸ κατοικοῦν ἐν σοὶ καθαρὸν ἔσται, μὴ ἐπισκοτούμενον ὑπὸ ἑτέρου πονηροῦ πνεύματος, ἀλλ’ ἐν εὐρυχώρῳ κατοικοῦν ἀγαλλιάσεται καὶ εὐφρανθήσεται μετὰ τοῦ σκεύους, ἐν ᾧ κατοικεῖ, καὶ λειτουργήσει τῷ θεῷ ἐν ἱλαρότητι πολλῇ, ἔχον τὴν εὐθηνίαν ἐν ἑαυτῷ. ἐὰν δὲ ὀξυχολία τις προσέλθῃ, εὐθὺς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, τρυφερὸν ὄν, στενοχωρεῖται, μὴ ἔχον τὸν τόπον καθαρόν, καὶ ζητεῖ ἀποστῆναι ἐκ τοῦ τόπου: πνίγεται γὰρ ὑπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ πνεύματος, μὴ ἔχον τόπον λειτουργῆσαι τῷ κυρίῳ, καθὼς βούλεται, μιαινόμενον ὑπὸ τῆς ὀξυχολίας. ἐν γὰρ τῇ μακροθυμίᾳ ὁ κύριος κατοικεῖ, ἐν δὲ τῇ ὀξυχολίᾳ ὁ διάβολος. ἀμφότερα οὖν τὰ πνεύματα ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ κατοικοῦντα, ἀσύμφορόν ἐστιν καὶ πονηρὸν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ, ἐν ᾧ κατοικοῦσιν. ἐὰν γὰρ λάβῃς ἀψινθίου μικρὸν λίαν καὶ εἰς κεράμιον μέλιτος ἐπιχέῃς, οὐχὶ ὅλον τὸ μέλι ἀφανίζεται, καὶ τοσοῦτον μέλι ὑπὸ τοῦ ἐλαχίστου ἀψινθίου ἀπόλλυται καὶ ἀπόλλυσι τὴν γλυκύτητα τοῦ μέλιτος, καὶ οὐκέτι τὴν αὐτὴν χάριν ἔχει παρὰ τῷ δεσπότῃ, ὅτι ἐπικράνθη καὶ τὴν χρῆσιν αὐτοῦ ἀπώλεσεν; ἐὰν δὲ εἰς τὸ μέλι μὴ βληθῇ τὸ ἀψίνθιον, γλυκὺ εὑρίσκεται τὸ μέλι καὶ εὔχρηστον γίνεται τῷ δεσπότῃ αὐτοῦ. βλέπεις ὅτι ἡ μακροθυμία γλυκυτάτη ἐστὶν ὑπὲρ τὸ μέλι καὶ εὔχρηστός ἐστι τῷ κυρίῳ, καὶ ἐν αὐτῇ κατοικεῖ. ἡ δὲ ὀξυχολία πικρὰ καὶ ἄχρηστός ἐστιν. ἐὰν οὖν μιγῇ ἡ ὀξυχολία τῇ μακροθυμίᾳ, μιαίνεται ἡ μακροθυμία καὶ οὐκέτι εὔχρηστός ἐστι τῷ θεῷ ἡ ἔντευξις αὐτῆς. Ἤθελον, φημί, κύριε, γνῶναι τὴν ἐνέργειαν τῆς ὀξυχολίας, ἵνα φυλάξωμαι ἀπ’ αὐτῆς. Καὶ μήν, φησίν, ἐὰν μὴ φυλάξῃ ἀπ’ αὐτῆς σὺ καὶ ὁ οἶκός σου, ἀπώλεσάς σου τὴν πᾶσαν ἐλπίδα. ἀλλὰ φύλαξαι ἀπ’ αὐτῆς: ἐγὼ γὰρ μετὰ σοῦ εἰμί. καὶ πάντες δὲ ἀφέξονται ἀπ’ αὐτῆς, ὅσοι ἂν μετανοήσωσιν ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν: μετ’ αὐτῶν γὰρ ἔσομαι καὶ συντηρήσω αὐτούς: ἐδικαιώθησαν γὰρ πάντες ὑπὸ τοῦ σεμνοτάτου ἀγγέλου. Ἄκουε νῦν, φησί, τὴν ἐνέργειαν τῆς ὀξυχολίας, πῶς πονηρά ἐστι, καὶ πῶς τοὺς δούλους μοῦ καταστρέφει τῇ ἑαυτῆς ἐνεργείᾳ καὶ πῶς ἀποπλανᾷ αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ τῆς δικαιοσύνης. οὐκ ἀποπλανᾷ δὲ τοὺς πλήρεις ὄντας ἐν τῇ πίστει οὐδὲ ἐνεργῆσαι δύναται εἰς αὐτούς, ὅτι ἡ δύναμις μου μετ’ αὐτῶν ἐστιν: ἀποπλανᾷ δὲ τοὺς ἀποκένους καὶ διψύχους ὄντας. ὅταν δὲ ἴδῃ τοὺς τοιούτους ἀνθρώπους εὐσταθοῦντας, παρεμβάλλει ἑαυτὴν εἰς τὴν καρδίαν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκείνου, καὶ ἐκ τοῦ μηδενὸς ὁ ἀνὴρ ἢ ἡ γυνὴ ἐν πικρίᾳ γίνεται ἕνεκεν βιωτικῶν πραγμάτων ἢ περὶ ἐδεσμάτων ἢ μικρολογίας τινὸς ἢ περὶ φίλου τινὸς ἢ περὶ δόσεως ἢ λήψεως ἢ περὶ τοιούτων μωρῶν πραγμάτων: ταῦτα γὰρ πάντα μωρά ἐστι καὶ κενὰ καὶ ἄφρονα καὶ ἀσύμφορα τοῖς δούλοις τοῦ θεοῦ. ἡ δὲ μακροθυμία μεγάλη ἐστὶ καὶ ἰσχυρὰ καὶ δύναμιν ἔχουσα καὶ στιβαρὰν καὶ εὐθηνουμένην ἐν πλατυσμῷ μεγάλῳ, ἱλαρά, ἀγαλλιωμένη, ἀμέριμνος οὖσα, δοξάζουσα τὸν κύριον ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ, μηδὲν ἐν ἑαυτῇ ἔχουσα πικρόν, παραμένουσα διὰ παντὸς πραεῖα καὶ ἡσύχιος: αὕτη οὖν ἡ μακροθυμία κατοικεῖ μετὰ τῶν τὴν πίστιν ἐχόντων ὁλόκληρον. ἡ δὲ ὀξυχολία πρῶτον μὲν μωρά ἐστιν, ἐλαφρά τε καὶ ἄφρων. εἶτα ἐκ τῆς ἀφροσύνης γίνεται πικρία, ἐκ δὲ τῆς πικρίας θυμός, ἐκ δὲ τοῦ θυμοῦ ὀργή, ἐκ δὲ τῆς ὀργῆς μῆνις: εἶτα ἡ μῆνις αὕτη ἐκ τοσούτων κακῶν συνισταμένη γίνεται ἁμαρτία μεγάλη καὶ ἀνίατος. ὅταν γὰρ ταῦτα τὰ πνεύματα ἐν ἑνὶ ἀγγείῳ κατοικῇ, οὗ καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον κατοικεῖ, οὐ χωρεῖ τὸ ἄγγος ἐκεῖνο, ἀλλ’ ὑπερπλεονάζει. τὸ τρυφερὸν οὖν πνεῦμα, μὴ ἔχον συνήθειαν μετὰ πονηροῦ πνεύματος κατοικεῖν μηδὲ μετὰ σκληρότητος, ἀποχωρεῖ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τοῦ τοιούτου καὶ ζητεῖ κατοικεῖν μετὰ πραότητος καὶ ἡσυχίας. εἶτα ὅταν ἀποστῇ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκείνου, οὗ κατοικεῖ, γίνεται ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος κενὸς ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ δικαίου, καὶ τὸ λοιπὸν πεπληρωμένος τοῖς πνεύμασι τοῖς πονηροῖς ἀκαταστατεῖ ἐν πάσῃ πράξει αὐτοῦ, περισπώμενος ὧδε κἀκεῖσε ἀπὸ τῶν πνευμάτων τῶν πονηρῶν, καὶ ὅλως ἀποτυφλοῦται ἀπὸ τῆς διανοίας τῆς ἀγαθῆς. οὕτως οὖν συμβαίνει πᾶσι τοῖς ὀξυχόλοις. ἀπέχου οὖν ἀπὸ τῆς ὀξυχολίας, τοῦ πονηροτάτου πνεύματος: ἔνδυσαι δὲ τὴν μακροθυμίαν καὶ ἀντίστα τῇ ὀξυχολίᾳ καὶ τῇ πικρίᾳ, καὶ ἔσῃ εὑρισκόμενος μετὰ τῆς σεμνότητος τῆς ἠγαπημένης ὑπὸ τοῦ κυρίου. βλέπε οὖν μήποτε παρενθυμηθῇς τὴν ἐντολὴν ταύτην: ἐὰν γὰρ ταύτης τῆς ἐντολῆς κυριεύσῃς, καὶ τὰς λοιπὰς ἐντολὰς δυνήσῃ φυλάξαι, ἅς σοι μέλλω ἐντέλλεσθαι. ἰσχυροῦ ἐν αὐταῖς καὶ ἐνδυναμοῦ, καὶ πάντες ἐνδυναμούσθωσαν, ὅσοι ἐὰν θέλωσιν ἐν αὐταῖς πορεύεσθαι.

excerpts.author: Hermas
english: I was fasting, sitting on a mountain, and thanking the Lord for everything He had done for me when I saw the Shepherd come and sit beside me. He asked, 'Why have you come here so early?' I answered, 'Because, Lord, I am keeping a station.' He replied, 'What is a station?' I said, 'I am fasting, Lord.' Then he asked, 'What is this fasting that you are practicing?' I told him, 'I fast as is customary, Lord.' He said, 'You do not know how to fast to the Lord. This fasting you are doing is useless to Him.' I asked, 'Why do you say this, Lord?' He answered, 'I tell you that what you think is fasting is not fasting at all. But I will teach you what fasting is acceptable and complete to the Lord. Listen. God does not want this kind of empty fasting, because fasting like this does nothing for righteousness. Instead, fast to God in this way: do no evil in your life, but serve the Lord with a pure heart. Keep His commandments, walk in His precepts, and let no evil desire rise in your heart. Believe in God, that if you do these things and fear Him and control yourself from every evil deed, you will live to God. And if you do these things, you will offer a great and acceptable fast to God.'

'Listen to the parable I am about to tell you; it illustrates this fasting. A certain man owned a field and many slaves. He planted part of the field as a vineyard. He chose a particular slave who was faithful, pleasing, and honorable, called him over, and said: "Take this vineyard I planted, dig around it until I return, and do nothing else to it. Keep this command of mine, and you will become free from me." Then the master went away on a journey. After he left, the slave dug around the vineyard. When he finished, he saw that it was full of weeds. He reasoned to himself: "I have fulfilled the Lord's command. I will now dig the soil further; the vineyard will look more beautiful when cultivated, and without weeds it will produce more fruit, since the weeds will not choke it." So he dug up the vineyard and pulled out every weed in it. The vineyard became exceptionally beautiful and healthy, with no weeds choking it. After some time, the master of the slave and the field returned and entered the vineyard. Seeing it neatly fenced, thoroughly cultivated, all the weeds removed, and the vines thriving, he rejoiced greatly over the slave's work.'

greek: Νηστεύων καὶ καθήμενος εἰς ὄρος τι κα εὐχαριστῶν τῷ κυρίῳ περὶ πάντων ὧν ἐποίησε μετ’ ἐμοῦ, βλέπω τὸν ποιμένα παρακαθήμενόν μοι καὶ λέγοντα: Τί ὀρθρινὸς ὧδε ἐλήλυθας; Ὅτι, φημί, κύριε, στατίωνα ἔχω. Τί, φησίν, ἐστὶ στατίων; Νηστεύω, φημί, κύριε. Νηστεία δὲ, φησί, τί ἐστιν αὕτη, ἣν νηστεύετε; Ὡς εἰώθειν, φημί, κύριε, οὕτω νηστεύω. Οὐκ οἴδατε, φησί, νηστεύειν τῷ κυρίῳ, οὐδέ ἐστιν νηστεία αὕτη ἡ ἀνωφελής, ἣν νηστεύετε αὐτῷ. Διατί, φημί, κύριε, τοῦτο λέγεις; Λέγω σοι, φησίν, ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν αὕτη νηστεία, ἣν δοκεῖτε νηστεύειν: ἀλλ’ ἐγώ σε διδάξω, τί ἐστι νηστεία δεκτὴ καὶ πλήρης τῷ κυρίῳ. Ἄκουε, φησίν. ὁ θεὸς οὐ βούλεται τοιαύτην νηστείαν ματαίαν: οὕτω γὰρ νηστεύων τῷ θεῷ οὐδὲν ἐργάσῃ τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ. νήστευσον δὲ τῷ θεῷ νηστείαν τοιαύτην: μηδὲν πονηρεύσῃ ἐν τῇ ζωῇ σου, ἀλλὰ δούλευσον τῷ κυρίῳ ἐν καθαρᾷ καρδίᾳ: τήρησον τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ πορευόμενος ἐν τοὶς προστάγμασιν αὐτοῦ καὶ μηδεμία ἐπιθυμία πονηρὰ ἀναβήτω ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου: πίστευσον δὲ τῷ θεῷ, ὅτι, ἐὰν ταῦτα ἐργάσῃ καὶ φοβηθῇς αὐτὸν καὶ ἐγκρατεύσῃ ἀπὸ παντὸς πονηροῦ πράγματος, ζήσῃ τῷ θεῷ: καὶ ταῦτα ἐὰν ἐργάσῃ, μεγάλην νηστείαν ποιήσεις καὶ δεκτὴν τῷ θεῷ. Ἄκουε τὴν παραβολήν, ἣν μέλλω σοι λέγειν, ἀνήκουσαν τῇ νηστείᾳ. εἶχέ τις ἀγρὸν καὶ δούλους πολλοὺς καὶ μέρος τι τοῦ ἀγροῦ ἐφύτευσεν ἀμπελῶνα: καὶ ἐκλεξάμενος δοῦλόν τινα πιστὸν καὶ εὐάρεστον ἔντιμον, προσεκαλέσατο αὐτὸν καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ: Λάβε τὸν ἀμπελῶνα τοῦτον, ὃν ἐφύτευσα, καὶ χαράκωσον αὐτόν, ἕως ἔρχομαι, καὶ ἕτερον δὲ μὴ ποιήσῃς τῷ ἀμπελῶνι: καὶ ταύτην μου τὴν ἐντολὴν φύλαξον, καὶ ἐλεύθερος ἔσῃ παῤ ἐμοί. ἐξῆλθε δε ὁ δεσπότης τοῦ δούλου εἰς τὴν ἀποδημίαν. ἐξελθόντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἔλαβεν ὁ δοῦλος καὶ ἐχαράκωσε τὸν ἀμπελῶνα. καὶ τελέσας τὴν χαράκωσιν τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος εἶδε τὸν ἀμπελῶνα βοτανῶν πλήρη ὄντα. ἐν ἑαυτῷ οὗν ἐλογίσατο λέγων: Ταύτην τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ κυρίου τετέλεκα: σκάψω λοιπὸν τὸν ἀμπελῶνα τοῦτον, καὶ ἔσται εὐπρεπέστερος ἐσκαμμένος, καὶ βοτάνας μὴ ἔχων δώσει καρπὸν πλείονα, μὴ πνιγόμενος ὑπὸ τῶν βοτανῶν. λαβὼν ἔσκαψε τὸν ἀμπελῶνα καὶ πάσας τὰς βοτάνας τὰς οὔσας ἐν τῷ ἀμπελῶνι ἐξέτιλλε. καὶ ἐγένετο ὁ ἀμπελὼν ἐκεῖνος εὐπρεπέστατος καὶ εὐθαλής, μὴ ἔχων βοτάνας πνιγούσας αὐτόν. μετὰ χρόνον ἦλθεν ὁ δεσπότης τοῦ δούλου καὶ τοῦ ἀγροῦ καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα. καὶ ἰδὼν τὸν ἀμπελῶνα κεχαρακωμένον εὐπρεπῶς, ἔτι δὲ καὶ ἐσκαμμένον καὶ πάσας τὰς βοτάνας ἐκτετιλμένας καὶ εὐθαλεῖς οὔσας τὰς ἀμπέλους, ἐχάρη λίαν ἐπὶ τοῖς ἔργοις τοῦ δούλου.

excerpts.author: Hermas
english: After I had finished writing down the commands and parables of the Shepherd, the angel of repentance came to me and said, "I want to show you everything the Holy Spirit revealed to you in the form of the Church, because that Spirit is the Son of God. Since you were too weak in the flesh, it was not disclosed to you through an angel. But once the Spirit strengthened you and your power grew so that you could actually see an angel, the building of the tower was revealed to you through the Church, and you saw it all well and reverently, as if by a virgin. Now you see through an angel by that same Spirit, but you must learn everything more accurately from me. That is why the glorious angel sent me to live in your house: so you can see everything with power, without fear, and not as you did before."

He then took me to Arcadia, to a breast-shaped mountain, and seated me on its summit. From there he showed me a vast plain encircled by twelve mountains, each with a distinct appearance. The first was black as soot. The second was bare, without any grass. The third was covered in thorns and thistles. The fourth had grass that was half-withered: the upper parts were green, but the parts near the roots were dry, and some of the grass withered completely when the sun scorched it. The fifth mountain had green grass and was rough terrain. The sixth was entirely split with fissures, both small and large; grass grew in the cracks, but it was not thriving—rather, it was withered. The seventh mountain had cheerful grass, and the whole mountain flourished; every kind of beast and bird lived there, and the more they grazed, the more the grass thrived. The eighth mountain was full of springs, and every kind of the Lord's creation drank from those springs. The ninth mountain had no water at all and was completely desolate; it contained deadly wild beasts and reptiles that destroy people. The tenth mountain had very large trees and was entirely shady; under the shade of the trees, sheep lay resting and being sheared. The eleventh mountain was heavily wooded, and its trees were laden with fruit, adorned with various kinds, so that anyone who saw them would desire to eat from them. The twelfth mountain was entirely white, its appearance cheerful, and it was the most beautiful of all.

In the middle of the plain he showed me a great white rock rising up from the ground. The rock stood higher than the mountains and was four-sided, so that it could contain the whole world. The rock was ancient, with a gate cut into it, yet the cutting of the gate looked recent to me. The gate shone brighter than the sun, so that I marveled at its brilliance. Twelve virgins stood around the gate.

τῆς Ἐκκλησίας: ἐκεῖνο γὰρ τὸ πνεῦμα ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν. ἐπειδὴ γὰρ ἀσθενέστερος τῇ σαρκὶ ἦς, οὐκ ἐδηλώθη σοι δἰ ἀγγέλου. ὅτε οὖν ἐνεδυναμώθης διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος καὶ ἴσχυσας τῇ ἰσχύϊ σου, ὥστε δύνασθαί σε καὶ ἄγγελον ἰδεῖν, τότε μὲν οὖν ἐφανερώθη σοι διὰ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας ἡ οἰκοδομὴ τοῦ πύργου: καλῶς καὶ σεμνῶς πάντα ὡς ὑπὸ παρθένου ἑώρακας. νῦν δὲ ὑπὸ ἀγγέλου βλέπεις διὰ τοῦ αὐτοῦ μὲν πνεύματος: δεῖ δέ σε παῤ ἐμοῦ ἀκριβέστερον πάντα μαθεῖν. εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ καὶ ἐδόθην ὑπὸ τοῦ ἐνδόξου ἀγγέλου εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου κατοικῆσαι. ἵνα δυνατῶς πάντα ἴδῃς, μηδὲν δειλαινόμενος καὶ ὡς τὸ πρότερον. ἦν μέλαν ὡς ἀσβόλη: τὸ δὲ δεύτερον ψιλόν, βοτάνας μὴ ἔχον: τὸ δὲ τρίτον ἀκανθῶν καὶ τριβόλων πλῆρες: τὸ δὲ τέταρτον βοτάνας ἔχον ἡμιξήρους, τὰ μὲν ἐπάνω τῶν βοτανῶν χλωρά, τὰ δὲ πρὸς ταῖς ῥίζαις ξηρά: τινὲς δὲ βοτάναι, ὅταν ὁ ἥλιος ἐπικεκαύκει, ξηραὶ ἐγίνοντο: τὸ δὲ πέμπτον ὄρος ἔχον βοτάνας χλωρὰς καὶ τραχὺ ὄν. τὸ δὲ ἕκτον ὄρος σχισμῶν ὅλως ἔγεμεν, ὧν μὲν μικρῶν, ὧν δὲ μεγάλων: εἶχον δὲ βοτάνας αἱ σχισμαί, οὐ λίαν δὲ ἦσαν εὐθαλεῖς αἱ βοτάναι, μᾶλλον δὲ ὡς μεμαραμμέναι ἦσαν. τὸ δὲ ἕβδομον ὄρος εἶχε βοτάνας ἱλαράς, καὶ ὅλον τὸ ὄρος εὐθηνοῦν ἦν, καὶ πᾶν γένος κτηνῶν καὶ ὀρνέων ἐνέμοντο εἰς τὸ ὄρος πηγῶν τοῦ ὄρους ἐκείνου. τὸ δὲ ἔννατον ὄρος ὅλως ὕδωρ οὐκ εἶχεν καὶ ὅλον ἐρημῶδες ἦν. εἶχε δὲ ἐν αὐτῷ θηρία καὶ ἑρπετὰ θανάσιμα διαφθείροντα ἀνθρώπους. τὸ δὲ δέκατον ὄρος εἶχε δένδρα μέγιστα καὶ ὅλον κατάσκιον ἦν, καὶ ὑπὸ τὴν σκέπην τῶν δένδρων πρόβατα κατέκειντο ἀναπαυόμενα καὶ μαρυκώμενα. τὸ δὲ ἑνδέκατον ὄρος λίαν σύνδενδρον ἦν, καὶ τὰ δένδρα ἐκεῖνα κατάκαρπα ἦν, ἄλλοις καὶ ἄλλοις καρποῖς κεκοσμημένα, ἵνα ἰδών τις αὐτὰ ἐπιθυμήσῃ φαγεῖν ἐκ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν. τὸ δὲ δωδέκατον ὄρος ὅλον ἦν λευκόν, καὶ ἡ πρόσοψις αὐτοῦ ἱλαρὰ ἦν: καὶ εὐπρεπέστατον ἦν ἐν αὑτῷ το ὄρος. Εἰς μέσον δὲ τοῦ πεδίου ἔδειξέ μοι πέτραν μεγάλην λευκὴν ἐκ τοῦ πεδίου ἀναβεβηκυῖαν. ἡ δὲ πέτρα ὑψηλοτέρα ἦν τῶν ὀρέων, τετράγωνος, ὥστε δύνασθαι ὅλον τὸν κόσμον χωρῆσαι. παλαιὰ δὲ ἦν ἠ πέτρα ἐκείνη, πύλην ἐκκεκομμένην ἔχουσα: ὡς πρόσφατος δὲ ἐδόκει μοι εἶναι ἡ ἐκκόλαψις τῆς πύλης. ἡ δὲ πύλη οὕτως ἔστιλβεν ὑπὲρ τὸν ἥλιον, ὥστε με θαυμάζειν ἐπὶ τῇ λαμπηδόνι τῆς πύλης. κύκλῳ δὲ τῆς πύλης εἱστήκεισαν παρθένοι δώδεκα.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: Now we receive a share of his Spirit, for the perfection and preparation of incorruptibility, gradually growing accustomed to receive and to bear God. The Apostle calls this a guarantee—that is, a portion of the honor God has promised us. Writing to the Ephesians he says, "In him you also, when you heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, and believed in him, were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit, who is the guarantee of our inheritance" (Ephesians 1:13-14).

Therefore this guarantee dwelling in us now makes us spiritual, transforming what is mortal by immortality. "You are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if in fact the Spirit of God dwells in you" (Rom 8:9). This change comes not by the loss of the flesh but by communion with the Spirit. Paul was not writing to people without bodies; he wrote to those who had received the Spirit of God, in whom we cry, "Abba, Father" (Rom 8:15; Gal 4:6).

If even now, while we hold the guarantee, we cry "Abba, Father," what will happen when we rise and see him face to face? What will happen when our members pour out a hymn of abundant exultation, glorifying the one who raised them from the dead and gave them eternal life? If the guarantee, embracing a person in itself, already makes him say "Abba, Father," what will the full grace of the Spirit do, which will be given to humanity by God? It will make us like him and perfect us as the Father—perfecting humanity according to the image and likeness of God (Gen 1:26).

Therefore those who possess the guarantee of the Spirit, and do not serve the flesh but subject themselves to the Spirit, living rightly in all things, the Apostle justly calls spiritual, because the Spirit of God dwells in them. Yet incorporeal spirits will not become spiritual human beings; it is our substance—the union of soul and flesh—that, by taking up the Spirit of God, perfects the human person.

Those, however, who reject the counsel of the Spirit and serve the pleasures of the flesh, who live irrationally and are cast down unrestrained into their desires, since they have no aspiration of the divine Spirit but live like pigs and dogs—the Apostle justly calls these people carnal, because they perceive nothing but carnal things.

The prophets also liken them to irrational animals for this same reason, because of their irrational gathering, saying: "Stallions maddened have become like mares, each one neighing after his neighbor's wife" (Jer 5:8). And again: "Man in his pomp yet without understanding is like the beasts that perish" (Ps 49:20). This is because he is likened to beasts for his own cause, imitating an irrational life. In common speech we too call such people beasts and irrational animals.

The Law, however, had foretold all these things figuratively, sketching a portrait of humanity from animals: "Whatever has a divided hoof and chews the cud, it declares clean; but whatever either lacks both of these or has only one of them, it sets apart as unclean" (Lev 11:3-4; Deut 14:6-7). Who then are clean? Those who make their journey to the Father and the Son firmly through faith; for this is the firmness of those with a divided hoof. And they meditate on the words of God day and night, that they may be adorned with good works (Ps 1:2); for this is the virtue of those who chew the cud.

Unclean are those who neither have a divided hoof nor chew the cud—that is, those who neither have faith in God nor meditate on his words. This is the abomination of the Gentiles. Those who chew the cud indeed but do not have a divided hoof are also unclean; this is the figurative description of the Jews. They have the words of God in their mouth, but they do not fix the stability of their root in the Father and the Son; for this reason their kind is slippery. They are like single-hoofed animals, easily slipping. But those who have a divided hoof are more firm, each step succeeding the next, one hoof supporting the other.

Similarly unclean are those who have a divided hoof indeed but do not chew the cud. This is the description of all heretics and those who do not meditate on the words of God, nor are adorned with works of justice. To them the Lord says, "Why do you call me 'Lord, Lord,' and not do what I tell you?" (Luke 6:46). Such people say they believe in the Father and the Son, yet they never meditate on the words of God as they ought, nor are they adorned with works of justice. Instead, as we said before, they have taken on the life of pigs and dogs, surrendering themselves to uncleanness, gluttony, and the rest of the vices.

Justly, therefore, the Apostle calls all such people carnal, because through their unbelief and self-indulgence they do not attain the divine Spirit. They cast themselves off with various dispositions, living irrationally in their lusts. The prophet called them beasts and wild animals; common usage interprets them as cattle and irrational creatures; the Law declares them unclean.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: We cannot know God by measuring his magnitude, for it is impossible to measure the Father; but we are led to God through his Word according to his love, and by obeying him we always learn how great God is. He is the one who establishes, chooses, and adorns all things in relation to us, and so we ourselves have been made together with everything he contains. This is what Scripture says: God formed the human being from the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life (Genesis 2:7). Therefore angels did not make us, nor did they form us, nor could angels make the image of God, nor anyone else except the Word of the Lord, nor any power far removed from the Father. God did not need such helpers to do what he had predetermined, as if he lacked his own hands. For the Word and Wisdom, the Son and Spirit, are always present with him, and through them and in them he freely and willingly made all things. He also speaks to them, saying, "Let us make man in our image and likeness," himself drawing from himself the substance of creatures, the pattern of things made, and the form of the world's ornaments.

Scripture has rightly declared: "First of all, believe that there is one God, who established and completed and made all things from what did not exist, so that all things might be: capable of all things, and not capable of being grasped by anyone." The prophet Malachi also says: "Is it not one God who established us? Is it not one Father of all of us?" (Malachi 2:10). And consequently the Apostle says: "There is one God, the Father, who is over all and in us all" (Ephesians 4:6). Similarly the Lord says: "All things have been handed over to me by my Father" — clearly by him who made all things, for nothing has been taken away. Because of this he is the Judge of the living and the dead, holding the key of David: "he will open, and no one will shut; he will shut, and no one will open." No one else could open the Father's book, neither in heaven nor on earth nor under the earth, nor even see it, except the Lamb who was slain and redeemed us with his blood from him who made all things by the Word and adorned them by Wisdom. He received all authority when the Word became flesh, so that just as the Word of God held primacy in heaven, so also he might hold primacy on earth — because the righteous man who committed no sin, in whose mouth no deceit was found — and primacy over the things under the earth, having become the firstborn of the dead. And so all things might see their King, as we have previously said; and so the paternal light might meet the flesh of the Lord, and radiant light might come to us from his flesh, and so humanity might become incorruptible, wrapped in the Father's light.

We have demonstrated through many passages that the Word, that is, the Son, was always with the Father. And since Wisdom, that is, the Spirit, was with him before all creation, Solomon says: "By wisdom the Lord founded the earth; by understanding he established the heavens; by his knowledge the deeps broke open, and the clouds dropped down dew" (Proverbs 8:22-31). And again: "The Lord created me at the beginning of his work, the first of his acts of old. Ages ago I was set up, at the first, before the beginning of the earth. When there were no depths I was brought forth, when there were no springs abounding with water. Before the mountains had been shaped, before the hills, I was brought forth" (Proverbs 8:22-31). And again: "When he established the heavens, I was there; when he drew a circle on the face of the deep, when he made firm the skies above, when he established the fountains of the deep, when he assigned to the sea its limit, when he marked out the foundations of the earth, then I was beside him, like a master workman, and I was daily his delight, rejoicing before him always, rejoicing in his inhabited world and delighting in the children of man" (Proverbs 8:22-31).

Therefore there is one God, who made and ordered all things by the Word and Wisdom. This is the Demiurge, who also assigned this world to the human race. According to his magnitude he is unknown to all who have been made by him, for no one has searched out his height — neither the ancients who have rested, nor those who are now. But according to love he is always known through him through whom he established all things: our Lord Jesus Christ, who in the last times became man among men, so that he might join the end to the beginning. And therefore the prophets, receiving the prophetic gift from the same Word, predicted his coming in the flesh, through which the mingling and communion of God and humanity was accomplished according to the Father's good pleasure. The Word of God had previously announced that God would be seen by humans, would converse with them on earth, would be present with his creation, saving it, being perceived by it, and liberating us from the hands of all who hate us — that is, from the spirit of all transgression — and making us serve him in holiness and justice all our days, so that humanity, having received the Spirit of God, might give glory to the Father.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: The true spiritual disciple receives the Spirit of God. From the beginning the Spirit was present to humanity in every disposition of God; he announced future things, showed present things, and narrated past things. He judges all people, yet no one judges him. He judges the nations, who serve the creature more than the Creator and consume their entire effort in vain with a reprobate mind. He also judges the Jews. They do not perceive the word of liberty, and they refuse to go free even though they have a Liberator present. They pretend to serve outside the Law at the wrong time, as though they needed nothing from God. They do not recognize the advent of Christ, which he accomplished for the salvation of humanity, and they refuse to understand. All the prophets announced two advents of his. The first: he became man and was struck, knowing how to bear weakness; he sat on a foal of a donkey; he was the stone rejected by the builders; he was led like a sheep to slaughter; he overcame Amalek by the extension of his hands. He gathered the scattered children from the ends of the earth into the Father's fold; he remembered his own dead who had fallen asleep, and he descended to them so that he might rescue them. The second: he will come upon the clouds, bringing a day like a burning furnace; he will strike the earth with the word of his mouth and kill the impious with the breath of his lips; he will hold a winnowing fork in his hand, clear his threshing floor, gather the wheat into his barn, and burn the chaff with unquenchable fire.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: All these heretics came long after the bishops to whom the Apostles entrusted the churches, a point we proved in the third book with every care. Because they are blind to the truth, they are forced to wander off onto one divergent path after another, so the footprints of their teaching lie scattered in discordant, incoherent disarray.

But those who belong to the Church walk the whole world over, bearing a firm tradition from the Apostles that lets us see one and the same faith everywhere: one and the same God the Father worshipped by all, the same mystery of the Son's incarnation believed, the same gift of the Spirit received, the same precepts pondered, the same pattern of ordination that serves the Church preserved, the same hope of the Lord's return cherished, and the same salvation of the whole person—soul and body—upheld.

The Church's preaching is true and steadfast, and in it the single way of salvation is displayed throughout the world. To the Church has been entrusted the light of God; therefore the wisdom of God, by which He saves all people, is sung in the streets, acts with authority in the squares, is proclaimed from the highest walls, and speaks constantly at the gates. Everywhere the Church preaches the truth, and she is the lamp that carries the light of Christ.

Those who abandon the Church's preaching accuse the saints of ignorance, never weighing how far the godly person surpasses the blasphemous, shameless sophist. All heretics are of this stripe, along with those who imagine they have discovered something beyond the truth. Following the paths already laid out, they make their journey in varied, shapeless, feeble ways, never holding the same convictions twice, like blind men led by the blind. Justly they fall into the pit of hidden ignorance, always searching, never finding the truth.

We must therefore flee their opinions and keep a more intent watch, so that we are not shaken by them; we must take refuge in the Church, be reared in her bosom, and be nourished with the Lord's own food. For the Church has been planted as a paradise in this world. 'From every tree of the garden you may eat,' says the Spirit of God—that is, from every Scripture that belongs to the Lord you may eat; but from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you must not eat, nor touch the whole heretious dissent (Genesis 2:17).

The heretics themselves claim to possess the knowledge of good and evil, and they hurl their impious judgments against the God who made them, presuming to know more than the measure of perception allows. That is why the Apostle warns: 'Do not be wise beyond what it is fitting to be wise, but be wise unto sobriety' (Romans 12:3), lest by eating their knowledge—which is wiser than it ought to be—we be cast out of the paradise of life. Into that paradise the Lord leads those who obey Him, recapitulating in Himself all things in heaven and on earth. The things in heaven are spiritual; the things on earth are ordered according to man's nature.

He has recapitulated everything in Himself, joining man to the Spirit and placing the Spirit in man. He Himself became the head of the Spirit, and gives the Spirit to be the head of man, for through Him we see, and hear, and speak.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: God indeed forms the human person within his own creation, and what follows is an adaptation to his child. For it is through the Father's hands — that is, through the Son and the Spirit — that a human being is made in the likeness of God, yet no single part constitutes the whole. The soul and the spirit may each be a part of a human being, but a human being is never merely one of them. A perfect human being is the mixture and union of the soul, which takes on the Spirit of the Father, blended with the flesh that has been formed according to the image. That is why the Apostle says, "We speak wisdom among the perfect" (1 Cor 2:6); by the perfect he means those who have received the Spirit of God and speak in tongues through the Spirit of God, just as we have heard many brothers speaking in the Church. They possess prophetic gifts, speak in every tongue through the Spirit, bring hidden human matters to light for the common good, and unfold the mysteries of God. The Apostle calls such people "spiritual" (1 Cor 2:15); they exist as spiritual by sharing in the Spirit, not by depriving or sidelining the flesh, and not by the Spirit alone. If someone strips away the substance of the flesh — that is, the formed body — and considers only the spirit, the result is not a spiritual human being but merely a human spirit or the Spirit of God. But when the spirit, mingled with the soul, is united to the formed body, then by the outpouring of the Spirit a spiritual and perfect human being comes into existence; and this is the one who is made in the image and likeness of God. If the Spirit is absent from the soul, that person is truly animal — carnal, abandoned, imperfect — possessing the image in the formed body but not taking on the likeness through the Spirit; such a one remains imperfect. Likewise, if anyone discards the image and despises the formed body, he can no longer grasp what a human being is, but only some part of a human being, as we have said before, or something else entirely apart from a human being. For the forming of the flesh, by itself, is not the perfect human being; it is the human body, a part of the human being. Nor is the soul by itself the human being; it is the human soul, a part of the human being. Nor is the Spirit the human being: the Spirit is called Spirit, not human being. The mixture and union of all these elements, however, produces the perfect human being.

For this reason the Apostle, explaining himself, sets forth the perfect and spiritual human being of salvation. In his first letter to the Thessalonians he prays: "May the God of peace himself sanctify you entirely; and may your spirit and soul and body be kept sound and blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ" (1 Thess 5:23). What other reason could he have had to ask for the integrity and perfection of these three — soul, body, and spirit — except that he knew their restoration, their union, and their one and the same salvation? That is why he also says the perfect are those who present the three without blame to the Lord. Therefore the perfect are those who keep the Spirit of God persevering within them and who have preserved their souls and bodies blameless, holding fast the faith that belongs to God — that is, faith directed toward God — and maintaining the justice owed to the neighbor.

From this it follows that the Apostle also calls the formed body the temple of God: "Do you not know that you are God's temple and that God's Spirit dwells in you? If anyone destroys God's temple, God will destroy that person. For God's temple is holy, and you are that temple" (1 Cor 3:16–17). He plainly identifies the body as the temple in which the Spirit dwells. Just as the Lord said of himself, "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up" (John 2:19), and the Evangelist notes that he was speaking of his own body. And not only is it a temple, but it is also the temple of Christ, as he tells the Corinthians: "Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I therefore take the members of Christ and make them members of a prostitute?" (1 Cor 6:15). He is not saying this about some other spiritual man; such a man does not join himself to a prostitute. Rather, our body — that is, the flesh that perseveres in holiness and purity — he declares to be members of Christ; but when it joins itself to a prostitute, the members become members of a prostitute. And because of this he said, "If anyone destroys God's temple, God will destroy that person" (1 Cor 3:17). So then, if the temple of God, in which the Spirit of the Father dwells, and the members of Christ do not share in salvation but are handed over to perdition, is that not the height of blasphemy? Since our bodies are raised not from their own substance but by the power of God, he says to the Corinthians: "The body is not meant for sexual immorality but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body. God raised the Lord and will also raise us by his power" (1 Cor 6:13–14).
