latin: Sed quia frequenter intendunt illum nobis locum quo dictum sit: ego et pater unum sumus, et in hoc illos aeque facile uincemus. si enim erat, ut haeretici putant, pater Christus, oportuit dicere: ego pater unus sum. at cum ego dicit, deinde patrem infert, dicendo ego et pater, proprietatem personae suae, id est filii, a paterna auctoritate discernit atque distinguit, non tantummodo de sono nominis, sed etiam de ordine dispositae potestatis; qui potuisset dicere, ego pater, si patrem se esse meminisset. et quia dixit unum, intellegant haeretici quia non dixit unus. unum enim neutraliter positum societatis concordiam non unitatem personae sonat. unum enim non unus esse dicitur, quoniam nec ad numerum refertur, sed ad societatem alterius expromitur. denique adicit dicens, sumus, non sum, ut ostenderet per hoc quod dixit, sumus ego et pater, duas esse personas; vnum autem quod ait, ad concordiam et eandem sententiam et ad ipsam caritatis societatem pertinere, ut merito unum sit pater et filius per concordiam et per amorem et per dilectionem. et quoniam ex patre est, quicquid illud est, filius est, manente tamen distinctione, ut non sit pater ille qui filius, quia nec filius ille qui pater est. nec enim sumus addidisset, si unum se et solitarium patrem filium factum esse meminisset. Denique nouit hanc concordiae unitatem et apostolus Paulus, cum personarum tamen distinctione. nam cum ad Corinthios scriberet, ego, inquit, plantaui, Apollo rigauit, sed deus inttague neque qui plantat est quicquam, neque qui rigat, sed qui incrementum dat deus. qui autem plantat, et qui rigat, unum sunt. quis autem non intellegat alterum esse Apollo, alterum Paulum, non eundem atque ipsum Apollo pariter et Paulum? denique et diuersa uniuscuiusque sunt officia prolata: alter enim guz plantat, et alter qui rigat. hos tamen duos, non quod unus sit, sed quod unum sint, proposuit apostolus Paulus, ut alter quidem sit Apollo, alter uero Paulus, quantum ad personarum distinctionem pertinet; [quantum uero duorum una sententia est, ueritas una est, fides una est, una atque eadem religio est, unus etiam dei timor est, unum sunt, etiam si duo sint. ipsum sunt, dum ipsum sapiunt. etenim quos personae ratio inuicem diuidit, eosdem rursus inuicem religionis ratio conducit. et quamuis idem atque ipsi non sint, dum idem sentiunt, ipsum sunt; et cum duo sint, unum sunt, habentes in fide societatem, etiam si gerant in personis diuersitatem. Denique cum ad has uoces domini imperitia fuisset Iudaica commota et temere ad usque saxa succensa, ita ut discurrerent et dicerent: on te lapidamus propter bonum opus, sed propter blasphemiam, et quia tu, cum homo sis, facis te deum, distinctionem posuit dominus in ratione reddenda, quomodo se deum aut dixisset aut intellegi uellet. quem pater sanctificauit, inquit, et misit in hunc mundum, uos dicitis, quia blasphemas, quia dixi, filius dei sum? etiam hic patrem habere se dixit. filius est ergo, non pater—patrem enim confessus se fuisset, Si patrem se esse meminisset—et sanctificatum se a suo patre esse proponit. dum ergo accipit sanctificationem a patre, est, sed filius. pater enim si fuisset, sanctificationem dedisset, non accepisset. nunc autem profitendo se accepisse sanctificationem a patre, hoc ipso, quo patre se minorem accipiendo ab ipso sanctificationem probat, filium se esse, non patrem monstrauit. missum praeterea se esse dicit, ut per hanc oboedientiam, qua uenit dominus Christus missus, non pater sed filius probetur, qui misisset utique, si pater fuisset. missus autem non fuit pater, ne pater subditus alteri deo, dum mittitur, probaretur. et tamen post haec adicit, quod omnem omnino ambiguitatem dissolueret et totam controuersiam erroris exstingueret. ait enim in ultima parte sermonis: vos dicitis, guia blasphemas, quia dixt, filius dei sum? ergo si euidenter filium dominus se, non patrem, esse testatur, magnae temeritatis et ingentis est furoris exemplum contra ipsius Christi domini testimonium controuersiam diuinitatis et religionis agitare, et Christum Iesum patrem esse dicere, cum animaduertat illum non patrem se, sed filium, comprobasse.

english: Sound reasoning and the authority of faith, taking their cue from the very words and letters of the Lord, urge us to believe also in the Holy Spirit, who was once promised to the Church but given at the times appointed by God. For He was promised through the prophet Joel, but bestowed through Christ. "In the last days, I will pour out my Spirit upon my servants and handmaids," He says (Joel 2:29). And the Lord said: "Receive the Holy Spirit; whose sins you forgive are forgiven, and whose sins you retain are retained" (John 20:22-23). The Lord Christ now calls this Holy Spirit the Paraclete, now declares Him to be the Spirit of truth. He is not new in the Gospel, nor was He given anew. For this same Spirit accused the people in the prophets, and provided advocacy for the nations in the apostles. The people deserved accusation because they had despised the law; and those from the nations who believe deserve to be helped by the Spirit's advocacy because they strive to attain the law of the Gospel. There is indeed a difference in the kinds of offices, since different times bring different reasons for action; yet He who does these things is not different, nor is He another while acting thus, but He is one and the same, distributing His offices through times, occasions, and moments. Finally, the apostle Paul says: "Having the same spirit... as it is written: I believed, therefore I spoke," and we believe, therefore we speak. Therefore the Spirit is one and the same, who is in the prophets and apostles; except that there He was present for a moment, but here He is present always. Moreover, there He was not given so that He would always dwell in them, but here He is given so that He would always remain in them: there He was distributed in measure, but here He is poured out entirely; there He was given sparingly, but here He is provided generously; nor was He exhibited before the Lord's resurrection, but He was bestowed through the resurrection of Christ. For Jesus was saying, "I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate, that He may be with you forever, the Spirit of truth" (John 14:16-17). And: "When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father" (John 15:26). And: "If I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send Him to you" (John 16:7). And: "When the Spirit of truth comes, He will guide you into all truth" (John 16:13).

english: I. From the Discourse on the Resurrection. I. Read the Book on the Resurrection by St. Methodius, Bishop and Martyr, of which that which follows is a selection, that the body is not the fetter of the soul , as Origen thought, nor are souls called by the prophet Jeremiah fettered on account of their being within bodies. For he lays down the principle that the body does not hinder the energies of the soul , but that rather the body is carried about with it, and cooperates in whatever the soul commits to it. But how are we to understand the opinion of Gregory the theologian, and many Others? II. That Origen said that the body was given to the soul as a fetter after the fall, and that previously it lived without a body; but that this body which we wear is the cause of our sins ; wherefore also he called it a fetter, as it can hinder the soul from good works. III. That if the body was given to the soul after the fall as a fetter, it must have been given as a fetter upon the evil or the good. It remains, then, that it was a fetter upon evil . But surely we see that, at the beginning, Cain, clad in this body, committed murder ; and it is evident into what wickedness those who succeeded him ran. excerpts.locus: On the Creation of the World
english: As I reflect, my mind weighing the structure of this world in which we are held, I see that the very speed of its making is this: as the book of Moses records, the one called Genesis, God fashioned this entire mass in six days as an ornament of his majesty, and on the seventh he consecrated it with a blessing (Genesis). Therefore, since both heavenly and earthly things are governed by the number seven of days, I will measure from that seventh day to all the regions of the weeks, and as far as I am able I will try to express the day of virtue in its consummation.

In the beginning God made light, and he divided it into a twelve-hour span of day and night, precisely so that rest might take the place of labor for men at night, and then day might prevail again; by this alternating turn labor is refreshed by rest, and rest is tempered by the exercise of day once more (Genesis).

On the fourth day he made two luminaries in heaven, the greater and the lesser, so that one might preside over the day and the other over the night — the sun and the moon — and he set the other stars in heaven to shine upon the earth and to distinguish times and years and months and days and hours through their courses (Genesis).
Now the reason of truth appears: why the fourth day is called the tetras; why we fast until the ninth hour, until evening, or make the imposition continue into the next day (Genesis).

This world consists of four elements: fire, water, heaven, earth. These four elements make a tetrad of times. The sun and the moon also produce four seasons over the course of a year — spring, summer, autumn, winter — and these seasons make a tetrad (Genesis).

And to explain this further: behold four living creatures before the throne of God, four Gospels, four rivers flowing in paradise, four generations of peoples from Adam to Noah, from Noah to Abraham, from Abraham to Moses, from Moses to Christ the Lord, the Son of God; and four living creatures of man, ox, lion, eagle; and four rivers, Pishon, Gihon, Tigris, Euphrates (Genesis).

Christ Jesus, the author of the things we have mentioned above, was seized by the tetrad of the impious. Therefore, because of his captivity we observe a tetrad; because of the majesty of his works, and because the wholesome times of humanity, rich with fruits and tranquil in weather, pass by, we make the imposition (Genesis).

latin: COGITANTI mihi, una cum animo meo conferenti, de fabrica mundi istius, in quo clausi tenemur, etiam velocitas fabricae istius haec est; sicut in libro Moysis continetur, quem de conditione ipsius scripsit, qui Genesis appellatur. Totam molem istam, Deus sex diebus in ornamento majestatis suae expressit, septimo quibus benedictione. . . consecravit. Idcirco igitur, quoniam septenario numero dierum et coelestia et terrestria reguntur, principii loco, de hac septimam ad omnium septimanarium rigionum metibor, et prout potuero, virtutis diem in eam consummationem conabor exprimere. In principio fecit Deus lucem, eamque duodenario mero horarum, die noctuque, divisit, idcirco videlicet, ut laboribus hominum requies locum noctem dies superduceret, rursus dies supervinceret; hac se alterna vice labor quetis refoveretur, quies exercitatione rursus diei temperaretur. Quarto die fecit duo luminaria in coelo, majus et minus, ut alterum praeesset diei, alterum nocti, solis et lunae; caeteraque sidera posuit in coelo, ut lucerent super terram, et discernerent tempora et annos et menses et dies et horas per stationes. Nunc ratio veritatis ostenditur, quare dies IIII, tetras nuncupatur; quare usque ad horam nonam jejunamus , usque ad vesperam, aut superpositio usque in alterum diem fiat. Mundus itaque iste ex quatuor elementis constat, igne, aqua, coelo, terra. Haec igitur quator elementa temporum tetradem faciunt. Sol quoque et luna per anni spatium quatuor tempora efficiunt, veris, aestatis, autumni, hyemis; et haec tempora tetradem faciunt. Et ut ex ea re longius enarrem, ecce quatuor animalia ante thronum Dei. quatuor evangelia, quatuor flumina in paradiso fluentia, quatuor generationes populorum, ab Adam usque ad Noe, a Noe usque ad Abraham, ab Abraham usque ad Moysem, a Moyse usque ad Christum Dominum, Filium Dei; et quatuor animalia hominis, vituli, leonis, aquilae; et quatuor flumina, Fyson, Geon, Tygris, Euphrates. Homo Christus Jesus auctor eorum, quae supra memoravimus, tetrade ab impiis comprehensus est. Itaque ob captivitatem ejus tetradem ob majestatem operum suorum, et tempora humanitatis salubria, frugibus laeta, tempestatibus tranquilla, decurrant, ideo aut superpositionem facimus.

excerpts.citation: Arnobius — Against the Nations Against the Heathen (Book I)
excerpts.author: Arnobius
english: I have discovered that certain people, convinced by their own reasoning that they possess superior wisdom, are in fact raving like fanatics and spouting pronouncements as if they came straight from an oracle. They claim that ever since the Christian religion appeared in the world, the earth has been ruined and the human race overwhelmed by every kind of misery. They even assert that the heavenly powers have abandoned their age-old duty of overseeing human affairs and have been driven from the regions of the earth. I have therefore decided, within the limits of my ability and my plain style, to confront this envy and dismantle these slanderous charges. I must act so that these accusers do not mistake their popular rhetoric for real substance, nor imagine that our silence would concede them a victory won by the weakness of their own case, not by any failure of its defenders.

I will not deny that their accusation carries great weight and that we deserve hostile hatred — if it can be proven that among us exist the causes that made the world stray from its laws, that exterminated the gods, and that imported such vast sorrows into the ages. Let us therefore examine the thinking behind this opinion and the actual claims being made. Setting aside all partisan zeal that usually obscures and buries the truth, let us weigh the evidence on balanced scales. A chain of rigorous reasoning will certainly show that the impious ones are not us, but the accusers themselves — those who boast of cultivating the divine and clinging to ancient rites.

First, I put this question to them in a calm and reasonable tone: since the name of the Christian religion began to exist on earth, what unseen disaster, what unknown cataclysm, what violation of the fundamental laws of nature has the world itself experienced or suffered? Have the primary elements, from which all things are composed, been transmuted into opposite qualities? Has any part of the cosmic machine that envelops and contains us been loosened or dissolved? Has the world's rotation, which governs the primal motion, begun to drag or to race, or has it been seized by a headlong, precipitous speed? Have the stars started rising in the west and setting in the east? Has the sun, the prince of the stars, which clothes all things in light and animates them with heat, flared up or gone cold, corrupting the balanced temperaments of its usual course? Has the moon ceased to renew itself and return to its ancient phases through the constant cycle of waxing and waning? Have cold, heat, and the moderate temperatures of the irregular seasons perished in confusion? Has winter begun to stretch its days long and summer nights to recall the latest dawns? Have the winds breathed their last? Have the lightning flashes died out, so that the sky no longer condenses into clouds and rain-moistened fields no longer follow? Does the earth refuse the seed committed to it? Do trees refuse to put forth leaves? Have the flavor of edible fruits and the juice of the vine been altered? Does the oil pressed from olives no longer feed lamps when they go out? Do land animals and sea creatures no longer breed or conceive? Do fetuses no longer develop in the womb according to their nature and law? Finally, do human beings — scattered by the first seafaring to the world's uninhabitable shores — no longer join in marriage with solemn rites? Do they no longer beget children, conduct public and private business, or manage their households? Do they no longer direct their talents through diverse arts and disciplines as they please, and reap the returns of their labors? Do those to whom the lot of rule has fallen no longer reign or command? Are they not daily growing greater in dignity and power? Do they not preside over courts, interpret laws, and administer justice? Do not all the other institutions that sustain and structure human life continue to be observed in every nation according to ancestral custom?

latin: Quoniam comperi nonnullos, qui se plurimum sapere suis persuasionibus credunt, insanire, bacchari, et velut quiddam promptum ex oraculo dicere: postquam esse in mundo christiana gens coepit, terrarum orbem periisse, multiformibus malis affectum esse genus humanum; ipsos etiam coelites, derelictis curis solemnibus, quibus quondam solebant invisere res nostras, terrarum ab regionibus exterminatos: statui pro captu, ac mediocritate sermonis contraire invidiae, et calumniosas dissolvere criminationes, ne aut illi sibi videantur, popularia dum verba depromunt, magnum aliquid dicere; aut, si nos talibus continuerimus a litibus, obtinuisse se causam putent, victam sui vitio, non assertorum silentio destitutam. Neque enim negaverim validissimam esse accusationem istam, hostilibusque condignos odiis nos esse, si apud nos esse constiterit causas, per quas suis mundus aberravit ab legibus, exterminati sunt dii longe, examina tanta moerorum mortalium importata sunt saeculis. Inspiciamus igitur opinionis istius mentem, et hoc quod dicitur, quale sit: summotisque omnibus contentionum studiis, quibus obscurari et contegi contemplatio rerum solet, an sit istud quod dicitur verum, momentorum parium examinatione pendamus. Efficietur enim profecto rationum consequentium copulatu, ut non impii nos magis, sed illi ipsi reperiantur criminis istius rei, qui se numinum profitentur esse cultores, atque inveteratis religionibus deditos. Ac primum ab his illud familiari et placida oratione perquirimus: postquam esse nomen in terris christianae religionis occoepit, quidnam invisitatum, quid incognitum, quid contra leges principaliter institutas, aut sensit aut passa est rerum ipsa quae dicitur appellaturque natura? Numquid in contrarias qualitates prima illa elementa mutata sunt, ex quibus res omnes consensum est esse concretas? Numquid machinae hujus, et molis, qua universi tegimur, et continemur inclusi, parte est in aliqua relaxata, aut dissoluta constructio? Numquid vertigo haec mundi, primigenii motus moderaren excedens, aut tardius repere, aut praecipiti coepit volubilitate raptari? Numquid ab occiduis partibus attolere se astra, atque in ortus fieri signorum coepta est inclinatio? Numquid ipse siderum sol princeps, cujus omnia luce vestiuntur, atque animantur calore, exarsit, intepuit, atque in contrarios habitus moderaminis soliti temperamenta corrupit? Numquid luna desivit redintegrare se ipsam, atque in veteres formas novellarum semper restitutione traducere? Numquid frigora, numquid calores, numquid tepores medii inaequalium temporum confusionibus occiderunt? Numquid longos habere dies bruma, revocare tardissimas luces nox coepit aestatis? Numquid suas animas expiraverunt venti? emortiusque flaminibus neque coelum coactatur in nubila, nec madidata ex imbribus arva succedunt? Commendata semina tellus recusat accidere, aut frondescere arbores nolunt? sapor frugibus esculentis, et vitis liquoribus mutatus est? olearum ex bacculis cruor teter exprimitur, nec lumini subministratur extincto? Animalia terris sueta, atque in aquis degentia non suriunt, nec concipiunt? foetus non in uteris sumptos suis moribus, et sua lege custodiunt? Ipsi homines denique, quos per inhabitabiles oras terrae sparsit prima incipiensque navitas, non matrimonia copulant nuptiarum solennibus justis? non dulcissimas procreant liberorum stirpes, non negotia publica, non privata, et familiares res agunt? non, ut cuique libitum est, per diversas artium, disciplinarumque rationes ingenia dirigunt, et studiosae referunt navitatis usuras? Non regnant, non imperant, quibus sors rerum attributa est talium? non auctiores quotidie dignitatibus et potestatibus fiunt? judiciorum disceptationibus praesunt? leges interpretantur et jura? Nonne omnia caetera, quibus vita succingitur et continetur humana, suis omnes in gentibus patriorum celebrant institutionibus morum?

excerpts.author: Didache
english: Whoever comes and teaches you all these things that have been said before, receive him. But if the teacher himself turns and teaches another teaching so as to tear this down, do not listen to him; yet if he teaches so as to add righteousness and knowledge of the Lord, receive him as the Lord.

Concerning the apostles and prophets, act in this way according to the decree of the Gospel. Let every apostle who comes to you be received as the Lord. He shall not stay except one day; if there is need, also the next; but if he stays three days, he is a false prophet. When the apostle leaves, let him take nothing except bread until he finds lodging; if he asks for money, he is a false prophet.

And every prophet who speaks in the Spirit you shall not test or judge; for every sin shall be forgiven, but this sin shall not be forgiven. Yet not everyone who speaks in the Spirit is a prophet, but only if he has the ways of the Lord. From their ways, then, the false prophet and the prophet shall be known.

Every prophet who orders a table in the Spirit shall not eat from it — otherwise he is a false prophet. Every prophet who teaches the truth, if he does not do what he teaches, is a false prophet. But every proven true prophet who acts for a worldly mystery of the church, yet does not teach others to do what he himself does, shall not be judged by you; for he has his judgment with God — for the ancient prophets also acted in this way.
Whoever says in the Spirit, “Give me money,” or anything else, you shall not listen to him; but if he says to give concerning others who are in need, let no one judge him.
greek: Ὃς ἂν οὖν ἐλθὼν διδάξῃ ὑμᾶς ταῦτα πάντα τὰ προειρημένα, δέξασθε αὐτόν· ἐὰν δὲ αὐτὸς ὁ διδάσκων στραφεὶς διδάσκῃ ἄλλην διδαχὴν εἰς τὸ καταλῦσαι, μὴ αὐτοῦ ἀκούσητε· εἰς δὲ τὸ προσθεῖναι δικαιοσύνην καὶ γνῶσιν κυρίου, δέξασθε αὐτὸν ὡς κύριον. Περὶ δὲ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ προφητῶν, κατὰ τὸ δόγμα τοῦ εὐαγγελίου οὕτω ποιήσατε. πᾶς δὲ ἀπόστολος ἐρχόμενος πρὸς ὑμᾶς δεχθήτω ὡς κύριος· οὐ μενεῖ δὲ εἰ μὴ ἡμέραν μίαν· ἐὰν δὲ ᾖ χρεία, καὶ τὴν ἄλλην· τρεῖς δὲ ἐὰν μείνῃ, ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστίν. ἐξερχόμενος δὲ ὁ ἀπόστολος μηδὲν λαμβανέτω εἰ μὴ ἄρτον, ἕως οὗ αὐλισθῇ· ἐὰν δὲ ἀργύριον αἰτῇ, ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστί. Καὶ πάντα προφήτην λαλοῦντα ἐν πνεύματι οὐ πειράσετε οὐδὲ διακρινεῖτε· πᾶσα γὰρ ἁμαρτία ἀφεθήσεται, αὕτη δὲ ἡ ἁμαρτία οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται. οὐ πᾶς δὲ ὁ λαλῶν ἐν πνεύματι προφήτης ἐστίν, ἀλλ’ ἐὰν ἔχῃ τοὺς τρόπους κυρίου. ἀπὸ οὖν τῶν τρόπων γνωσθήσεται ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης καὶ ὁ προφήτης. καὶ πᾶς προφήτης ὁρίζων τράπεζαν ἐν πνεύματι οὐ φάγεται ἀπ’ αὐτῆς, εἰ δὲ μήγε ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστί. πᾶς δὲ προφήτης διδάσκων τὴν ἀλήθειαν, εἰ ἃ διδάσκει οὐ ποιεῖ, ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστί. πᾶς δὲ προφήτης δεδοκιμασμένος, ἀληθινός, ποιῶν εἰς μυστήριον κοσμικὸν ἐκκλησίας, μὴ διδάσκων δὲ ποιεῖν ὅσα αὐτὸς ποιεῖ, οὐ κριθήσεται ἐφ’ ὑμῶν· μετὰ θεοῦ γὰρ ἔχει τὴν κρίσιν· ὡσαύτως γὰρ ἐποίησαν καὶ οἱ ἀρχαῖοι προφῆται. ὃς δ’ ἂν εἴπῃ ἐν πνεύματι· δός μοι ἀργύρια ἢ ἕτερά τινα, οὐκ ἀκούσεσθε αὐτοῦ· ἐὰν δὲ περὶ ἄλλων ὑστερούντων εἴπῃ δοῦναι, μηδεὶς αὐτὸν κρινέτω.

excerpts.author: Didache
english: Every true prophet who wants to settle among you is worthy of his food. Likewise a true teacher is himself worthy, like the worker, of his food.

Therefore take every firstfruit of the produce of winepress and threshing floor, of oxen and sheep, and give the firstfruit to the prophets; for they are your high priests. But if you have no prophet, give to the poor.
greek: Πᾶς δὲ προφήτης ἀληθινὸς θέλων καθῆσθαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἄξιός ἐστι τῆς τροφῆς αὐτοῦ. ὡσαύτως διδάσκαλος ἀληθινός ἐστιν ἄξιος καὶ αὐτὸς ὥσπερ ὁ ἐργάτης τῆς τροφῆς αὐτοῦ. πᾶσαν οὖν ἀπαρχὴν γεννημάτων ληνοῦ καὶ ἅλωνος, βοῶν τε καὶ προβάτων λαβὼν δώσεις τὴν ἀπαρχὴν τοῖς προφήταις· αὐτοὶ γάρ εἰσιν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ὑμῶν. ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἔχητε προφήτην, δότε τοῖς πτωχοῖς.

excerpts.author: Didache
english: Appoint for yourselves, then, bishops and deacons worthy of the Lord — men meek, not lovers of money, true, and proven; for they also perform for you the ministry of the prophets and teachers. Do not despise them; for they are the ones honored among you, together with the prophets and teachers.
greek: Χειροτονήσατε οὖν ἑαυτοῖς ἐπισκόπους καὶ διακόνους ἀξίους τοῦ κυρίου, ἄνδρας πραεῖς καὶ ἀφιλαργύρους καὶ ἀληθεῖς καὶ δεδοκιμασμένους· ὑμῖν γὰρ λειτουργοῦσι καὶ αὐτοὶ τὴν λειτουργίαν τῶν προφητῶν καὶ διδασκάλων. μὴ οὖν ὑπερίδητε αὐτούς· αὐτοὶ γάρ εἰσιν οἱ τετιμημένοι ὑμῶν μετὰ τῶν προφητῶν καὶ διδασκάλων.

excerpts.author: Hermas
english: He showed me people sitting on a bench, and another man sitting on a chair, and he says to me, “Do you see those sitting on the bench?” “I see them, Lord,” I say. “These,” he says, “are believers, and the one sitting on the chair is a false prophet who destroys the mind of the servants of God — of the double-minded, not of the faithful.”

These double-minded ones come to him as to a diviner and ask him what will happen to them; and that false prophet, having in himself no power of a divine spirit, speaks with them according to their questions and according to the desires of their wickedness, and fills their souls as they themselves wish. For being empty himself, he also answers empty things to the empty.

Every spirit given from God is not questioned, but having the power of the Godhead it speaks everything of itself, because it is from above, from the power of the divine Spirit. But the spirit that is questioned and speaks according to human desires is earthly and light, having no power; and it does not speak at all unless it is asked.

“How then,” I say, “Lord, will a person know which of them is a prophet and which a false prophet?” “Listen,” he says, “concerning both kinds of prophet… Test from the life the man who has the divine Spirit. First, the one who has the Spirit from above is gentle and quiet and humble-minded, and keeps away from every wickedness and vain desire of this age, and makes himself poorer than all people, and answers nothing to anyone when questioned, nor speaks alone, nor does the Holy Spirit speak when a person wants to speak; but then he speaks when God wants him to speak.

So when the man who has the divine Spirit comes into an assembly of righteous men who have faith of a divine Spirit, and prayer is made to God by that assembly, then the angel of the prophetic Spirit who rests upon him fills the man, and the man, filled with the Holy Spirit, speaks to the multitude as the Lord wills. In this way the Spirit of the Godhead will be clear.

Now listen concerning the earthly and empty spirit that has no power but is foolish. First, that man who thinks he has a spirit exalts himself and wants the first seat, and at once he is bold and shameless and talkative, living in many luxuries and many other deceits, and taking wages for his prophecy; if he does not receive, he does not prophesy. Can a divine spirit take wages and prophesy? It is not possible for a prophet of God to do this; but of such prophets the spirit is earthly.

Then he does not approach an assembly of righteous men at all, but flees from them; he clings to the double-minded and empty and prophesies to them in a corner and deceives them, speaking emptily according to their desires. But when he comes into an assembly full of righteous men who have a Spirit of Godhead, and prayer comes from them, that man is emptied, and the earthly spirit flees from him for fear, and that man is struck dumb and wholly shattered, able to say nothing.

You have the life of both kinds of prophet. Test, then, from works and life the man who says he is Spirit-bearing. Trust the Spirit that comes from God and has power; trust nothing in the earthly and empty spirit, for there is no power in it — for it comes from the devil.
greek: Ἔδειξέ μοι ἐπὶ συμψελλίου καθημένους ἀνθρώπους καὶ ἕτερον ἄνθρωπον καθήμενον ἐπὶ καθέδραν, καὶ λέγει μοι: Βλέπεις τοὺς ἐπὶ τοῦ συμψελλίου καθημένους; Βλέπω, φημί, κύριε. Οὗτοι, φησί, πιστοί εἰσι, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τὴν καθέδραν ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστίν, ὃς ἀπόλλυσι τὴν διάνοιαν τῶν δούλων τοῦ θεοῦ: τῶν διψύχων δὲ ἀπόλλυσιν, οὐ τῶν πιστῶν. οὗτοι οὖν οἱ δίψυχοι ὡς ἐπὶ μάντιν ἔρχονται καὶ ἐπερωτῶσιν αὐτόν, τί ἄρα ἔσται αὐτοῖς: κἀκεῖνος ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης, μηδεμίαν ἔχων ἐν ἑαυτῷ δύναμιν πνεύματος θείου, λαλεῖ μετ’ αὐτῶν κατὰ τὰ ἐπερωτήματα αὐτῶν καὶ κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς πονηρίας αὐτῶν καὶ πληροῖ τὰς ψυχὰς αὐτῶν, καθὼς αὐτοὶ βούλονται. αὐτὸς γὰρ κενὸς ὢν κενὰ καὶ ἀποκρίνεται κενοῖς: ὃ γὰρ ἐὰν ἐπερωτηθῇ, πρὸς τὸ κένωμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀποκρίνεται. τινὰ δὲ καὶ ῥήματα ἀληθῆ λαλεῖ: ὁ γὰρ διάβολος πληροῖ αὐτὸν τῷ αὐτοῦ πνεύματι, εἴ τινα δυνήσεται ῥῆξαι τῶν δικαίων. ὅσοι οὖν ἰσχυροί εἰσιν ἐν τῇ πίστει τοῦ κυρίου, ἐνδεδυμένοι τὴν ἀλήθειαν, τοῖς τοιούτοις πνεύμασιν οὐ κολλῶνται, ἀλλ’ ἀπέχονται ἀπ’ αὐτῶν: ὅσοι δὲ δίψυχοί εἰσι καὶ πυκνῶς μετανοοῦσι, μαντεύονται ὡς καὶ τὰ ἔθνη καὶ ἑαυτοῖς μείζονα ἁμαρτίαν ἐπιφέρουσιν εἰδωλολατροῦντες: ὁ γὰρ ἐπερωτῶν ψευδοπροφήτην περὶ πράξεώς τινος εἰδωλολάτρης ἐστὶ καὶ κενὸς ἀπὸ τῆς ἀληθείας καὶ ἄφρων. πᾶν γὰρ πνεῦμα ἀπὸ θεοῦ δοθὲν οὐκ ἐπερωτᾶται, ἀλλὰ ἔχον τὴν δύναμιν τῆς θεότητος ἀφ̓ ἑαυτοῦ λαλεῖ πάντα, ὅτι ἄνωθέν ἐστιν ἀπὸ τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ θείου πνεύματος. τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα τὸ ἐπερωτώμενον καὶ λαλοῦν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐπίγειόν ἐστι καὶ ἐλαφρόν, δύναμιν μὴ ἔχον: καὶ ὅλως οὐ λαλεῖ, ἐὰν μὴ ἐπερωτηθῇ. Πῶς οὖν, φημί, κύριε, ἄνθρωπος γνώσεται, τίς αὐτῶν προφήτης καὶ τίς ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστίν; Ἄκουε, φησί, περὶ ἀμφοτέρων τῶν προφητῶν: καὶ ὥς σοι μέλλω λέγειν, οὕτω δοκιμάσεις τὸν προφήτην καὶ τὸν ψευδοπροφήτην. ἀπὸ τῆς ζωῆς δοκίμαζε τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν ἔχοντα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἄνωθεν πραΰς ἐστι καὶ ἡσύχιος και ταπεινόφρων καὶ ἀπεχόμενος ἀπὸ πάσης πονηρίας καὶ ἐπιθυμίας ματαίας τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου καὶ ἑαυτὸν ἐνδεέστερον ποιεῖ πάντων τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ οὐδενὶ οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνεται ἐπερωτώμενος, οὐδὲ καταμόνας λαλεῖ, οὐδὲ ὅταν θέλῃ ἄνθρωπος λαλεῖν, λαλεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, ἀλλὰ τότε λαλεῖ, ὅταν θελήσῃ αὐτὸν ὁ θεὸς λαλῆσαι. ὅταν οὖν ἔλθῃ ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων τῶν ἐχόντων πίστιν θείου πνεύματος καὶ ἔντευξις γένηται πρὸς τὸν θεὸν τῆς συναγωγῆς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐκείνων, τότε ὁ ἄγγελος τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος ὁ κείμενος πρὸς αὐτὸν πληροῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, καὶ πληρωθεὶς ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ λαλεῖ εἰς τὸ πλῆθος, καθὼς ὁ κύριος βούλεται. οὕτως οὖν φανερὸν ἔσται τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς θεότητος. ὅση οὖν περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς θεότητος τοῦ κυρίου ἡ δύναμις αὕτη. ἄκουε νῦν, φησί, περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐπιγείου καὶ κενοῦ καὶ δύναμιν μὴ ἔχοντος, ἀλλὰ ὄντος μωροῦ. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὁ δοκῶν πνεῦμα ἔχειν ὑψοῖ ἑαυτὸν καὶ θέλει πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἔχειν, καὶ εὐθὺς ἰταμός ἐστι καὶ ἀναιδὴς καὶ πολύλαλος καὶ ἐν τρυφαῖς πολλαῖς ἀναστρεφόμενος καὶ ἐν ἑτέραις πολλαῖς ἀπάταις καὶ μισθοὺς λαμβάνων τῆς προφητείας αὐτοῦ: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ λάβῃ, οὐ προφητεύει. δύναται οὖν πνεῦμα θεῖον μισθοὺς λαμβάνειν καὶ προφητεύειν; οὐκ ἐνδέχεται τοῦτο ποιεῖν θεοῦ προφήτην, ἀλλὰ τῶν τοιούτων προφητῶν ἐπίγειόν ἐστι τὸ πνεῦμα. εἶτα ὅλως εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων οὐκ ἐγγίζει, ἀλλ’ ἀποφεύγει αὐτούς: κολλᾶται δὲ τοῖς διψύχοις καὶ κενοῖς καὶ κατὰ γωνίαν αὐτοῖς προφητεύει καὶ ἀπατᾷ αὐτοὺς λαλῶν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας αὐτῶν πάντα κενῶς: κενοῖς γὰρ καὶ ἀποκρίνεται: τὸ γὰρ κενὸν σκεῦος μετὰ τῶν κενῶν συντιθέμενον οὐ θραύεται, ἀλλὰ συμφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις. ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ εἰς συναγωγὴν πλήρη ἀνδρῶν δικαίων ἐχόντων πνεῦμα θεότητος καὶ ἔντευξις ἀπ’ αὐτῶν γένηται, κενοῦται ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος, καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἐπίγειον ἀπὸ τοῦ φόβου φεύγει ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ κωφοῦται ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος καὶ ὅλως συνθραύεται, μηδὲν δυνάμενος λαλῆσαι. ἐὰν γὰρ εἰς ἀποθήκην στιβάσῃς οἶνον ἢ ἔλαιον καὶ ἐν αὐτοῖς θῇς κεράμιον κενόν, καὶ πάλιν ἀποστιβάσαι θελήσῃς τὴν ἀποθήκην, τὸ κεράμιον ἐκεῖνο, ὃ ἔθηκας κενόν, κενὸν καὶ εὑρήσεις: οὕτω καὶ οἱ προφῆται οἱ κενοὶ ὅταν ἔλθωσιν εἰς πνεύματα δικαίων, ὁποῖοι ἦλθον, τοιοῦτοι καὶ εὑρίσκονται. ἔχεις ἀμφοτέρων τῶν προφητῶν τὴν ζωήν. δοκίμαζε οὖν ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων καὶ τῆς ζωῆς τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν λέγοντα ἑαυτὸν πνευματοφόρον εἶναι. σὺ δὲ πίστευε τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἐρχομένῳ ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἔχοντι δύναμιν· τῷ δὲ πνεύματι τῷ ἐπιγείῳ καὶ κενῷ μηδὲν πίστευε, ὅτι ἐν αὐτῷ δύναμις οὐκ ἔστιν· ἀπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου γὰρ ἔρχεται.
translator_notes: New English from locked Greek. Core ante-Nicene test of prophetic gift vs paid/corner ‘prophecy’.
πνευματοφόρον = Spirit-bearing.

added_allusions.reason: Prophecy ordered in the assembly, not chaos.

notes: Promoted 2026-09-10 for gifts-and-order enrichment.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: But him we worship and adore — and the Son who came from him and taught us these things, and the army of the other good angels who follow and are made like him — and the prophetic Spirit, honoring them in word and truth, and freely handing on to everyone who wants to learn what we were taught.
greek: ἀλλ’ ἐκεῖνόν τε καὶ παρ’ αὐτοῦ υἱὸν ἐλθόντα καὶ διδάξαντα ἡμᾶς ταῦτα, καὶ τὸν τῶν ἄλλων ἑπομένων καὶ ἐξομοιουμένων ἀγαθῶν ἀγγέλων στρατόν, πνεῦμά τε τὸ προφητικὸν σεβόμεθα καὶ προσκυνοῦμεν, λόγῳ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ τιμῶντες, καὶ παντὶ βουλομένῳ μαθεῖν, ὡς ἐδιδάχθημεν, ἀφθόνως παραδιδόντες.
translator_notes: New English from locked Greek. Justin’s triad includes worship of the prophetic Spirit — foundation for charismata talk.
notes: Promoted 2026-09-10; bridges spirit-prophecy and gifts-and-order.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
excerpts.source: Harvey ed. of Irenaeus (origin scan uncommitted 2026-10-02; original-language text in-record)
english: For some truly and firmly drive out demons, so that those cleansed from the evil spirits often even believe and are in the church. Others also have foreknowledge of things to come, and visions, and prophetic utterances. Others heal those who are sick by the laying on of hands, and restore them to health. And already, as we have said, the dead have been raised and have remained with us for a good many years.

And why not? It is not possible to state the number of the gifts which the church, having received from God throughout the whole world in the name of Jesus Christ who was crucified under Pontius Pilate, performs each day for the benefit of the nations — neither deceiving anyone nor taking money. For as she received freely from God, she also ministers freely.
greek: Οἱ μὲν γὰρ δαίμονας ἐλαύνουσι βεβαίως καὶ ἀληθῶς, ὥστε πολλάκις καὶ πιστεύειν αὐτοὺς ἐκείνους τοὺς καθαρισθέντας ἀπὸ τῶν πονηρῶν πνευμάτων, καὶ εἶναι ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ. Οἱ δὲ καὶ πρόγνωσιν ἔχουσι τῶν μελλόντων, καὶ ὀπτασίας, καὶ ῥήσεις προφητικάς. Ἄλλοι δὲ τοὺς κάμνοντας διὰ τῆς τῶν χειρῶν ἐπιθέσεως ἰῶνται, καὶ ὑγιεῖς ἀποκαθιστᾶσιν. Ἤδη δέ, καθὼς ἔφαμεν, καὶ νεκροὶ ἠγέρθησαν, καὶ παρέμειναν σὺν ἡμῖν ἱκανοῖς ἔτεσι. Καὶ τί γάρ; οὐκ ἔστιν ἀριθμὸν εἰπεῖν τῶν χαρισμάτων, ὧν κατὰ παντὸς τοῦ κόσμου ἡ ἐκκλησία παρὰ Θεοῦ λαβοῦσα, ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦ σταυρωθέντος ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτου, ἑκάστης ἡμέρας ἐπ’ εὐεργεσίᾳ τῇ τῶν ἐθνῶν ἐπιτελεῖ, μήτε ἐξαπατῶσα τινάς, μήτε ἐξαργυριζομένη. Ὡς γὰρ δωρεὰν εἴληφε παρὰ Θεοῦ, δωρεὰν καὶ διακονεῖ.
translator_notes: New English from Harvey’s Greek of AH 2.32.4 (Mass. numbering). Classic witness that χαρίσματα still operate in the churches of Irenaeus’s day.
δωρεὰν…δωρεὰν = freely…freely (cf. Matt 10:8).

added_allusions.reason: Varieties of gifts from one Spirit.

notes: Promoted 2026-09-10 for gifts-and-order enrichment.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
excerpts.source: Harvey ed. of Irenaeus vol. 2 (origin scan uncommitted 2026-10-02; NEEDS RE-SOURCING: no original-language text attached)
english: But others, so that they may frustrate the gift of the Spirit which in the last times according to the Father’s good pleasure has been poured out on the human race, do not admit that form which is according to John’s Gospel, in which the Lord promised that he would send the Paraclete; but they reject both the Gospel and the prophetic Spirit together.

Truly wretched are those who want to be false prophets, yet drive the grace of prophecy away from the church. … For in the letter to the Corinthians Paul spoke carefully about prophetic gifts, and he knows men and women prophesying in the church.
latin: Alii vero ut donum Spiritus frustrentur, quod in novissimis temporibus secundum placitum Patris effusum est in humanum genus, illam speciem non admittunt, quae est secundum Johannis Evangelium, in qua Paracletum se missurum Dominus promisit; sed simul et Evangelium, et propheticum repellunt Spiritum. Infelices vere, qui pseudoprophetae quidem esse volunt, prophetiae vero gratiam repellunt ab Ecclesia… In ea enim Epistola quae est ad Corinthios, de propheticis charismatibus diligenter locutus est, et scit viros et mulieres in Ecclesia prophetantes.
translator_notes: New English from Harvey Latin AH 3.11.9. Aimed at those who claim prophecy while emptying the church of the gift — Montanist/anti-Johannine edge labeled as debate in topics.yml.

added_allusions.reason: Spirit poured out in last days.

notes: Promoted 2026-09-10; Montanism debate locus.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
excerpts.source: Harvey ed. of Irenaeus vol. 2 (origin scan uncommitted 2026-10-02; NEEDS RE-SOURCING: no original-language text attached)
english: God has placed in the church first apostles, second prophets, third teachers. Where the gifts of the Lord are placed, therefore, there one ought to learn the truth — among those with whom there is the succession of the church from the apostles, and what is sound and blameless in way of life, and what stands unadulterated and incorruptible in speech.
latin: Posuit Deus in Ecclesia primo Apostolos, secundo prophetas, tertio doctores. Ubi igitur charismata Domini posita sunt, ibi discere oportet veritatem, apud quos est ea quae est ab Apostolis Ecclesiae successio, et id quod est sanum et irreprobabile conversationis, et inadulteratum et incorruptibile sermonis constat.
translator_notes: New English from Harvey Latin (Mass. 4.26.5 / Harvey CAP. XLII). Charismata located with apostolic succession — gifts with order.
Locus numbering follows Massuet commonly cited as 4.26.5.
notes: Promoted 2026-09-10 for gifts-and-order enrichment.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
excerpts.source: Harvey ed. of Irenaeus vol. 2 (origin scan uncommitted 2026-10-02; original-language text in-record)
english: Just as we also hear of many brothers in the church who have prophetic gifts, and who through the Spirit speak in all kinds of tongues, and bring the secrets of people into the open for benefit, and explain the mysteries of God.
greek: καθὼς καὶ πολλῶν ἀκούομεν ἀδελφῶν ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ, προφητικὰ χαρίσματα ἐχόντων, καὶ παντοδαπαῖς λαλούντων διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος γλώσσαις, καὶ τὰ κρύφια τῶν ἀνθρώπων εἰς φανερὸν ἀγόντων ἐπὶ τὸ συμφέρον, καὶ τὰ μυστήρια τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐκδιηγουμένων.
translator_notes: New English from Harvey Greek of AH 5.6.1 (also in Eusebius HE 5.7). Living prophetic χαρίσματα and tongues in Irenaeus’s hearing.

added_allusions.reason: Secrets of the heart made plain.

notes: Promoted 2026-09-10 for gifts-and-order enrichment.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
excerpts.source: Harvey ed. of Irenaeus vol. 2 (origin scan uncommitted 2026-10-02; NEEDS RE-SOURCING: no original-language text attached)
english: But now we receive some portion from his Spirit, toward perfection and preparation for incorruption, gradually becoming accustomed to receive and carry God — which the Apostle also called a pledge…

If therefore, now having the pledge, we cry “Abba, Father,” what will it be when, rising, we see him face to face…? For if the pledge, embracing the human being into itself, already makes us say “Abba, Father,” what will the whole grace of the Spirit do, which will be given to human beings by God? It will make us like him, and will perfect us by the Father’s will; for it will make the human being according to the image and likeness of God.
latin: Nunc autem partem aliquam a Spiritu ejus sumimus, ad perfectionem et praeparationem incorruptele, paulatim assuescentes capere et portare Deum: quod et pignus dixit Apostolus… Si igitur nunc pignus habentes clamamus, Abba Pater; quid fiet quando resurgentes faciem ad faciem videbimus eum… Si enim pignus complectens hominem in semetipsum, jam facit dicere, Abba Pater, quid faciet universa Spiritus gratia, quae hominibus dabitur a Deo? similes nos ei efficiet, et perficiet voluntate Patris; efficiet enim hominem secundum imaginem et similitudinem Dei.
translator_notes: New English from Harvey Latin AH 5.8.1. Present gifts as pledge (ἀρραβών) of the Spirit’s full grace.
notes: Promoted 2026-09-10; links gifts to eschatological fullness.

excerpts.author: Tertullian
english: Hear now how he also announced that gifts would come after Christ was received into heaven: “He ascended on high… he gave gifts to the sons of men” — that is, the grants which we call charismata.
And now also that promise of the Spirit stands fulfilled which was made through Joel: “In the last times I will pour out of my Spirit on all flesh, and their sons and daughters shall prophesy…”

Compare, then, the kinds named by the Apostle and by Isaiah. “To one,” he says, “is given through the Spirit a word of wisdom” — at once Isaiah also placed a spirit of wisdom; to another a word of knowledge… to another faith in the same Spirit… to another gifts of healings, to another workings of powers… to another prophecy, to another distinguishing of spirits, to another kinds of tongues, to another interpretation of tongues…

I can say: the very fact that he matched the unity of our body through many and diverse members to the fitting-together of various gifts shows the same Lord of the human body and of the Holy Spirit — who did not want the rankings of gifts in the Spirit’s body to be what he also did not place among the members in the human body — and who also instructed the Apostle that love is to be preferred to all the gifts.
latin: accipe nunc, quomodo et a Christo in caelum recepto charismata obuentura pronuntiarit: ascendit in sublimitatem… data dedit filiis hominum, id est donatiua, quae charismata dicimus… iam nunc et illa promissio spiritus absoluta, facta per Iohelem: in nouissimis temporibus effundam de meo spiritu in omnem carnem, et prophetabunt filii filiaeque eorum… compara denique species apostoli et Esaiae. alii, inquit, datur per spiritum sermo sapientiae… alii sermo scientiae… alii fides in eodem spiritu… alii donum curationum, alii uirtutum… alii prophetia, alii distinctio spirituum, alii genera linguarum, alii interpretatio linguarum… ipsum quod corporis nostri per multa et diuersa membra unitatem charismatum uariorum compagini adaequauit, eundem et corporis humani et spiritus sancti dominum ostendit… qui de dilectione quoque omnibus charismatibus praeponenda apostolum instruxerit.
translator_notes: New English from CCL/Kroymann Latin Adv. Marc. 5.8. Catalog of charismata tied to Creator’s Spirit vs Marcion; love above gifts.

added_allusions.reason: Spirit poured out; sons and daughters prophesy.

notes: Promoted 2026-09-10 for gifts-and-order enrichment.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: Ignatius, also called God-bearer, to the church of God the Father and of the beloved Jesus Christ, which has been shown mercy in every gift, filled with faith and love, lacking in no gift, most God-fitting and bearing what is holy — the church that is in Smyrna of Asia — abundant greeting in a blameless Spirit and in the word of God.
greek: Ἰγνάτιος, ὁ καὶ Θεοφόρος, ἐκκλησίᾳ θεοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ ἠγαπημένου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἠλεημένῃ ἐν παντὶ χαρίσματι, πεπληρωμένῃ ἐν πίστει καὶ ἀγάπῃ, ἀνυστερήτῳ οὔσῃ παντὸς χαρίσματος, θεοπρεπεστάτῃ καὶ ἁγιοφόρῳ, τῇ οὔσῃ ἐν Σμύρνῃ τῆς Ἀσίας. ἐν ἀμώμῳ πνεύματι καὶ λόγῳ θεοῦ πλεῖστα χαίρειν.
translator_notes: New English from locked Greek. παντὸς χαρίσματος = every gift/charism — church already described as gift-filled.
notes: Wave 2026-09-10 gifts expansion.

excerpts.author: Clement of Alexandria
english: Again: “To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good. To one is given through the Spirit a word of wisdom, to another a word of knowledge according to the same Spirit, to another faith in the same Spirit, to another gifts of healings in the same Spirit, to another workings of powers, to another prophecy, to another discerning of spirits, to another kinds of tongues, to another interpretation of tongues; but all these the one and the same Spirit works, distributing to each individually as he wills.”

Things being so, the prophets are perfect in prophecy, the righteous in righteousness, and the martyrs in confession, and others in proclamation — not without share in the common virtues, yet succeeding in what they were appointed to.
greek: πάλιν τε αὖ ἑκάστῳ δίδοται ἡ φανέρωσις τοῦ πνεύματος πρὸς τὸ συμφέρον. ᾧ μὲν γὰρ δίδοται διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος λόγος σοφίας, ἄλλῳ δὲ λόγος γνώσεως κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα, ἑτέρῳ πίστις ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ πνεύματι, ἄλλῳ δὲ χαρίσματα ἰαμάτων ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ πνεύματι, ἄλλῳ δὲ ἐνεργήματα δυνάμεων, ἄλλῳ προφητεία, ἄλλῳ διάκρισις πνευμάτων, ἑτέρῳ γένη γλωσσῶν, ἄλλῳ δὲ ἑρμηνεία γλωσσῶν· πάντα δὲ ταῦτα ἐνεργεῖ τὸ ἓν καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα, διαιροῦν ἰδίᾳ ἑκάστῳ καθὼς βούλεται. ὧν οὕτως ἐχόντων οἱ μὲν προφῆται ἐν προφητείᾳ τέλειοι, οἱ δίκαιοι δὲ ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ οἱ μάρτυρες ἐν ὁμολογίᾳ, ἄλλοι δὲ ἐν κηρύγματι, οὐκ ἀμέτοχοι μὲν τῶν κοινῶν ἀρετῶν, κατορθοῦντες δὲ ἐν οἷς ἐτάχθησαν.
translator_notes: New English from locked Greek citing 1 Cor 12; Clement distributes perfection by appointed gift without denying common virtues.
notes: Wave 2026-09-10 gifts expansion.

excerpts.author: Tertullian
english: But we also ascribe bodily lines to the soul, not only from confidence in its bodily nature by estimation, but also from the constancy of grace by revelation. For because we acknowledge spiritual gifts, we have also been granted to receive prophecy after John.

There is today among us a sister who has obtained gifts of revelations, which she suffers in the Spirit through ecstasy in the church amid the Lord’s solemnities. She converses with angels, sometimes also with the Lord; she both sees and hears sacred things, discerns the hearts of some, and takes medicines for those who desire them. Indeed, as the Scriptures are read or psalms are sung or addresses are offered or petitions are delegated, from these the materials for visions are supplied.

After the solemnities were finished and the people dismissed, by the custom in which she usually reports to us what she has seen (for these things are also carefully recorded so that they may even be tested), she said among the rest: “The soul was shown to me corporeally…” And God is witness, and the apostle is a fit surety of gifts that will be in the church.
latin: Sed nos corporales quoque illi inscribimus lineas, non tantum ex fiducia corporalitatis per aestimationem, uerum et ex constantia gratiae per reuelationem. Nam quia spiritalia charismata agnoscimus, post Iohannem quoque prophetiam meruimus consequi. Est hodie soror apud nos reuelationum charismata sortita, quas in ecclesia inter dominica sollemnia per ecstasin in spiritu patitur; conuersatur cum angelis, aliquando etiam cum domino, et uidet et audit sacramenta et quorundam corda dinoscit et medicinas desiderantibus sumit. Iamuero prout scripturae leguntur aut psalmi canuntur aut allocutiones proferuntur aut petitiones delegantur, ita inde materiae uisionibus subministrantur. … Post transacta sollemnia dimissa plebe, quo usu solet nobis renuntiare quae uiderit (nam et diligentissime digeruntur, ut etiam probentur)… Et deus testis et apostolus charismatum in ecclesia futurorum idoneus sponsor.
translator_notes: New English from locked Latin (tertullian.org). Montanist-era witness: living revelation-gifts in assembled worship, tested by record.
Label Montanism as debate in topics.yml — do not hide the New Prophecy context.

added_allusions.reason: Prophecy after the apostolic age claimed.

excerpts.author: Novatian
english: This is the one who strengthened their minds and thoughts, who distinguished the gospel mysteries, who was in them the illuminator of divine things — by whom, confirmed for the Lord’s name, they feared neither prisons nor chains; rather they trampled the powers of the age and its torments, already armed and strengthened through him, having in themselves the gifts which this same Spirit distributes and directs to the church, the bride of Christ, as certain ornaments.

This is the one who appoints prophets in the church, trains teachers, directs tongues, works powers and healings, performs wonderful works, extends discernings of spirits, contributes governances, suggests counsels, and arranges and distributes whatever other gifts of the charismata there are — and therefore makes the Lord’s church perfect and complete on every side and in all things.
latin: Hic est enim qui ipsorum animos mentesque firmauit, qui euangelica sacramenta distinxit, qui in ipsis illuminator rerum diuinarum fuit, quo confirmati pro nomine Domini nec carceres nec uincula timuerunt… habentes in se dona quae hic idem Spiritus ecclesiae Christi sponsae quasi quaedam ornamenta distribuit et dirigit. Hic est enim qui prophetas in ecclesia constituit, magistros erudit, linguas dirigit, uirtutes et sanitates facit, opera mirabilia gerit, discretiones spirituum porrigit, gubernationes contribuit, consilia suggerit quaeque alia sunt charismatum dona componit et digerit et ideo ecclesiam Domini undique et in omnibus perfectam et consummatam facit.
translator_notes: New English from locked Latin. Full 1 Cor 12-style catalog attributed to the Spirit’s ongoing work in the church.

excerpts.citation: Cyprian — On the Unity of the Church 15
excerpts.author: Cyprian
excerpts.work: On the Unity of the Church
excerpts.source: Cyprian, De unitate scan (origin scan uncommitted 2026-10-02; NEEDS RE-SOURCING: no original-language text attached)
english: For to prophesy and to cast out demons and to do great powers on earth is indeed a lofty and wonderful thing; yet whoever is found in all these does not obtain the heavenly kingdom unless he walks by keeping to the observation of the right and just path.

The Lord declares and says: “Many will say to me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and cast out demons in your name, and do many mighty works in your name?’ And then I will say to them, ‘I never knew you; depart from me, you who work iniquity.’”
Work of righteousness is needed, that one may be able to deserve God the Judge; his precepts and warnings must be obeyed, that our merits may receive their wage.
latin: Nam et prophetare et daemonia excludere et virtutes magnas in terris facere sublimis utique et admirabilis res est, non tamen regnum coeleste consequitur, quisquis in his omnibus invenitur, nisi recti et iusti itineris observatione gradiatur. Denuntiat Dominus et dicit: Multi mihi dicent in illo die: Domine, Domine, nonne in tuo nomine prophetavimus et in tuo nomine daemonia exclusimus et in nomine tuo virtutes magnas fecimus? Et tunc dicam illis: Nunquam vos cognovi, recedite a me, qui operamini iniquitatem.
translator_notes: New English from locked Latin. Gifts without unity/obedience do not save — gifts under moral and ecclesial order.

added_allusions.reason: Prophecy and powers without being known by the Lord.

notes: Wave 2026-09-10 gifts expansion.

excerpts.citation: Origen — Against Celsus (on gifts of healings)
excerpts.author: Origen
english: But the apostles also, performing gifts of healings and workings of powers, by that very working were doing goods for human beings and freeing them from evils.

excerpts.author: Eusebius of Caesarea
english: And he also writes that prophetic gifts shone in the church even up to his own time; and he mentions John’s Apocalypse, saying clearly that it is the apostle’s…
greek: Γράφει δὲ καὶ ὡς ὅτι μέχρι καὶ αὐτοῦ χαρίσματα προφητικὰ διέλαμπεν ἐπὶ τῆς ἐκκλησίας, μέμνηταί τε τῆς Ἰωάννου Ἀποκαλύψεως, σαφῶς τοῦ ἀποστόλου αὐτὴν εἶναι λέγων.

excerpts.author: Eusebius of Caesarea
excerpts.source: Routh, Reliquiae Sacrae vol. 1 (origin scan uncommitted 2026-10-02; original-language text in-record)
english: When those around Montanus and Alcibiades and Theodotus in Phrygia were then first putting out among many the opinion about prophesying — for very many other marvelous works of the divine gift were still at that time being performed in various churches, and this was giving many people faith that those men also prophesied — and since there was disagreement about the matters declared, again the brothers in Gaul set out their own judgment about these things also, a cautious and most orthodox one…
greek: Τῶν δ᾽ ἀμφὶ τὸν Μοντανὸν καὶ Ἀλκιβιάδην καὶ Θεόδοτον, περὶ τὴν Φρυγίαν ἄρτι τότε πρῶτον τὴν περὶ τοῦ προφητεύειν ὑπόληψιν παρὰ πολλοῖς ἐκφερομένων· πλεῖσται γὰρ οὖν καὶ ἄλλαι παραδοξοποιΐαι τοῦ θείου χαρίσματος εἰσέτι τότε κατὰ διαφόρους ἐκκλησίας ἐκτελούμεναι, πίστιν παρὰ πολλοῖς τοῦ κἀκείνους προφητεύειν παρεῖχον· καὶ δὴ διαφωνίας ὑπαρχούσης περὶ τῶν δεδηλωμένων, αὖθις οἱ κατὰ τὴν Γαλλίαν ἀδελφοί, τὴν ἰδίαν κρίσιν καὶ περὶ τούτων, εὐλαβῆ καὶ ὀρθοδοξοτάτην ὑποτάττουσιν.
translator_notes: New English from Routh/Eusebius Greek. Key: divine χάρισμα still performed in many churches while Montanist prophecy claims are disputed.
notes: Wave 2026-09-10. Montanism debate locus.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
excerpts.source: Harvey ed. of Irenaeus vol. 2 (origin scan uncommitted 2026-10-02; NEEDS RE-SOURCING: no original-language text attached)
english: For some of them saw the prophetic Spirit and his operations poured out into all kinds of gifts; but others saw the coming of the Lord and the administration that is from the beginning…
latin: Quidam enim eorum videbant Spiritum propheticum et operationes ejus in omnia genera charismatum effusas: alii vero adventum Domini, et eam quae est ab initio administrationem.
translator_notes: New English from Harvey Latin. Prophetic Spirit’s operations poured into all kinds of charismata.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: …knowing that still day by day some are being discipled into the name of his Christ and leaving the way of error, who also receive gifts, each as they are worthy, being enlightened through the name of this Christ: for one receives a spirit of understanding, another of counsel, another of strength, another of healing, another of foreknowledge, another of teaching, another of fear of God.

And I said to him: “Listen, sir… after Christ’s ascent into heaven it was prophesied that he would take us captive from error and give us gifts. And these are the words: ‘He ascended on high, he led captivity captive, he gave gifts to human beings.’ We who have received gifts from the Christ who ascended on high therefore show from the prophetic words that you… are without understanding…”
greek: γινώσκων ἔτι καθʼ ἡμέραν τινὰς μαθητευομένους εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπολείποντας τὴν ὁδὸν τῆς πλάνης, οἳ καὶ λαμβάνουσι δόματα ἕκαστος ὡς ἄξιοί εἰσι, φωτιζόμενοι διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ τούτου· ὁ μὲν γὰρ λαμβάνει συνέσεως πνεῦμα, ὁ δὲ βουλῆς, ὁ δὲ ἰσχύος, ὁ δὲ ἰάσεως, ὁ δὲ προγνώσεως, ὁ δὲ διδασκαλίας, ὁ δὲ φόβου θεοῦ. … μετὰ τὴν τοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀνέλευσιν προεφητεύθη αἰχμαλωτεῦσαι αὐτὸν ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τῆς πλάνης καὶ δοῦναι ἡμῖν δόματα. Εἰσὶ δὲ οἱ λόγοι οὗτοι· Ἀνέβη εἰς ὕψος, ᾐχμαλώτευσεν αἰχμαλωσίαν, ἔδωκε δόματα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις.
translator_notes: New English from Perseus/First1KGreek Dialogue. Living gifts after the Ascension: healing, foreknowledge, teaching, etc.
notes: Wave 2026-09-10 Justin Dialogue lock.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: For among us even until now there are prophetic gifts; from which you yourselves ought also to understand that what of old was in your nation has been transferred to us.

And just as there were also false prophets in the time of the holy prophets who arose among you, so among us now there are also many false teachers, whom our Lord foretold that we should guard against…
greek: Παρὰ γὰρ ἡμῖν καὶ μέχρι νῦν προφητικὰ χαρίσματά ἐστιν, ἐξ οὗ καὶ αὐτοὶ συνιέναι ὀφείλετε, ὅτι τὰ πάλαι ἐν τῷ γένει ὑμῶν ὄντα εἰς ἡμᾶς μετετέθη. Ὅνπερ δὲ τρόπον καὶ ψευδοπροφῆται ἐπὶ τῶν παρʼ ὑμῖν γενομένων ἁγίων προφητῶν ἦσαν, καὶ παρʼ ἡμῖν νῦν πολλοί εἰσι καὶ ψευδοδιδάσκαλοι, οὓς φυλάσσεσθαι προεῖπεν ἡμῖν ὁ ἡμέτερος κύριος…
translator_notes: New English from locked Greek. Classic μέχρι νῦν — prophetic gifts still present; false teachers also present.
notes: Wave 2026-09-10 Justin Dialogue lock.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: And among us it is possible to see both females and males who have gifts from the Spirit of God. So it was not because he was lacking in power that it was prophesied the powers numbered by Isaiah would come upon him, but because they were no longer going to be beyond him.
greek: Καὶ παρʼ ἡμῖν ἔστιν ἰδεῖν καὶ θηλείας καὶ ἄρσενας, χαρίσματα ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ θεοῦ ἔχοντας. Ὥστε οὐ διὰ τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐνδεῆ δυνάμεως ἐπεπροφήτευτο ἐλεύσεσθαι ἐπʼ αὐτὸν τὰς δυνάμεις τὰς κατηριθμημένας ὑπὸ Ἡσαΐου, ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸ ἐπέκεινα μὴ μέλλειν ἔσεσθαι.
translator_notes: New English from locked Greek. Men and women visibly holding Spirit-gifts in Justin’s churches.

added_allusions.reason: Powers of the Spirit numbered by Isaiah.

notes: Wave 2026-09-10 Justin Dialogue lock.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: The Word does not say these numbered powers of the Spirit came upon him as though he lacked them, but as about to make their rest upon him — that is, to make an end in him — so that prophets would no longer arise in your nation according to the old custom, which you can also see with your eyes: for after him no prophet at all has arisen among you.
greek: Ταύτας τὰς κατηριθμημένας τοῦ πνεύματος δυνάμεις οὐχ ὡς ἐνδεοῦς αὐτοῦ τούτων ὄντος φησὶν ὁ λόγος ἐπεληλυθέναι ἐπʼ αὐτόν, ἀλλʼ ὡς ἐπʼ ἐκεῖνον ἀνάπαυσιν μελλούσας ποιεῖσθαι, τουτέστιν ἐπʼ αὐτοῦ πέρας ποιεῖσθαι, τοῦ μηκέτι ἐν τῷ γένει ὑμῶν κατὰ τὸ παλαιὸν ἔθος προφήτας γενήσεσθαι, ὅπερ καὶ ὄψει ὑμῖν ἰδεῖν ἔστι· μετʼ ἐκεῖνον γὰρ οὐδεὶς ὅλως προφήτης παρʼ ὑμῖν γεγένηται.
translator_notes: Pairs with Dial 82/88: prophetic powers rest in Christ and transfer; Jewish succession of prophets ends while church gifts continue.

added_allusions.reason: Spirit powers resting on the shoot of Jesse.

excerpts.author: John Chrysostom
excerpts.source: Field ed. of Chrysostom, 1 Corinthians homilies (origin scan uncommitted 2026-10-02; original-language text in-record)
english: Why then does it not happen now? … What then used to happen then? If someone was baptized, he immediately spoke in tongues — and not in tongues only, but many also prophesied, and some displayed still more powers.

For those coming from the idols, knowing nothing clearly and not raised on the old books, when baptized immediately received the Spirit; but they did not see the Spirit (for it is invisible), so the grace gave a perceptible proof of that working: one spoke at once in the Persian tongue, another in the Roman, another in the Indian, another in some other such language — and this made plain to outsiders that there was a Spirit in the one speaking.

And they had gifts, some lesser, some greater. Yet among them the gift of tongues was more than all — and this became a cause of schism for them, not from its own nature, but from the ungraciousness of those who received it.
greek: Τί δήποτε γὰρ τότε μὲν ἐγίνετο, νῦν δὲ οὐκέτι; … Τί οὖν τότε συνέβαινεν; Εἴ τις ἐβαπτίσατο, γλώσσαις εὐθέως ἐλάλει, καὶ οὐ γλώσσαις μόνον, ἀλλὰ πολλοὶ καὶ προεφήτευον, τινὲς δὲ καὶ ἑτέρας πλείους δυνάμεις ἐπεδείκνυντο. … καὶ ὁ μὲν τῇ Περσῶν, ὁ δὲ τῇ Ῥωμαίων, ὁ δὲ τῇ Ἰνδῶν, ὁ δὲ ἑτέρᾳ τινὶ τοιαύτῃ εὐθέως ἐφθέγγετο γλώσσῃ· καὶ τοῦτο ἐφανέρου τοῖς ἔξωθεν, ὅτι πνεῦμα ἐστιν ἐν αὐτῷ τῷ φθεγγομένῳ. … καὶ χαρίσματα δὲ εἶχον, οἱ μὲν ἐλάττονα, οἱ δὲ μείζονα. Πλέον δὲ πάντων τὸ τῶν γλωσσῶν ἦν παρ’ αὐτοῖς χάρισμα. Καὶ τοῦτο αἴτιον σχίσματος αὐτοῖς ἐγένετο, οὐ παρὰ τὴν οἰκείαν φύσιν, ἀλλὰ παρὰ τὴν ἀγνωμοσύνην τῶν εἰληφότων.
translator_notes: New English from Field 1847 Greek OCR (cleaned). Landmark 4th-c. claim: baptismal tongues/prophecy were then common; Chrysostom asks why not now — Explore rupture toward later cessation talk.
OCR noise corrected conservatively against sense; re-check Field PDF before source_verified.

added_allusions.reason: On spiritual gifts / manifestation of the Spirit.

notes: Wave 2026-09-10 post-Nicene gifts expansion (~390).

excerpts.author: John Chrysostom
excerpts.source: Field ed. of Chrysostom, 1 Corinthians homilies (origin scan uncommitted 2026-10-02; original-language text in-record)
english: Therefore they also received discernings of spirits, so as to discern and know who speaks by a pure spirit and who by an unclean one. For it was not possible to give proof of the things said on the spot — prophecy does not furnish the test of its own truth at the time it is spoken, but at the time of the outcome…

And the prophet is not like the diviner, but with sober mind and self-control and composure, knowing what he utters, he says everything. So even before the outcome you may recognize from this the diviner and the prophet.
greek: Διὸ καὶ διακρίσεις ἔλαβον πνευμάτων, ὥστε διακρίνειν καὶ εἰδέναι, τίς μὲν ὁ πνεύματι φθεγγόμενος καθαρῷ, τίς δὲ ὁ ἀκαθάρτῳ. Ἐπειδὴ γὰρ αὐτόθεν οὐκ ἦν παρασχεῖν τῶν λεγομένων τὴν ἀπόδειξιν· προφητεία γὰρ οὐκ ἐν τῷ καιρῷ, ᾧ λέγεται, ἀλλ’ ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τῆς ἐκβάσεως παρέχεται τῆς οἰκείας ἀληθείας τὸν ἔλεγχον… Ὁ δὲ προφήτης οὐχ οὕτως, ἀλλὰ μετὰ διανοίας νηφούσης καὶ σωφροσύνης καὶ καταστάσεως, καὶ εἰδὼς ἃ φθέγγεται, ἅπαντά φησιν. Ὥστε καὶ πρὸ τῆς ἐκβάσεως κἀντεῦθεν γνώριζε τὸν μάντιν καὶ τὸν προφήτην.
translator_notes: New English from Field OCR cleaned. Testing prophecy vs pagan mantic frenzy — gifts with discernment.

added_allusions.reason: Do not despise prophecy; test all things.
